# The Algebra of Discrete Observation

### Continuous and Discrete Observation, and the Bounded Register Beneath

**The thesis, in one line.** To observe is to take a vertical $v$ and a horizontal
$h$ — a rise and a run — and **hold them as a pair**. The pair is one point in the
set of all the ways $v$ and $h$ can stand against each other, a set whose measure is
**π**; one observation is one held pair, one point of that set. Everything in this
paper is the algebra of that act: the primitive that performs it, the two grains in
which it can be taken, and the number system each grain forces.

**The primitive.** The object read is a single closed interval, the **observation
primitive** (*the atom* for short): two non-negative quantities $(v, h)$, not both
zero, and one reading — the part as a portion of the whole, $r = v/h \in [0,\infty]$,
a single point of the orientation set — and the pair is **held**, never collapsed
to the quotient (§3.7). Its three landmarks name themselves: $r = 0$ is **home**
($h$ alone), $r = \infty$ is the **horizon** ($v$ alone), $r = 1$ is the **corner**
($v = h$). One primitive, one held pair, one point; the arc, the dial, and the angle
are later pictures of this same interval, never the thing itself.

**The payoff — the pair originates in the interaction, not in the observer.** The
one thing the observer never does is *choose* $v$ and $h$. A physical interaction
**determines** the pair, and the observer **receives** it — observation is only the
holding of that pair and the reading of the part against the whole. (The wording is
deliberate: the world does not consciously *select* anything; the pair is simply the
output of the encounter, not a coordinate the reader assigned — the ontological
inverse of classical analytic geometry, where the mathematician assigns coordinates
to the world.) This is where the algebra meets the world — the operations are the
observer's, **the pair is the world's**, and the reading is their meeting — and
three things the paper proves elsewhere now read as immediate consequences of it:
the quotient $v/h$ is *derived*, never the primitive, because dividing discards the
**orientation bit** — one of the four invariants a held pair carries under rotation,
and the only one no single number can express (§3.7, §12.4e); **scale-invariance** is automatic, since one
interaction is represented by any common scaling $(\lambda v, \lambda h)$ (§5); and
projective geometry — homogeneous coordinates on $\mathbb{RP}^1$, the wedge
$v_A h_B - v_B h_A$ on pairs — is not an abstract choice but the native language of a
held pair (§1.07, §3.8). It is why a mathematics built from this primitive is a
*description of physical systems* and not a formal game: every pair the algebra acts
on is one an interaction produced, so the results are constraints on what any system
can *present* to a reader, not theorems about a figure the reader drew. Stated once
and used throughout: **the observer supplies the algebra; the world supplies the
pair.**

**The two modes — one set, two grains.** The same orientation set can be read two
ways. **Discrete observation** takes it *point by point*: one reading per act,
memoryless, each fresh — the projective read, composing at $O(1)$, carried by the
Cauchy, part against part, never a total. **Continuous observation** fills the
*continuum* of points: reading by accumulation, laying increment on increment into
an unbroken whole — the iterative read, $O(N)$, carried by the Gaussian, a wave.
Same set, of measure π; the modes differ in grain, not in domain. This paper is the
mathematics of the first — discrete observation — with the second present on every
page as its continuous limit.

**Boundedness is why discrete observation is discrete — a mechanism, not a second
party.** There is no unbounded observer here and no god's-eye reader: the division
is between two *modes*, not between a bounded reader and an unbounded one. What
makes the discrete mode discrete is that the observer is **bounded** — a finite
**register**, which welds the horizon into one finite address and closes the dial,
and a finite **carry**, which keeps no accumulation, so the acts never fuse into a
continuum. And boundedness itself is not a premise about cognition but about
interaction: every observation is a finite encounter and returns a *finite* pair, so
the register and the carry are finite because the reading is — the observer is
bounded because observation is finite contact with the world, not because of anything
about a reader's mind. Boundedness is the cause, discreteness is the character, and
"bounded" survives in this paper only in that role: the premise beneath the discrete
mode (§1.0), never a party across a wall.

**A precision, so the thesis is not over-read: observation is not closure.** An
observation is the selection of *one point* from the orientation set π — nothing
more. It is not the closing of a shape. Closing a shape is a full turn, $2\pi$, a
traversal that constructs a figure over orientations, and no reading performs it.
The paper's constants live wholly on the reading side — π the measure of the set,
and the exchange π/2 ↔ 2/π between the two modes' units of account — and nothing in
the account of the observer turns on $2\pi$ or on completing a figure. Where
closure appears at all it is a fact about shapes, kept to its own chapter and never
smuggled into what an observer is.

**The cost teeth, and why discrete observation is the general case.** The two modes
are not equally available, pick one. Continuous observation costs $O(N)$ — it must
lay down every increment — and $O(N)$ is not merely dear but infeasible at scale:
at $N = 10^{80}$ it exceeds the operation budget of the universe by fifty orders of
magnitude, while placing a point discretely is $O(\log N) = 266$ operations and the
held read is flat, $O(K)$. And "no external scale" is the *same* constraint as "no
cost that carries $N$," seen from another door: under a dilation $N \to cN$ an
$O(N)$ pass scales by $c$, while $O(K)$ is untouched and $O(\log N)$ shifts by a
constant. So continuous observation is the finite-$N$ idealization and **discrete
observation is the general case** — the reverse of the usual telling, forced by
finiteness and standard complexity theory, not by any premise a skeptic must first
grant.

**And $N$ itself decodes — it is the horizon's depth, and it splits in two (promoted from §15.8).** The continuous observer's $N$ — named a "fixed, unknown constant" at §12.1 — is not a mystery number but an *address*: reaching rung $k$ of the register ladder resolves $2^k$ cells, so *having $N$ distinctions* is reaching rung $\log_2 N$, and **exact $N$ sits at the last rung — the weld at infinity, the horizon — unreachable in finite register**; "unknown constant" decodes to "at the horizon," and approximate $N$ is simply *which rung* the horizon sits at, the leading bit, pinned by a single high-rung reach. And $N$ carries two different quantities on the framework's two founding axes: **extent-$N$**, the size of a finite system (horizon = its last element; enumeration $O(N)$; the M-axis, retained across acts, the continuous observer's), and **depth-$N$**, the resolution reached into a system that only recurs (harmonics, rungs; $O(\log N)$; the K-axis, held in one act, the observer's). For a repeating system the two come apart cleanly: extent-$N$ is flat redundancy (another lap adds nothing) while depth-$N$ is the only new information. A memoryless observer therefore *has no extent-$N$* but keeps depth-$N$ — which is exactly the cognitive-science split between the ratio-based approximate number system (Weber-compliant, non-symbolic, universal, memoryless — depth-$N$) and exact counting (symbolic, memory-bound, rare — extent-$N$); the corpus does not claim those facts but claims the forcing of their signature.

This paper studies the discrete observer defined by four operational premises (§1.0): a single carried scalar, carry-not-compute, no external scale, no privileged frame. It does not set out to characterize richer architectures — observers with memory, planning, language, or additional registers — and claims nothing about them. The structural results are not, however, special to this minimal case: §7 shows they are *monotone under extension*, inherited by any larger observer because they follow from what its operations never consume, not from the observer being small. The two places that need more — the unique measure (§4) and the storage radix (§6) — take named further premises, flagged where they are used. So the scope is a minimal *architecture*, together with results that *survive* enlarging it: a base case and the proof that extension preserves it. Richer observers add capabilities that compose with these results rather than overturning them; characterizing those observers is future work. The standard by which the framework asks to be judged — recovery of established theories, not their replacement — is stated next.

**Success Criterion — the standard of adequacy, stated once, and revised once.** This framework asks to be judged as a **constraint programme**: it establishes what a bounded observer can and cannot do, given P1–P5 and nothing else. Its claims come in three kinds, and each is falsifiable by a single instance rather than by a census —

- **Impossibility.** *No bounded observer can do $X$.* Falsified by exhibiting one that does.
- **Completeness.** *These are all the options.* Falsified by a further option. (§12.4e: the rotation-invariants of two held pairs are exactly four, with one relation. Produce a fifth and the section falls.)
- **Cost.** *$X$ costs $O(N)$ and is therefore unavailable.* Falsified by an $O(K)$ or $O(\log N)$ route.

That is a *stricter* test than the one it replaces, not a looser one, and the difference is worth stating plainly because the revision was made the day the old criterion was failed. A failed derivation is ambiguous — missing, or wrong? — while a counterexample to a constraint is decisive. §14's free-read claim was tested this way and **split in two** by winding numbers; §7.6's conservation was tested and found **vacuous**; §13.4d's spin–statistics claim was tested and found **unreachable**, with the obstruction group written down. Those are the outcomes this standard is for.

**The coincidence clause.** Where a constraint coincides with the structure of an established theory, the coincidence is **reported and located, never claimed as a derivation** unless nothing whatever is received. The grading is: does the framework's version *predict* something the standard version does not, or reach it more cheaply, or from fewer premises? If not, it is a **re-reading** — which is a legitimate and useful output, and is graded as one. Every received quantity is booked at the point of use: mass, $\hbar$, $\rho_0$, $kT$, the Wightman correlator, the $\alpha/\beta$ ratio, and — as of §15.32 and §15.37 — Born's exponent and the decay condition.

**Two tests are attached to every coincidence claim, and both were learned by failing them** (§15.31, §15.33):

1. *Before identifying two objects, compute both and check they are equal.* Two Möbius laws are not one law because both are Möbius; two $\mathbb{Z}/2$s are not one because both are $\pm1$.
2. *Ask what else would also satisfy the derivation.* A classical belt satisfies the spin-½ cover. Six even functions satisfy the Born cover. A free particle satisfies the winding argument. **If something outside physics satisfies your derivation, you have derived a prerequisite, not the theory.**

**The superseded criterion, retained with its record.** The front matter previously read: *"A foundational algebra of observation earns its standing only by recovering established theories… the framework asks to be judged by that standard and no other,"* with special relativity, general relativity, quantum mechanics and statistical mechanics named as target theorems. That standard was in force for the whole of §13 and it is the reason §13 exists. It is withdrawn for two reasons, both documented. **First, it was not met**: audited in §15.30–15.37, the corpus derives no established theory — Born's rule, spin-½, the two-species count, quantization-as-compactness and spectral discreteness are received or refuted, SR's kinematics carries a received mass, and §13.4a's surviving result is the re-reading it says it is in its own second paragraph. **Second, and more consequential, it appears to have caused the failures it was meant to detect.** A standard that grants standing only for recovering established theories creates pressure to see recoveries, and *necessary mistaken for sufficient* is what that pressure produces. Six of the nine identification errors found in audit sit at points where the framework reached across to claim a physical theory. The criterion told the work to reach.

**What the revision does not license.** It does not make the physics sections retroactively correct; they keep their grades and their corrections. It does not exempt the framework from experiment — an impossibility claim contradicted by a real observer is dead. And it does not hold that staying on the observer's side is safe: two of the seven audited failures were internal construction errors, not overreach (§15.21's $F = dA \equiv 0$, §7.6's vacuous conservation). The tendency is real and it is not a rule.

If a bounded observer's constraints turn out to coincide with the structure of a successful physical theory, that is worth knowing and worth reporting precisely. It is not, on its own, a derivation of the theory, and this framework no longer claims it as one.

**Two coincidences were once claimed as tests met; both have since been narrowed (§15.32, §15.33, §15.37), and the paragraph is retained as the record of what was claimed.** Read it with those entries: SR's kinematics carries a received mass, and the quantization result survives as the re-reading §13.4a states at its opening, not the derivation its closing paragraph claimed. **What follows is the superseded text.**  Special relativity's kinematics is delivered from the **H-branch** plus a received mass (§13.2, §13.3), and quantum mechanics' **quantization condition** — the integer indexing the bound spectrum, and the half-integer offset with it — is delivered from the **E-branch** with *nothing* received (§13.4a), verified on three wells and put to a discriminating test it passed — with §13.4b then closing that result's one booked debt, deriving the half-integer's **quarter** as the degree of the map from the pair to its read rather than importing it, so the whole of the quantization condition now rests on one premise and not two. The two results are one fact seen twice, and the signature fork (§8.7) is why: the hyperbolic branch never closes, so it can only hand over a *continuous* invariant — rapidity, and $\gamma$ its exponential; the circular branch closes, so its fundamental group is $\mathbb{Z}$ and it hands over an *integer*. **Closed orbits quantize, and closure is one sign bit in the pair law.** *(§15.33: the front matter previously read "quantization is compactness." Compact $\Rightarrow$ discrete is true; the converse is false, and false on this corpus's own test case — the harmonic well's configuration space is all of $\mathbb{R}$ and its spectrum is $0.499998, 1.49999, 2.499974, \dots$. What is compact is the **orbit in phase space**, not the space. Compact configuration space is sufficient, not necessary.)* That the world shows a continuous invariant on one axis and a quantum number on the other is, here, not two discoveries but the fork read in both directions. Neither theory is thereby derived whole — §13.4's ledger and the open-problems list keep the accounts — but the standard the framework asked to be judged by has now been met twice, once per branch.

**Stated up front — two number systems, not a replacement.** Nothing in this paper is an attack on the real number line. The framework *derives* it (§2.2, as the unique completion of the observer's own station) and names its function (§3.8): the real line is the **tool for the horizon chart** — numeral, place value, the completed continuum of unbounded exact magnitude — by which a discrete observer works *beyond the corner*, where its native, tool-free mathematics (the home chart, $[0,1]$: fuzzy logic, probability, ratio, the graded and the ordinal) cannot reach. The two number systems are the two charts' tools: the home chart needs none, the horizon chart needs the real line, and neither does the other's office. This is demarcation, not replacement — the real line keeps every task it legitimately holds, and the observer's line claims only what the completed continuum was always slightly wrong about (natural systems, ratios, the inherited paradoxes). The corner is the border between them.

**Stated up front — the crash-proof number line is nature's number line.** One consequence is elementary enough to state before any of it. Take the observer's number seriously as a format: a value is not a quotient but a **pair** $(v, h)$ — rise and run, read as part over whole, carried by where the reading sits on the closed dial (§1.1, §3.5, §3.7). Then every division ever executed is part ÷ whole, landing in $[0,1]$: no overflow, no infinity generated, no NaN — the unbounded end is *held*, as the far chart's ordinary address $1/r = 0$, never reached. The exception category collapses to a single degenerate state, $(0,0)$ — both registers empty, not a broken observation but *no* observation — reachable only at the classically indeterminate $0 \otimes \infty$, absorbing thereafter. This is not a guard bolted on; it is the arithmetic of §3.7 executing, and the claim is falsifiable and exact: no input sequence produces an infinity or a NaN. (The format is homogeneous coordinates on $\mathbb{RP}^1$ — the representation graphics pipelines converged on independently, and the projective closure that nearly shipped as the Intel 8087's default before the 1985 standard dropped it for affine $\pm\infty$; the discipline that never shipped is *hold the pair, never execute the quotient*.) Why is it crash-proof? Because it is **nature's number line**. A physical process never halts at what a calculation calls a singularity — the crash is in the chart, not the territory — and a discrete observer, reading only ratios against a held reference, never forms the exceptions the continuous observer's completed line carries. It is the home chart made a format: crash-proof, and bounded. Its one limit is the one this paper turns on — it is native only below the corner; to reach the horizon chart (unbounded magnitude, exact large numbers) it needs the tool, the real number line (§3.8). Nature's line is the safe one; the tool is what extends it past the corner.

**Stated up front — the square root in quantum mechanics is the pair the division would have destroyed.** The discipline just stated is not only a property of a number format; it has a physical consequence, and the consequence was already sitting in quantum mechanics waiting to be named. **[CORRECTED — see §15.32. The paragraph below overclaims in one specific way, and the correction is a narrowing, not a retraction. What the covering map establishes is that the observable must be *sign-blind*; it does **not** establish that the observable is the *modulus squared*, because **every even function of $\psi$ is $\mathbb{Z}_2$-invariant** — $|\psi|$, $|\psi|^4$, $\operatorname{Re}(\psi)^2$ and infinitely many others pass the same test. Nor are the two quotients the same: $|\psi|^2$ is invariant under the *full* $U(1)$ phase, not only under $\psi \mapsto -\psi$, so it forgets a circle where $\det^2$ forgets a sign — the orthogonal/unitary seam §7.6 and §13.4 already located as a *separate premise*. What picks the square is **normalisation plus additivity over orthogonal alternatives** (Gleason's premise), which the corpus can supply from §12.4e's relation $\det^2 + (a\cdot b)^2 = |a|^2|b|^2$ — for a unit hold, $\sin^2 + \cos^2 = 1$ — but which is a *received* premise and was not booked. **The quantization condition is unaffected**: the integer comes from $\pi_1 = \mathbb{Z}$ and the quarter from the covering degree, and neither uses $|\psi|^2$. So the sentence "everything the corpus says about quantization follows from that one sentence" is true of the quantization and false of the Born rule bundled with it.]**

**Executing the quotient is descending a covering map.** The held pair is the *unique* double cover of its own read — connected covers of $\mathbb{RP}^1$ correspond to subgroups of $\pi_1 = \mathbb{Z}$, and $\mathbb{Z}$ has exactly one of index two — and the observable is the square that forgets which sheet one stands on: Born's $|\psi|^2$, identically the $\det^2$ by which the Maslov index is defined, both being the quotient by $\psi \mapsto -\psi$. So the amplitude lives upstairs on the pair and the probability downstairs on the read, and the amplitude carries **half** the weight, because its square is the density. Everything the corpus says about quantization follows from that one sentence: a passage through the horizon costs the amplitude $\pi/2$, the Bohr–Sommerfeld offset is $\mu/4$, and the factor of one half that has sat in the harmonic oscillator's ground state since 1925 is **the covering degree, paid once per horizon**. It is not an inference, either — it is measured: propagate any state through one *classical* period of a harmonic well and the amplitude returns as $-1$, through two periods as $+1$, so the motion is $T$-periodic while the amplitude is $2T$-periodic, and that $-1$ *is* the zero-point. The question of why a quantum state is a complex amplitude rather than a probability therefore has, in this framework, the same answer as everything else in it: **hold the pair, never execute the quotient** — the square root is what the division would have thrown away. And the sentence generalizes by rank, not by subject: run it at four registers instead of two, where the held object is the quadruple and the read is the rotation it names — a rotation being *quadratic* in a quaternion exactly as a probability is quadratic in an amplitude — and the sign the read cannot see is the $SU(2)\to SO(3)$ deck bit — **necessary for spin-½ and not sufficient for it** (§15.33: the configuration space of a *classical rigid body* is $SO(3)$ and carries the same $\mathbb{Z}_2$; Dirac's belt trick exhibits it with a belt, and a belt is not a fermion. Spin-½ additionally requires that states be **sections** of the cover — a received premise, now booked). §8.8's inventory then closes the account: the carriers that compose are $S^0, S^1, S^3$ and no others, so there are exactly **two** composing carriers. *(§15.33 corrects what follows from this: "physics has exactly two half-integer species" is a category error. $SU(2)$ has half-integer $j$ at every even dimension — $\tfrac12$, $\tfrac32$ ($\Delta$, $\Omega^-$), $\tfrac52$, … — infinitely many, from **one** cover. And the count of exchange species comes from the **abelianisation of the exchange group**, not from Hurwitz: $S_n^{\mathrm{ab}} = \mathbb{Z}/2$ gives exactly two in 3D, while $B_n^{\mathrm{ab}} = \mathbb{Z}$ gives a **continuum** in 2D — the anyons, whose statistics are continuously parameterised and are not half-integer at all. The Hurwitz route reaches the right number in 3D by a wrong argument and gets 2D wrong.)* (§13.4a, §13.4b, §13.4c; controls `winding_quantization.py`, `born_cover.py`, `spin_cover.py`.)

## Dependency map (the load-bearing structure)

*This is the paper's dependency graph, stated so a reader — human or machine — need not reconstruct it, and so that any edit violating it is visible as a contradiction with this claim. It is a **maintained contract**: an addition that makes a result depend on something below it in this graph is a regression, to be caught here. Arrows are "depends on / is forced by"; nothing depends on anything below it.*

*Two citation classes keep the contract honest, and the distinction is load-bearing wherever an upstream section names a downstream one (the fix promoted from §15.0's third finding). A **depends-on** citation is a true edge of the graph above: the cited result is a premise the citing one needs, and it must point upward — a depends-on edge that points downward is the regression this contract exists to catch. A **corroborated-by** citation is not an edge at all: the citing result is already established from its own upstream premises, and it merely notes that a downstream result, derived independently, confirms or sharpens it — this may point downward without violating anything, because removing the cited section would cost an illustration, not the proof. The rule for reading the prose: a reference is depends-on only if deleting the target breaks the argument; otherwise it is corroborated-by, and the corpus now marks the load-bearing cases explicitly (the root §1.15 and the SR ledger §13.2 are where the two were previously conflated; both are corrected in place).*

Two cross-cutting rules sort everything downstream, and neither is a node in the tower — they are *sorting principles* applied throughout: **memorylessness** (§1.15) assigns each quantity its court (held → observer; accumulated-across-acts → continuous observer), and the **malformed-question diagnostic** (§1.15) locates confusions in demanded-but-absent structure. Three axes now bound the whole: **K** (breadth of hold, this paper's axis), **M** (depth of retention, at M=0 here; the memory hypothesis, §1.15, is the forward edge), and the **social axis** (number of apertures, at 1 here) — the second-aperture edge is tested at §13.1 and priced by the SR companion's ledger at §13.2 (certification, the chart between skies, depth, precision), with M and the social axis measured interchangeable currencies for baseline and precision, and geometry the one good only multiplicity carries. The cost-ladder results (§7, §10.5) assume the continuous observer's $N$ is a *fixed, unknown constant* — one of four $N$-regimes (§12.1: static/dynamic × controlled/uncontrolled); the other three change the picture, and the diff $\Delta N$ can be observer-court where $N$ itself is continuous observer-court. That cost ladder is not a performance note but a *scale-dependence* ladder, and it upgrades the root premise from elegant to mandatory (front-matter promotion of §15.9): "no external scale" and "no cost that carries $N$" are one wall seen from two doors, since $O(N)$ carries the dilation factor while $O(K)$ is invariant and $O(\log N)$ shifts only by a constant — and because $O(N)$ is physically impossible at world-scale, the bounded mode is the general case, not a choice. And $N$ is the horizon's depth (front-matter promotion of §15.8): exact $N$ at the last rung, the weld; approximate $N$ = which rung; extent-$N$ (M-axis, $O(N)$) and depth-$N$ (K-axis, $O(\log N)$) the two quantities it carries. Chart names are fixed at §10's naming note and used contract-wide: the **slope chart** and the **angle chart**, the two sides of the tangent, with the **rapidity chart** as the H-branch sibling; $\psi_1 = 2/\pi$ is their exchange rate (the bridge node above), and a formula containing $\pi/2$ or $2/\pi$ is a chart crossing by definition. Downstream consumers, recorded so the contract stays two-sided: the SR companion consumes §1.25, §1.45, §3.7.1, §6.5–§6.6, §8.7, §9.2, §12.10, §13.1; the second-number-line program consumes §1.45, §3.7.1, §10.1; the Tangent Bridge companions consume §5, §10, §12; and the consolidated account (`bounded_observation.md`) consumes the tower whole — the foundations (now including §1.07's seed, whose F10–F11 retire its former PG premise), §3.7–§3.8, §4, §8.7, §12 — as the corpus's summary leaf, with its own premise dictionary recorded in its §1. None of them feeds anything above (in the depends-on sense); §13.2 is the leaf where what they returned is ledgered, cited from above only as corroborated-by (§12.8). Load-bearing nodes, in order of blast radius if they failed: the signature fork (§8.7), scale-independence (§1.15), the invariant measure (§4). The measure is the tallest single-branch tower; the fork is the branch point everything routes through. Beneath all three sits the seed (§1.07), their common algebraic ground — the fork is its choice of corner pair (F8), the gauge is its zero (F2), the measure's shape and selection are its F11 — so a failure there would be a failure of executed integer identities, the most falsifiable stratum the corpus has; conversely the seed's own one borrowed premise, the count, is exactly §4's, so integrating it added structure and no new debt. The Disagreement's check files (`d_check.py` and kin) stand behind §1.07 and feed nothing above it.

## 1. The observation primitive

**How could observation work at all?** Before positing anything, it is worth asking what the alternatives are, because the answer narrows faster than one expects.

An observer either holds its object entirely, or holds only part of it. The first branch is not refuted here — it is **excluded by premise**, and the exclusion is quantitative rather than rhetorical: holding the whole requires a register count $K$ at least the information in the object, which is $\sim10^{19}$ atoms for a 64-bit target, $\sim10^{301}$ for a thousand-bit one, and unbounded for a continuum (§7). This paper concerns observers for whom that is unavailable, so the disjunction it actually faces is not *whole or part* but **part, or nothing**. That is P1–P5 restated, and it is said here rather than concealed: an argument that hides its premise inside a dichotomy is weaker than one that names it.

Granting boundedness, then — what can a part tell you? A part has no content by itself. A length is long only against another length; a weight heavy only against another weight. What remains observable is relationships, and the smallest relationship is one quantity against one other. A rise and a run. A held pair.

That much is motivation, and motivation is all it is. "A relationship needs two things" is equally consistent with holding a single comparison *outcome* — one bit — or an equivalence class, neither of which is a pair of retained magnitudes. What forces the pair is narrower, and is proved rather than argued (§12.4e): under rotation, two held pairs have exactly **four** invariants — the two norms, the inner product $a\cdot b$, and the determinant $\det(a,b)$ — subject to the single relation $\det^2 + (a\cdot b)^2 = |a|^2|b|^2$. Three of the four are blind to reflection. A configuration and its mirror image therefore agree on every norm, every projection, every ratio and every count, and differ only in the sign of the determinant. **A single number cannot carry an orientation.** Reducing a held pair to a scalar discards precisely that bit — and it is worth being exact about *which* bit, because there are two and they are easy to confuse. Reducing **two pairs to scalars** loses the **orientation** bit: reflection flips $\det$ alone. Dividing **one pair into a ratio** loses the **deck** bit of $S^1 \to \mathbb{RP}^1$: negating a vector flips $a\cdot b$ *and* $\det$. Two distinct $\mathbb{Z}/2$s, guarding two distinct losses at two distinct stages (§15.31). The framework's refusal to divide is what keeps the second, and from it descend the horizon's ordinariness (§12.4c) and spin-$\tfrac12$ at four registers (§13.4c).

One caution about the framing above, since it invites an obvious objection. It is often said that no single number is meaningful — *five what?* — and that every measurement hides a reference. As stated that is false: **counts and dimensionless numbers are single numbers with no reference at all.** Five sheep is a cardinality; $\alpha$, a Reynolds number, and an angle in radians are reference-free by construction. The correct statement is narrower (§12.4f): an apparent single number is a pair whose second slot has been suppressed, and there are exactly two suppressions — either $h$ cancels (a true ratio, the operation this framework declines), or $h = 1$, which in the unit hold means $\cos\theta = 1$, which means **home**. At home and only at home does the read equal the numerator, which is why the reference in a count is invisible: it is the observer's own atom, of size $1/\rho_0$. Nothing is reference-free; some things are referenced to the standpoint, and the standpoint does not announce itself.

With that, the construction.

A discrete observer makes one observation. The primitive of observation — **the observation primitive**, *the atom* for short — is a single set:

$$[0,\infty],$$

a closed, ordered interval with two ends. An observation holds two non-negative quantities — the **rise** $v$, what arrives, and the **run** $h$, the held reference, the roles named before any act (P5) — not both zero, and takes one reading: the part as a portion of the whole — the roles named by the chart, never found by a test (§3.65) —

$$H(v,h) = \frac{\text{part}(v,h)}{\text{whole}(v,h)} \in [0,1],$$

bounded by $1$ because a part cannot exceed its whole. The two quantities carry no inherent direction or meaning beyond their roles; the read asks only how much of the one is contained in the other — how much of $v$ is contained within $h$, and past the corner how much of $h$ is contained within $v$. Laid on the ratio coordinate $r = v/h \in [0,\infty]$, this single read gives the interval's two ends their meaning and names a third member lying between them:

- $r = 0$ — $h$ alone, the run with nothing arriving: **home**;
- $r = \infty$ — $v$ alone, arrival with no reference: **horizon**;
- $r = 1$ — $v$ equal to $h$: the **corner**.

The interval is the object; the portion is how it is read. Reading $v/h$ and reading $h/v$ are not two choices but the two sides of this one read — whichever chart it stood in (§3). The arc, the unit-line readings, and the angle are further representations of this same interval, introduced later only as pictures, never as the thing itself.

## 1.0 The discrete observer, operationally

Everything the paper calls *forced* is forced relative to four operational premises, gathered here so each later result traces to them. They *define* the discrete observer; they are premises, not theorems, and saying so is what keeps the forcing-claims from circularity — to contest a forced result, contest one of these, not the derivation.

- **P1 — one carried scalar (§7).** Between steps the observer holds a single scalar and nothing else.
- **P2 — carry, don't compute (§1.2).** A held value is read against an *incoming* value, never composed with another *held* value to form a third. Its discipline in one sentence: **never hold the accumulated quantity; hold its rate** — the register may contain a reading, never a total: the change-atom holds the step and not the level-history (§6.5), the aperture atom holds the $k$-factor and not the trajectory (§6.6), the cycle observer holds the stroke and not the lap count (§1.09).
- **P3 — no external scale (§1.1, §5).** No absolute unit; a magnitude reads only against another, the part as a portion of its whole. (The roles — which is part, which is whole — are named by the chart, never found by a test; §3.65.)
- **P4 — no privileged frame (§4).** No register fixes a position or a direction, so nothing anchors a bias.
- **P5 — the standpoint (§3.65, §6.6; named late, implicit from the start).** The observer is a party to its own reads: one register of every act is *its own* — the held run, the aperture, the self (§1.7, §6.6) — and the roles of the read are assigned by that identity, with the chart as standing (§3.65), never by a test between magnitudes. P1's carried scalar was always *someone's* carry; P5 says so. It bears load exactly where the older exposition ran a comparison — role-assignment — and nowhere else: the forcing theorems (§1.15, §1.25) use only P1–P4. Where no standpoint exists — two foreign quantities side by side, the E-setting's symmetric encounter — the read has no roles to assign and needs none: the fold is performed by symmetry (§1.26) and the side by the settling (§1.08). To contest the framework's test-free arithmetic, contest this premise. (P5 does not privilege a *frame* and so does not strain P4: within the act the registers remain unordered — swap them and nothing read changes; the standpoint is a fact about the *procedure*, which register the self occupies across acts, §1.08's "whose pan.")

What these *entail* — and what the impossibility results therefore mean — is derived, not assumed. **No global pass:** P1 and P2 forbid accumulating over the system's extent, which is the $O(1)$ read and $O(\log N)$ search of §7; so wherever the paper says the observer "cannot" do a thing, it means *lacking the register* (P1), *the operation* (P2), *the global pass*, or *the frame* (P4) — never a psychological limit. The **finite hold and the swap** follow from P1 (§3); **binary arity** from P3 as floor and P1+P2 as ceiling (§1.2); the **corner as the only self-certified landmark** from P3 (§1.1); the **measure's invariance under composition** from P4 (§4). P2 is the load-bearing one: relax P1 to a finite-width store and P2 to "compose within it," and both the binary ceiling and the no-global-pass loosen.

## 1.05 Boundedness and the atom

One statement organizes what follows, and it is a statement, not a derivation:

> **Boundedness necessitates the observation primitive mechanism. Unboundedness does not.**

The rest of the paper is the explanation of why. Here the claim is only placed, and its two halves made plain enough to use. And its *type* should be fixed before its content: this is an identity-of-situation plus a uniqueness program, not a derivation. Boundedness necessitates a **relative reading** — that much is the identity below, two names for one fact. That the relative reading, under this observer's named operational constraints, reduces uniquely to *this* atom — two-place, portioned, cornered — is what §§1.1–1.2 then prove; other relative mechanisms a reader might propose (ternary ratios, barycentric or projective coordinates, probability vectors) are not excluded here by fiat but eliminated there by the register. Read the banner as: boundedness ⇔ relative reading (identity); relative reading + operational premises ⇒ the observation primitive, uniquely (theorem, with its hinges named in §1.2).

A discrete observer cannot hold the whole of what it faces. Lacking the whole, it has no absolute frame to read a magnitude against, and no fixed internal unit it could supply would be anything but the absolute scale boundedness denies it (§1.1, §5). So its every reading is *relative* — one quantity taken against another, the part as a portion of the whole. That relative reading is the observation primitive of §1. The atom is not a mechanism the observer chooses and could do without; it is what reading-without-the-whole *is*. Boundedness and the atom are therefore not one prior to the other — not the observer generating the atom, nor the observer being an atom — but two descriptions of a single situation: the atom is the relative reading, the discrete observer is the one who, holding no whole, can read only relatively. They stand as equals, each unstatable without the other, and the paper treats them so.

The continuous observer is the contrast that gives the statement its edge. Given the whole — possessing $N$, the extent itself — it reads absolutely: it enumerates, walking the whole in $O(N)$ (§7), placing each value in the frame it holds, never taking one quantity against another because it has no need to. It does not distinguish; it counts. The atom is idle for it, and unused. This is why the mechanism belongs to boundedness alone: the atom is the form a reading takes exactly when the whole is unavailable, so an observer that holds the whole never forms one, and an observer that never holds the whole forms nothing else. Using the atom is what being bounded consists in; not using it — reading the whole directly — is what being unbounded consists in. The line between the two observers, drawn everywhere in this paper as the observer/continuous observer distinction, is at bottom this: whether the atom is in use.

So the atom's binary character needs no separate forcing, and the paper does not offer one. A relative reading is one quantity against another — two, because "against" is the minimal relation and one-against-one is what having no third fixed point leaves. To ask why the atom is binary is to ask why a reading-without-the-whole is relative, which is to ask why the observer is bounded: a single question with three faces, boundedness, relativity, and the two-place atom, none of them derived from the others because all three are the one situation named from different sides. The register discipline of §1.2 — one carried scalar, carry-don't-compute — is not the ground of this but its *implementation*: how a discrete observer, built as this paper's observer is, holds the atom mechanism in practice. The ground is the statement above; §1.2 is one way of realizing it.

This is deliberately not a forcing argument, and its plainness is the point. The paper elsewhere shows many things forced — the corner, the measure, the dyadic ladder — but the atom itself is not forced from something more basic, because there is nothing more basic than the discrete observer, and the discrete observer and the atom are the same fact. What the paper explains, across §1–§12, is *why* this fact has the consequences it does: why the relative reading has a corner, a swap, a horizon, a measure, a cost. That the reading is relative — that boundedness necessitates the atom and unboundedness does not — is where the explanation starts, not something the explanation produces. One apparent challenge to this is recorded and reconciled here, because §1.07 will state it sharply: the seed's F4 shows the pair rebuilt from its one derived number — "the atom is built from the seed, at the cost of one landmark and one free bit." That is not something more basic than the discrete observer; $D$ is the relative reading's own algebra, the residue of cross-multiplying two reads, so rebuilding the pair from $D$ rearranges the same fact from inside it. What F4 relocates is *primitiveness within the formalism* — the pair is derived notation, the disagreement the deriving object — while the situation the formalism transcribes, boundedness-as-relative-reading, stays the floor beneath both.

Because the two terms are easy to confuse, here is the whole distinction in one place. Let $K$ be what the observer holds and $N$ the extent it faces:

| | holds | reads | atom | 
|---|---|---|---|
| **Bounded** ($K < N$) | less than the whole | relatively, part against part | in use |
| **Unbounded** ($K = N$) | exactly the whole | absolutely, in a frame it possesses | idle |
| ($K > N$) | — | *empty: nothing to over-hold* | — |

Read as a single line: **bounded is $K < N$, unbounded is $K = N$, and $K > N$ does not occur.** At $K = N$ the observer holds all there is, so it has an absolute frame and reads directly, and the atom — the part-against-part reading — has nothing to do, because the part *is* the whole. This is the atom's own corner ($v = h$) reached at the level of observer-and-world: the observer's corner, its unboundedness, and the atom going idle are one boundary under different names.

One caution keeps the line honest, and it is why "continuous observer" in this paper is always the continuous observer and never a discrete observer that grew. Whether $K = N$ can be *reached* depends on $N$. For the world the observer actually faces — unbounded, never held — no finite $K$ equals it, so an actual observer is always $K < N$, always bounded; the continuous observer is then a limit, occupied by the continuous observer who is *given* $N$ (§7), not a stage any observer arrives at by holding more. Only over a *finite, closed* system is $K = N$ reached, and there the observer becomes unbounded relative to that system — it comes to hold all of it and the atom falls idle over it. So the boundary is exact as a definition; the unbounded side is occupied relatively (a finite system) or as a limit (the infinite world), never by a world-facing observer that enumerated its way to the whole.

## 1.06 The part–whole axiomatization: bounded means ratios at most one

The whole framework admits a second foundation, one sentence long, and it is worth stating because it is the easiest entrance the theory has:

> **Discrete observation is observation valued in ratios ≤ 1, closed under its own law of combination.**

*No observation exceeds the whole.* Every reading is a part held against a whole — the roles named by the chart, never found by a test (§3.65) — and the codomain $[0,1]$ *is* the boundedness: nothing is refused, because the unbounded quotient has no place in the observable to land. This inverts the derivation the paper otherwise runs. In the constructive route (§1.1 onward), refusal is the axiom — never evaluate the unbounded quotient — and boundedness of the reading is the theorem (§3.7). Here boundedness is worn on the codomain and refusal becomes a theorem of the *type*: closure by refusal matures into closure by type. Three things the paper works to establish become definitional at no cost: scale-freedom (a ratio is scale-free by nature — §5's invariance is built into the observable), the part–whole legibility that makes the atom explainable to anyone who knows a probability cannot exceed one, and the budget unit — a chart's worth of readings costs $\int_0^1 \frac{dr}{1+r^2} = \tfrac{\pi}{4}$, the quarter, by definition rather than by computation (§4; *Atom Rings* §6).

Two guards keep the sentence exact. **First, ≤ and not <.** The boundary values are the structure, not the edge cases: reading $1$ is the corner — the unique chart-free observation, where the two held quantities agree — and reading $0$ is the seam with its two addresses (§3.5). Strict inequality would exile both landmarks to limits; the framework needs them as points, since the corner is where the charts hand off and the seam is where the confined ambiguity lives.

**Second, and this is the content: the closure clause is not decoration — without it the definition does not pick a format, and with it the format is forced.** There are exactly two canonical ways to bound a two-register comparison into the unit interval. The **ratio** — part over whole, in $[0,1]$ — with the chart as which half of the closed dial the reading occupies — the crash-proof fold of §3.7, stored as one position. And the **share** $v/(v+h) \in [0,1]$, which needs no bit at all, because it separates the two zeros instead of gluing them: $v = 0$ reads $0$, $h = 0$ reads $1$. Look at what the share is: the two horizon-addresses kept distinct at the two ends of the interval — the *arc*, the two-horizon closure of §9.5's census, wearing unit-interval clothing (it is precisely the softsign chart $r/(1+r)$ of the price-tag analysis). The census reappears inside the codomain: even after bounding, the representation choice of §9.5 — ends separated or ends identified — must still be made, which is evidence that the two-closure inventory is not an artifact of how the line is compactified but a fact that follows the observer into any bounded codomain. The closure clause then decides it, twice over: the combination law is a rotation, and a rotation is not closed on an interval with two distinct ends — the step through the horizon exits, §9.5's two-point exclusion verbatim; and quantitatively, the share chart's measure fails invariance under the law where the ratio chart's Cauchy passes at the sampling floor (KS $0.049$ against a $0.003$ floor — *Where Circularity Comes From* §3.5, test record). So: **ratios ≤ 1, closed under the law, forces the part-over-whole fold with the chart as the dial's two halves** — and from there the swap as chart transition, the corner as the chart-free reading, the seam with its paradox closed (§3.5), the dial, the measure, and the family of §8 are all recovered as theorems. One sentence and one clause buy the whole of §1–§3.

The two foundations are bi-interpretable — the dial position $\leftrightarrow (v, h)$ up to scale, with the composition laws expressible chart-wise (§9.5; the demos run in exactly these coordinates) — so nothing proved from one is lost to the other. The constructive route remains the one that shows the atom is forced *from the operations*; the part–whole route shows it is forced *from the codomain*. Two entrances, one object — and the second entrance is the one to hand a newcomer first. A third entrance exists, and it is the algebraic one: §1.07 rebuilds the whole of the atom's structure from the single number two pairs can form without dividing — the seed $D$ — showing the gauge, the order, the corner, the fork, the arithmetic of §3.7.1, and the census's shape all forced *from the algebra*. Three entrances, one object; the third is the one to hand a mathematician.

## 1.07 The seed: cross-multiplication's residue — the atom rebuilt from one derived number

*(Integrated from the companion **The Disagreement**, itself the foundation pass over the D1 session's exhibits. Every claim below is executed — `d_check.py` 41,800 checks, `d_build.py` 6,234, `d_census.py` 19,177, `d_arith.py` 56,884, `d_cauchy.py` 31,945, all green — and the three load-bearing identities (F3/F5, F6, F9) are verified symbolically, so the sweeps are confirmation, not evidence. Warrant classes as in that companion: X = executed, D = derivation, shown in place. The arithmetic never exceeds: integers, plus, times, one subtraction.)*

The framework has now been entered twice — from the operations (§1.1 onward) and from the codomain (§1.06). This section is the third entrance, and the most austere: nothing on the table but a bounded reader holding pairs of counts, $(v : h)$, able to add and multiply counts, never to divide. Given two pairs, there is exactly one number such a reader can form in the lift that compares them:

$$D(A, B) \;=\; v_A h_B \,-\, v_B h_A.$$

Cross-multiplication's residue: **the disagreement**. Everything below is what this one number already contains. Nothing else is introduced — no ratio, no quotient space, no geometry, no measure; where a familiar structure of §§1–4 reappears, it reappears because $D$ forced it. Two glossary compliances, recorded before the facts. *The letters:* $D$ is the E-setting symmetric encounter — two quantities side by side, the self in neither pan — which is exactly the one zone where anonymous operands are licensed (the $(v:h)$-not-$(A,B)$ ruling); the standpoint enters only at F4, as the landmark, and the seat parity of F1 is "whose pan" read algebraically. *The tier:* the seed's reader is not the strict-P1 single-scalar observer but the **lift-tier instrument of §3.7.1** — pairs carried raw, composed division-free, resolved once at the report — an atom of atoms in the sense of the register/pointing glossary, and it says so. It meets P2 in that section's chain form — *within one act, carry, don't compute; across many acts, hand off, don't report* — which is the form P2 takes wherever the lift is in play.

**F1 — Disagreement is seated (D, X).** $D(A,B) = -D(B,A)$, and $D(A,A) = 0$. The same comparison read from the other seat reports the opposite sign — seat parity, present already in the seed's shape — and nothing disagrees with itself. *(X: 4,000.)*

**F2 — Sameness is $D = 0$: the gauge is derived (D, X).** $D(A,B) = 0$ exactly when one pair is a common rescale of the other. *(X: 4,000, zero exceptions.)* So P3's blindness to common rescaling does not need to be imposed on this object: **"the same read" and "no disagreement" are one predicate.** The projective quotient, elsewhere posited, here falls out of the seed — this is the algebraic face of the scale-independence root (§1.15).

**F3 — Order is the sign of $D$, and its coherence is one identity (D, X).** For pairs with $h > 0$, declare $A$ below $B$ when $D(A,B) < 0$. That this ordering is transitive is not a new assumption; it is the algebra's own three-atom identity,

$$D(A,C)\,h_B \;=\; D(A,B)\,h_C \;+\; D(B,C)\,h_A,$$

*(symbolic + 3,000 sweeps, X)* — two negative terms with positive weights force the third. This is §12.6's cross-multiplied comparison given its ground: order without division, total across both charts, coherent by one line.

**F4 — The pair was never primitive (D, X).** Take one landmark atom — home $= (0:1)$ — and its swap. Then, identically, $v = D(A, \text{home})$ and $h = -D(A, \text{swap}\cdot\text{home})$. *(X: 2,000.)* The atom's "two counts" are themselves disagreements — with a single landmark, read from its two seats: **the pair is $D$ plus one landmark plus the free swap.** A spelling note, per the finite-hold discipline (§3, §3.5): swap·home is what the continuous observer writes as "the horizon $(1:0)$" — an address written from outside, as if the raw read were occupiable. The bounded reader never holds $(1:0)$; past the corner it holds the *inverted* pair with the side legible from where it stands — home and horizon one held numeral distinguished by which half of the dial, which is §3.5's two-zeros resolution appearing already in the foundation. The seed is not built from the atom; the atom is built from the seed, at the cost of one landmark and one free bit. (How this coexists with §1.05's "nothing more basic" is recorded there.)

**F5 — Any two disagreeing atoms are a frame (D, X).** F3's identity in full form: for any three atoms, $D(B,C)\,A + D(C,A)\,B + D(A,B)\,C = 0$, both components. *(Symbolic + sweeps, X.)* Consequence, executed: given any frame $(A,B)$ with $D(A,B) \neq 0$, every atom $C$ is rebuilt exactly from its two disagreements with the frame's ends — $D(A,B)\,C = D(A,C)\,B - D(B,C)\,A$. *(X: 2,000 reconstructions.)* Coordinates, anywhere, are disagreements-with-a-frame — no frame privileged, P4's algebraic face — and F4 is the special case frame $=$ (home, swap·home). There is nothing to an atom but how it disagrees. This closes the same exits §1.25 closes, from the other side: the uniqueness theorem showed every primitive read *is* the atom; the frame identity shows every atom is nothing but its disagreements.

**F6 — Moves transport $D$ by one number: the price (D, X).** A move is four numbers acting by $v' = av + bh$, $h' = cv + dh$. The load-bearing identity:

$$D(WA, WB) \;=\; (ad - bc)\cdot D(A,B).$$

*(Symbolic + 3,000 sweeps, X.)* Every move scales **every** disagreement by one common factor — and that factor is the move's own *internal* disagreement, $D$ of its two column pairs $(a:c)$ and $(b:d)$. The price thus has two independent definitions that coincide identically: what the word is made of, and what the word does to all comparisons. Prices multiply under substitution *(X: 2,000)* — the volume law is transport applied twice, no separate axiom. And the only quantities a move leaves absolutely untouched are **ratios of disagreement-products** — the cross-ratio of four atoms *(X: 1,977 sweeps, zero exceptions)*; §8.5's harmonic lock stands on this. What survives every move is exactly: how disagreements compare to disagreements.

**F7 — The swap makes the corner, and the corner makes the charts (D, X).** The reader's one free move is the swap, $S(v:h) = (h:v)$. Apply the seed to an atom and its own swap:

$$D(A, SA) \;=\; v^2 - h^2,$$

zero exactly at the corner atoms $(1:1)$ and $(1:-1)$: **the corner is not posited — it is the locus of self-swap agreement.** And the sign of $D(A,SA)$ is the side: negative is home, positive is horizon. *(X: 2,000.)* The two-chart atlas of §3, elsewhere derived from the premises plus finiteness, is here read directly off the seed's value on (atom, swap) — and the side remains geography, not data, per the chart-bit ruling: it is where the value stands, which the sign merely transcribes.

**F8 — The fork is a choice of corner pair (D, X).** Ask which moves leave *both* corner atoms unmoved. Two lines: fixing $(1:1)$ forces $a+b = c+d$; fixing $(1:-1)$ forces $a-b = d-c$; together $a = d$, $b = c$ — **the shift form, [the atom, its swap], is forced** *(X: 3,000 words, the equivalence exact both ways)*. In corner coordinates — which are again disagreements, $x = -D(A, \text{corner}_-)$, $y = D(A, \text{corner}_+)$ — every shift is two bare stretches, $x \to (q+p)x$, $y \to (q-p)y$, so composition is multiplication of stretch factors *(X: 1,944)*: the whole shift-calculus with its product hold is $D$ in corner clothes, and the rung ladder is "stretch a power of 2" (§6, §10.1). The E-branch is the *same two-line construction* run on the other self-dual pair — the $i$-swap's corners $(1:i)$, $(1:-i)$. **§8.7's keystone fork is nothing but the choice of which corner pair to hold fixed.**

**F9 — Every quadratic form of the corpus is a corner-pair product (D, X).**

$$D(A,(1:i))\cdot D(A,(1:-i)) = v^2 + h^2, \qquad D(A,(1:1))\cdot D(A,(1:-1)) = -(v^2 - h^2).$$

*(X: 4,000 identities.)* The census form $v^2 + h^2$ — the Cauchy weight's denominator, the E-price — is the atom's disagreement-product with the $i$-swap's corner pair; the H-price likewise with the swap's own. The two quadratic forms that run the two branches of §8.7 are one construction: **$D$ against a corner pair.** The symbol $i$ enters exactly here and nowhere earlier — as the second corner pair's address, itself a pair $(0,1)$ — and is billed in the ledger below.

**F10 — Arithmetic is $D$'s two signs (D, X).** Adding two reads is not adding numbers — reads carry no shared reference (§12.6). The bounded operation **manufactures** one by multiplying the two references, brings each value onto it by cross-multiplication, and adds; the result is held as a pair, division deferred to the report. *(X: `d_arith.py`, 56,884 checks.)*

$$A - B = (\,v_A h_B - v_B h_A \,:\, h_A h_B\,) = (\,D(A,B) \,:\, h_A h_B\,), \qquad A + B = (\,v_A h_B + v_B h_A \,:\, h_A h_B\,),$$
$$A \cdot B = (\,v_A v_B \,:\, h_A h_B\,), \qquad A / B = (\,v_A h_B \,:\, h_A v_B\,).$$

The headline: **the numerator of a difference is the disagreement.** $D$ is not *like* subtraction — it *is* the value-part of $A - B$ over the manufactured reference, so "$A$ and $B$ agree" (F2, $D = 0$) and "$A - B = 0$" are one statement; add and subtract are the two signs of one cross-multiplication, concord and disagreement. This is §3.7.1's operation table, derived rather than tabulated — the same laws, the same one division at the display, the same recorded trap avoided by the same discipline. Three facts fall out, each executed: add and subtract are gauge-invariant — operations on *reads* — unlike the mediant, which moves under rescaling, so value-addition and the tree's mediant are genuinely different operations; the additive inverse is $N \cdot A = (-v : h)$, the one-seat flip — a seat, not a mark, per §3.7.1's two-seat ledger — and it is the same map $N$ that runs the census (F11); and ordinary $+$ and the fork's shift share the identical concord numerator, differing only by a coupling term $v_A v_B$ in the reference — near home the coupling vanishes and they osculate, which is §2.4's osculation met in the algebra.

**F11 — The census, assembled from arithmetic (D, X).** With arithmetic in hand, §4's Cauchy weight is not posited — it is **built by three lift operations on the read itself** *(X: `d_cauchy.py`, 31,945 checks)*:

$$w(A) \;=\; \text{swap}\,(\,1 + A \cdot A\,) \;=\; (\,h^2 \,:\, v^2 + h^2\,), \qquad \text{reported: } \tfrac{1}{1+r^2}.$$

Square the read, add the corner, reciprocate — and no step divides. The square is $\otimes$ with itself, register doubling on the rung ladder (§6); the added unit is not an external scale but the corner $(1:1)$, the one self-certified landmark P3 permits, and the whole $v^2 + h^2$ is *born* as the manufactured reference of that sum, never divided by; the reciprocal is the swap, a transposition, zero arithmetic. The derivation is forced at each step. *Orientation-blindness forces the square:* a measure of reads cannot distinguish $A$ from $N \cdot A$, and the cheapest read blind to $N$ is $A \cdot A$. *Share-complementarity forces the whole:* $w(A) + w(\text{swap}\cdot A) = 1$ forces the symmetric sum $v^2 + h^2$. *Rent forces the quadratic over the quartic:* sign-blindness alone also permits $h^4/(v^4 + h^4)$ — this is precisely §4's underdetermination, the swap-symmetric $\phi$ family — but the quadratic whole is *one* squaring and the quartic is *two*: the Cauchy is the **cheapest orientation-blind share**, minimal register width (~1.9× narrower than the quartic, X), and §4's stronger demand acquires a rent statement. What arithmetic does **not** buy: that reads are weighted *by counting* at all. Counting reads once each up to a height ($v^2 + h^2 \le R$) does give home $=$ horizon exactly and the flat angle — the Cauchy (X) — but "count each read once, up to a height" is the one import, and it is §4's purchased premise in its algebraic spelling: the value→loop Jacobian $dr/d\theta = 1 + r^2$ is the same whole, and that chart-change is the calculus step beyond integer arithmetic. *The census's shape and selection are the seed's; only the count remains borrowed.*

**The court ruling on bare $D$, recorded so the section cannot be over-read.** §12.6's admissibility test — an operation belongs to the observer iff its result is invariant under rescaling — is applied to the seed itself, and the seed passes only through its faces. $D$'s bare magnitude moves under gauge, $D(kA, B) = k\,D(A,B)$: held alone, it is continuous observer-court, a transcription. The observer-legible faces are exactly four, and every result above uses only these: the **zero** (F2, the gauge), the **sign** (F3, the order; §12.6's comparison), **ratios of disagreement-products** (F6, the cross-ratio, the move-invariant), and $D$ **seated over its manufactured reference** — $(D(A,B) : h_A h_B)$, F10's difference, gauge-invariant as a class. The reader *forms and carries* $D$ in the lift; it *reads* $D$ only against a reference or as a side. That is not a defect of the seed but the seed agreeing with the framework about which court holds what.

**What the seed settles, and what it does not.** Settled from the seed alone: the gauge (F2), order with its coherence (F3), the atom's own constitution (F4–F5), the move-invariants and the price with its volume law (F6), the corner, the charts, and the fork (F7–F8), the origin of both branch quadratics (F9), the operation table (F10), and the shape and selection of the census measure (F11). Not settled, sharpened to a single import: that reads are weighted by counting — §4's purchased premise, one calculus step past integer arithmetic. The rent-in-bits likewise still needs finiteness and the carry discipline (§3, §6), and the price's unit stays where the corpus already holds it, in the two-observer court (§1.15). The seed gives the structure, the arithmetic, and the census's shape; only the count, and the unit, are borrowed.

**The sugar ledger.** Each row names arithmetic already above; nothing in it adds content.

| sugar | desugared |
|---|---|
| "determinant," "cross product (2D)," "Plücker bracket," "symplectic form" | $D$ — cross-multiplication's residue, the seed |
| "projective equivalence" | $D = 0$ (F2) |
| "basis," "coordinates" | a disagreeing frame; disagreements with its ends (F5) |
| "$\det(AB) = \det A \cdot \det B$" | transport applied twice (F6) |
| "cross-ratio" | the ratio of disagreement-products — the move-invariant (F6, §8.5) |
| "light-cone coordinates," "$k$-calculus" | disagreements with the corner pair; stretches (F8) |
| "$i$" | the second corner pair's address, a pair $(0,1)$ (F9) |
| "adding fractions / common denominator" | manufacture the shared reference by product, then add tops (F10, §3.7.1) |
| "negation $-x$" | $N \cdot A = (-v : h)$, the one-seat flip (F10) |
| "the Cauchy / Fubini–Study weight" | swap$(1 + A \cdot A)$ — square, add corner, reciprocate; the minimal sign-blind share (F11, §4) |

*Files: `d_check.py`, `d_build.py`, `d_census.py`, `d_arith.py`, `d_cauchy.py`; the D1 exhibits behind them (compression, the rational criterion, the ramified prime, the free-set asymmetry, the silver ladder) are banked in `d1_check.py` and `d1_spinor_register.md`, none load-bearing here, all to be re-derived as further clothes of $D$ — F9 is the first installment. The one sentence to carry forward: **the atom is its disagreements — the pair is $D$ with a frame, the corner is $D$ with the swap, the price is $D$ of the move itself, arithmetic is $D$'s two signs, and the census is swap$(1 + A\cdot A)$ counted — so the measure's shape and selection are the seed's, and only the act of counting is still borrowed.***
