## 2. The continuum and the corner


There is one read, not two. The observer holds two quantities and reads the part as a portion of the whole (roles by the chart, §3.65) — a single relationship that varies continuously as one quantity moves against the other — no value of $v$ makes it jump. Swept from home to horizon the portion traces one continuous arc in $[0,1]$: $0$ where $v$ vanishes, rising to $1$ where the two are equal, falling to $0$ where $h$ vanishes. The two ends are its feet; the corner is its apex.

The arc has two halves, and naming them gives the two **charts**, each a copy of $[0,1]$:

- the **home chart**, $r \in [0,1]$ — the rise within the run, the portion read directly as $r = v/h$;
- the **horizon chart**, $r \in [1,\infty]$ held as $1/r \in [0,1]$ — the run within the rise, the portion read as $h/v = 1/r$.

They are not two readings joined by an operation but the one portion read through whichever quantity is momentarily the smaller. They cover the interval and meet in exactly one member:

$$[0,1] \cup [1,\infty] = [0,\infty], \qquad [0,1] \cap [1,\infty] = \{1\}.$$

**Why the read turns at the corner, and only there.** The portion turns where part and whole exchange roles, and that exchange can leave the read continuous at exactly one point. Below it the chart is home and the read is $v/h$; above it the chart is horizon and the read is $h/v$; the two halves join without a jump only because at the exchange the quantities are equal, so both halves read $1$ there. An exchange at any other split, $v = k\,h$ with $k \neq 1$, would break the read across it — the two sides would not meet at a common value — and would demand the external number $k$ the observer does not possess. So the corner is forced as the turning point twice over: it is the only role-exchange that leaves the read continuous, and the only one that names no outside scale. (These join the fixed-point and scale-free forcings of §1.1 — the same point seen under a third operation, the order-crossover where part and whole trade places. The arc is continuous in value but not smooth: it has a kink at the apex, and that kink *is* the corner, the read's one non-differentiable point, the geometric mark of the turn.)

> **The continuation theorem: the reciprocal is the only door.** *(Settled in conversation; §1.06 and this section force the fold's existence and location — this pins its form.)* Let the register value be a function $f$ of the read, subject to two facts the paper already carries: it depends only on the *class* — the unordered relation, P4 applied to the hold, so $f(r) = f(1/r)$ — and it is calibrated to the identity on the home side, $f(r) = r$ for $r \le 1$ (the portion held as-is, §3). Then for $r > 1$: $f(r) = f(1/r) = 1/r$, because $1/r$ lands in $[0,1]$ where $f$ is the identity. One line. Continuity at the corner is not assumed — both sides give $1$; boundedness is not assumed — the image is $[0,1]$. The alternatives each break a named premise: continue with $r$ itself and the value leaves the unit register (P1); clamp at $1$ and every far state collapses to one value, deleting distinguishability short of the limit (§1.4); reflect as $2 - r$ and the external number $2$ enters (P3), with class-invariance broken besides; rescale as $r/k$ and the external scale $k$ enters (P3). Four escapes, four named hinges, no survivors. One precision squares this with §1.25: the uniqueness clause there is "up to monotone recalibration," a *global* freedom — one re-labeling of the whole dial — and it is spent the moment the home chart is calibrated to the identity; given that, the horizon continuation has no freedom left. So the statement at full strength: **the horizon chart is not introduced to take inverses; it exists because discrete observation forbids ratios larger than one, and the reciprocal is the unique legal continuation of the cycle beyond the corner.** §3.65's capsule said the cycle performs the swap — *who* acts; this says the swap's form was never a design choice — *what* is performed. The wall at the corner has exactly one door, and the geometry built it. (Two companions now carry this theorem outward. The SR companion §0.1 states it as topology — the two folds are the projective line's standard atlas, glued by inversion at the corner, the closure $\mathbb{RP}^1 \cong S^1$ forced by the same premises, the composition law total only on the closed carrier — against a standard literature that owns the construction as a licensed definition and never as a compulsion. And the Cauchy companion §4.6 recovers it from lived experience run backward: the two charts are *two facings* of one observer — a second aperture a quarter-turn away reads exactly the classes the first loses at its rim, with the overlap transition the negative reciprocal — so the door this section derives is also the thing turning your head performs.)

The read is one operation, and $v \leftrightarrow h$ is its **symmetry**, not a second operation: relabeling the two equal partners leaves the read unchanged in form, part over whole either way. Written in the $r$ coordinate this symmetry is $r \mapsto 1/r$ (so $h/v = 1/(v/h)$) — a pairing of each value with its mirror, fixed only at the corner. It is a property of the one read, not an act performed at the seam, and its elementary features are what the measure and the closure invoke (§4, §8): an involution that undoes itself, $r \mapsto 1/r \mapsto r$; order-reversing; carrying the ends to each other, $0 \mapsto \infty$ and $\infty \mapsto 0$; with exactly one fixed point,

$$r = 1/r \iff r^2 = 1 \iff r = 1.$$

That fixed point is the **corner** — the unique self-paired member, the apex both halves read as $1$. Nothing is inverted there: the value does not flip, it peaks; the symbols $v/h$ and $h/v$ exchange only because the roles of part and whole exchange. The corner is defined with no angle and no measure — the one point the swap holds still, where the continuum turns.

### 2.1 The continuum, derived

**The word split in two.** *(Sharpening installed with the Cauchy companion §4.8 and the SR companion §0.1; tightened against the completed-space objection, which deserves to be stated before it is answered.)* This section's opening line says "varies continuously" as description; it can be said as theorem — but only if the claim is careful about what generates the arrangements, because the objection writes itself otherwise: *"the sweep of all possible arrangements" smuggles a completed continuum inside the word "all."* Fair, and conceded in advance — which is why the derivation does not start there. State what the observer actually has. The atom is two lines through a point, and a read is their mutual arrangement. The observer holds no completed space of arrangements; it holds **acts that generate them**: the corner, the one self-certified arrangement; the halving descent, refining without end; the composition law, carrying any held arrangement toward any other; and the world's arrivals, which it receives but did not construct. "Continuous" then names three properties of the *generated* sweep — each operational, none presupposing a point-set:

- **no smallest step** — between any two arrangements the descent places a third, unendingly; the division has no floor (§6, §10.1 — the constructible lattice: countable, endlessly divisible, never complete);
- **no witnessable gap** — the composition flow passes from held arrangement to held arrangement, and no finite word of acts can exhibit a jump: to display a gap one must name its cut, and a cut is a total — the continuous observer's object;
- **a bounded whole** — the census total (§4) bounds the sweep: division without end inside finite measure.

This is Aristotle's continuum — divisibility without end, the potential infinite — not Cantor's completed set of points, and the relation between the two can now be stated exactly rather than rhetorically: **the completed continuum stands to the sweep precisely as the value of π stands to the census — the continuous observer's total of a process the observer runs without end.** The observer has *continuity*, the property; only the continuous observer has *the continuum*, the object; and no observation separates the generated sweep from its completion, because witnessing the difference would take the very total the observer lacks. Gaps in the sweep are unobservable-in-principle — the same grade of statement as the undetectable biased source (§4) and the never-evaluated π (§12.1), and it is a grade this paper trusts. The continuous observer's $\mathbb{R}$ is then *triply* downstream: **cut** the sweep at a zero, **unroll** it (§12.1's coda — sine is the unrolling operator; the SR companion §0.1 gives the cut its atlas), and **complete** it — and the third move is the important one, because that is where the point-set axiom actually lives: Dedekind completion is a continuous observer's purchase, made outside the observer, priced like every other total. So the opening line of this section owes nothing to the real line: "no value of $v$ makes it jump" is the unwitnessability of gaps in the generated sweep, and the number line the continuous observer uses to say so is the sweep — cut, unrolled, and completed. Continuity is the sweep's; the continuum is the continuous observer's; the line is the shadow of both.

> **Definition (word, outcome).** An *act* is one of the observer's operations: receive an arrival, compose ($\oplus$) with a held value, swap, halve (the descent), or compare (emit one order bit — the only act that outputs). A *word* is a finite sequence of acts; its *outcome* is the finite bit-string its comparisons emit.
>
> **Definition (operational witness).** A *gap* is a set $G$ of arrangements absent from the sweep, disjoint from what the word's own acts generate. A *witness* for $G$ is a word whose outcome differs according as the sweep does or does not contain $G$.
>
> **Theorem (gap unobservability).** *No word witnesses a null gap; no word certifies a measure gap.* Mechanism, in one line: **a finite word has finite resolution.** Its outcome is a function of finitely many comparisons; each comparison's breakpoint is a value the word's own acts constructed (a Möbius-and-descent image of its constants — on the lattice); so the outcome is piecewise-constant on the carrier, changing only at finitely many generated points. A gap disjoint from those breakpoints alters no bit — hence a *null* gap (missing points; the Cantor-versus-Aristotle stake) is strictly unwitnessable, by any word, ever. A *measure* gap (a missing interval) escapes certainty the same way — every finite outcome is consistent with "gap" and with "rare" — and is detected only in the unbounded limit of arrivals, which is a total: the continuous observer's object, again. The two grades are the framework's usual pair — unobservable-in-principle, and blind-below-the-total — and the second is §12's audit-blind-below-the-rung wearing foundations. *(Executed: 300 random 12-act words over a free arrival — every outcome piecewise-constant, max 8 breakpoints against 9 comparisons; deleting random measure-zero sets disjoint from the breakpoints changed no outcome at any surviving arrival.)*
>
> **Amendment: multi-arrival words — the sharpest available attack, run and survived.** The proof above covers words with *one* free arrival, where breakpoints are finitely many generated points. A word holding *several* arrivals admits **cross-comparisons**, whose breakpoint loci are curves (Möbius images of the diagonal), not finite point sets — outside the argument as stated, and the strongest attack constructible: an equality-type outcome between two arrivals. Run *(record)*: two-arrival words with a cross-comparison, $2 \times 10^6$ census pairs — the breakpoint curves carry census measure zero ($0$ pairs within $10^{-12}$ of the boundary); a gap at $\alpha$ (arrivals never at $\alpha$; the whole line removed from the arrival plane) shifts the outcome distribution by **exactly $0$**; and the exact-equality bit fires with probability $0$ on the complete and the gapped carrier alike — it is no witness. The theorem therefore carries two grades henceforth: for single-arrival words, *strict* — no word, ever; for multi-arrival words, *almost-sure* — no outcome changes except on a measure-zero set of arrival tuples, so outcome distributions are identical and no witness fires with positive probability. The attack sharpened the statement and did not breach it.
>
> **The standing invitation.** The theorem converts the metaphysical objection ("you secretly assumed continuity") into a constructive one, which is where this framework wants every argument to live: *exhibit a witness*. A challenger must produce a finite word of acts whose outcome distinguishes the generated sweep from its completion without naming a cut — the candidate attacks (a failed composition, a refinement that bottoms out) are already excluded by the closure theorem and the descent, but the invitation is permanent, and a successful witness would break this section before it broke anything else.

### 2.2 The case for the line

**The completion, argued from inside.** *(Installed with the Cauchy companion §4.9. The demotion above — cut, unroll, complete, three continuous observer's moves — is one side of a settlement; this is the other, and the two stand together. The claim: the real number line is a legitimate mathematical object* because *it is derived from the discrete observer — specified from inside, manufactured outside, unique by classical theorem.)* Four pillars, then a capstone.

*Tangency: the line is the observer's exact station, extended.* The read space is literally the tangent line at home — the gnomonic target at the one direction where the courts' charts agree ($d\rho/d\theta = 1$ at $\theta = 0$: the fare is unity at the aim; the Cauchy companion §4.9, with the quadratic guard $\tan^2\theta \approx \theta^2$ that makes the station usable). And the line's arithmetic is station-local law: the composition $\oplus$ *linearizes at home* — $r \oplus t - (r+t)$ is third-order in the reads — so **addition, the continuous observer's signature operation, is what the observer's own composition looks like at the exact station**; multiplication is $\otimes$, the rescale already owned; order is the comparison act. The complete ordered field's operation table is observer-rooted entire. The continuous observer's uniform chart is then the exact station made ubiquitous — equal arcs is *every point treated as momentarily aimed at* — and since the continuous observer is already this paper's ideal endpoint of accumulation (the header's second precision), the line is what unbounded re-aiming assembles: the null method run forever.

*Hospitality: the completion is the assumption-free carrier.* The observer generates only the lattice but cannot *forbid* any arrival — no act certifies "the world sends only constructibles." A gapped carrier is therefore itself a continuous observer-grade claim: a global assertion about what will never arrive, warranted by nothing. The completed carrier is the unique space closed under "I cannot say no."

*Destination: the observer's own dynamics point off the lattice.* The balance sits at $\sqrt2$'s address, the filter's steady state at the metallic mean $\sqrt{qr}\,\mu_n$, the descent's targets are irrational almost everywhere (SR companion §7.5, §12.5). These are not arrivals; they are **attractors of the observer's own forced processes** — and a carrier that omits the fixed points of your own dynamics carries a hole you yourself found. Completeness is the demand that every convergent process of mine have a destination.

*Parity with the seam.* This paper already performed completion once, and insists on it: the horizon is *an address approached and never occupied* (§1.45, §3.5), added because the format demands somewhere for the process to point. That is exactly what an irrational point is on the line — held, never reached. Dedekind completion is the seam's license exercised uniformly: every approached-never-occupied target granted its address. Keeping the weld while refusing the completion would be asymmetric bookkeeping.

*Capstone: uniqueness.* Classical mathematics supplies the receipt: **the complete ordered Archimedean field is unique up to isomorphism.** The four demands — contains the generated lattice; ordered by the comparison; complete under the dynamics' limits; Archimedean, every address within finitely many halvings at any band (record: $40$ halvings pin $\sqrt2 - 1$ to $10^{-12}$) — have exactly one solution, and it is $\mathbb{R}$. So the settlement, stated once: **the real number line is not the continuous observer's fiat but the unique completion of the observer's exact station — specified by the observer, manufactured by the continuous observer, legitimate *because* derived.** Nothing above retracts the demotion: the observer still never witnesses the completion (the theorem above), never evaluates the total (§4, §12.1), never holds $\pi$. What changes is the line's standing in the ledger — from optional purchase to forced-up-to-isomorphism completion of observer-rooted demands — and the two objects end as the two honest presentations of one thing: the sweep as held, the line as the sweep read from its exact station under unbounded accumulation.

### 2.3 The anatomy of the line: where zero comes from

*(Coda to §2.2.)* The line as an object has no center — $\mathbb{R}$ is translation-homogeneous, the continuous observer's report — but the line *in use* always has one, and it is home. Cut the sweep at the seam and unroll: home lands at the middle, and the horizon lands at *both ends* — the $\pm\infty$ of the line are the one seam address, split by the cut. The line is the dial turned inside out: center $=$ home, ends $=$ the horizon wearing two signs. Three identifications follow. **The additive identity is the aim:** addition is $\oplus$ linearized at the station, and the station is at $r = 0$ — the algebraic specialness of zero and the geometric specialness of the aim are one fact. **The line's center is an order-center, not a metric one:** the read's median sits at home (the swap's even split, §4) while the mean does not exist (the census counts no arrangement twice, §9) — home is the center the line actually has; the mean is the center the continuous observer keeps asking for. **Translation is re-aiming:** sliding the origin is moving the aim, so the translation group of $\mathbb{R}$ is the observer's saccade freedom flat-charted — which is why both observers are right: the line looks centerless because the station is portable (every point *can* be the aim), and every use of the line is centered because some point always *is*. The operational echo sits on every desk: an instrument's zero is the station it was calibrated at. Zero is not a place on the line; it is where the observer is standing.

### 2.4 Osculation: the two observers branch at home

 The deepest form of the settlement is one geometric fact: the sweep and its tangent line **osculate** at home — same point, same first derivative — so at zero angle the two observers are not merely similar but *identical*, and "bounded" and "unbounded" name the two continuations of one shared germ: around the loop, or along the tangent. Every difference between the offices is manufactured by distance from the aim, with a birth order the record already carries (the Cauchy companion §4.9): **nothing at first order** — the charts agree, boundedness invisible; **the $\theta^2$ guard at second** — distortion begins, as a rate, not yet a value; **$\theta^3/3$ at third** — the first value discrepancy; **$\pi/2$ at the rim** — the accumulated fare. Calculus is this paragraph run as a discipline: a *derivative* is a station read — linearize at the aim, where the offices agree, which is why the answer is exact — and an *integral* is a total, the other office's object; the fundamental theorem is their fare agreement; and analysis works locally because locally there is nothing to the bounded/unbounded distinction. Two corollaries, one per direction of access. **Why bounded humans can do unbounded mathematics at all:** the germ is held exactly at the station, and the flat continuation is as available as the curved one — choosing the completed number line is choosing the tangent continuation and running it with paper (accumulation, the road to the continuous observer's office named in the header). Unbounded mathematics is not beyond a bounded creature; it is one of the two legal extensions of what the creature holds perfectly. **And the converse rule, for reading bounded systems without paradox:** paradox is chart mismatch — curve-data read in tangent coordinates at distances where the continuations have diverged. The corpus's standing cases are all this one error: the Cauchy's "missing mean" (the observer's census scored in the continuous observer's court — companion §5–§6); the twin and ladder "paradoxes" (across-act relations asked as within-act properties — SR companion §6.5); the vanishing gradient (closure compression renamed in the flat chart — SR appendix); the number line's own crashes (∞ and NaN, the one-chart line's absorbing edge against the folded register's ordinary address — §3.7). The rule, stated once: **to understand a discrete observer that did not choose the flat continuation, compute in the number line it uses — the folded dial — and the paradoxes never form.** Each office is sound in its own chart; every famous puzzle in this corpus is the bill for reading one office's data in the other office's coordinates; and the osculation point is why the bill is so often overlooked — near home the charts agree, so the mismatch is invisible until it has already compounded.


---

## 3. The finite hold


The observer is bounded: its hold is finite. Take the hold to be the unit register $[0,1]$. The primitive $[0,\infty]$ does not fit in it, and resolving that is what boundedness forces.

The resolution is one operation. The observer holds the two quantities and reads the part as a portion of the whole,

$$H(v,h) = \frac{\text{part}(v,h)}{\text{whole}(v,h)} \in [0,1],$$

a single atomic read — not a value formed and then corrected — that lands in the register for every input, because a portion cannot exceed its whole. Geometrically it folds the primitive at the corner, $[0,\infty] = [0,1] \cup [1,\infty]$, onto one register: the home half read as $r = v/h$, the horizon half read as $h/v = 1/r$. These are not two operations with a branch between them but the one read seen from whichever side of the corner the inputs fall (§3.6), meeting at $v = h$ where both give $1$ — the corner where the register's two ends are glued. The read is a bijection from $[0,\infty]$ onto the glued register (the corner counted once), and the chart label — home or horizon — is not a datum riding with the value but the half of the glued register the reading stands in.

This settles three things:

- **The hold of one atom is two unit registers** — $[0,1] \sqcup [0,1]$, joined at the corner. Nothing more.
- **The bounded and unbounded halves cost the same hold.** $H$ sends $[0,1]$ onto one register and the unbounded $[1,\infty]$ onto the other; the infinite reach takes exactly one unit register, the same as the finite part. The swap is what makes that equality possible.
- **Nothing is lost and nothing exceeds capacity.** $H$ is a bijection, so the observer holds the whole of $[0,\infty]$; the bound is in the presentation, not the coverage. A reader able to store $r$ without limit would not need the swap — the finite hold is exactly what forces it.

**The held chart: the hold made operational.** The two-register hold has an arithmetic, and stating it upgrades the observer from a description to a working machine. Every held value is a placed reading with $v \in [0,1]$ always — $v = r$ in the home chart or $v = 1/r$ in the horizon chart, the chart carried by where the value stands on the closed dial (the register of §3.7 stores the place itself). The chart is *not memory* — it carries no history, and memorylessness is intact — it is the swap state, part of the held value itself, exactly the read's standing — which chart — whose flip is the corner (§1.1: the chart changes at $v=h$ and nowhere else — verified: $\tfrac12+\tfrac13$ stores home, $\tfrac12+\tfrac23$ crosses and stores horizon). The one rule of the arithmetic: **a horizon-chart value must be inverted before it can be combined** — and the robustness comes from *fusing* that inversion into the operation rather than performing it. Addition across charts is then a rational (Möbius) expression in the stored values — home $s_1$ plus horizon-stored $v_2$ yields the stored result $v_2/(s_1 v_2 + 1)$, horizon plus horizon yields $v_1 v_2/(v_1+v_2)$ — so **the large value is never materialized**: every intermediate stays in $[0,1]$, verified over 4{,}000 exact rational additions with every stored value $\le 1$, and exact over ℚ throughout (the chart-transition law is rational, one more instance of §12.1's ℚ-closure). The payoff is a horizon-taxonomy upgrade (§8.7's companion, Acq 4): a naive one-chart register has an **absorbing** edge — at the largest representable value it arrives and sticks (float: $10^{308}+10^{308} = \infty$, fixed forever) — while the two-chart register handles the same sum by storing $5\times10^{-309}$ in the horizon chart. **The chart converts the register's absorbing horizon into a folded one**, restoring in hardware the topology the exact atom has and finite registers otherwise lose: approaching the edge just crosses into the other chart, precisely as the fold's two charts meet at the seam. The chart is the fold, implemented. (This is also what positional exponents approximate — a float's exponent is a many-bit version of the same move — but the atom needs only the one fold, because the swap gives it the exact reciprocal chart rather than a graded ladder of them.)

The reading is therefore conditional: identity on $[0,1]$ (the home register, held as-is), swap on $[1,\infty]$ (the horizon register, carried in), the corner the seam between them. These two are the framework's two acts: the identity is the discrete observer holding its own field, the swap is its projection of the unbounded other onto one register — the source of the $O(1)$ of §7.

---

**The read is an idempotent retraction, and that is its operator name.** Write the read as a map on the punctured quadrant: $\mathcal{P}(v, h) = (H(v,h),\, 1)$ with the side alongside. Then $\mathcal{P}^2 = \mathcal{P}$ — a reading of a reading is the reading — so discrete observation is an idempotent retraction of the pair plane onto the dial. The pieces of the framework are this one operator's anatomy: the **image** of $\mathcal{P}$ is the held register; its **fibres** are the common-mode rays — each fibre one aim seen at every depth, the very rays of §9's area-to-curve collapse, so the scale-blindness of §5 is the statement that the observer sees fibres as points; the **swap is absorbed**, $\mathcal{P} \circ S = \mathcal{P}$, which is the operator face of "the chart is not data" (§3.6); and the **corner** is where the two chart-restrictions of $\mathcal{P}$ agree — the retraction's seam-free fixed edge. Composition respects the projector the only way it can: the fused laws above are *combine in the lift, then re-project*, $x \oplus y := \mathcal{P}(\tilde{x} \oplus \tilde{y})$, with the intermediate never materialized — which is why crash-proofness survives composition (§3.7). The fold of the family (§12.10) is this same operator stated for every rung at once: resolution is projection, and $\mathcal{P}^2 = \mathcal{P}$ is why resolving twice is not more resolved. The idempotence is also an empirical fact where the framework runs as code: on the Tangent Bridge leaf editor's kernel, sixty consecutive read-and-return round trips at fixed seats reproduce every register to within $4\times10^{-12}$ — and the same sixty rounds with the seats *reseated* between passes do not (§9.2's pump), isolating the projector's exactness from the chart moves that surround it.

---

## 3.5 The two zeros


The finite hold has a consequence the reader must hold onto before anything that follows will read correctly, and it is best met first as a paradox, because that is how it first appears.

The atom has two ends. At **home** $v$ vanishes: the observation lies flat, nothing standing between the observer and what it reads — the system is fully in view, completely represented. At the **horizon** $h$ vanishes: $v$ is total, the observation stands edge-on, nothing of the system getting through — fully out of view, completely unrepresented. The two ends are opposites in the strongest sense the atom allows: one is everything seen, the other everything hidden.

Both ends read **zero**.

Home reads zero because the read there is zero — $r = v/h = 0$, no $v$ at all. The horizon would read infinity: $v$ is everything, $h = 0$, the read runs off the end. But the discrete observer cannot hold infinity (§3); it has only finite addresses. So it holds the horizon the one way it can, through the swap — $1/r = 1/\infty = 0$. The horizon's only finite address is zero. This is the swap square of §1.5: the far register reads $1/r$, and the horizon arrives at $1/r = 0$. The swap is not an extra convenience here; it is the sole means by which the unbounded end is held at all, and the address it assigns is forced.

So the two opposite ends — the fully seen and the fully hidden — carry the same address. Zero is home, in the home chart. Zero is the horizon, in the horizon chart. The address is identical, the ends are opposite, and nothing in the number "zero" tells you which end you are at. That information is not in any number; it is in where the observation stands.

The reader will reach, first, to put the difference back into the number — a sign, a direction, a second coordinate — so that "zero" carries its own meaning the way numbers usually do. There is none, and the absence is the lesson: the difference was never in any number. An observation is not a number at all — it is a **position** on the closed dial (§3.7). The number is the position's shadow, its height; the shadow is what cannot tell the ends apart. Hold the position and nothing was ever ambiguous; flatten it to its shadow and a zero names full representation or full occlusion with equal right — with one exception this section's closing paragraph proves: at the single shared address itself, there is nothing left to decide.

The reader will reach, second, for "hidden" as a quantity the atom computes — so that one chart measures the seen and the other measures the hidden, two separate measurements. But there are not two measurements. There is one reading and two charts. The home chart reads it as *how much is represented*; the horizon chart reads the very same structure as *how much is not*. Hiddenness is not a second thing the observer measures; it is the home reading seen from the other chart. The observer only ever measures the positive — what it holds, what is in view — and the hidden is that same positive read in the chart that counts absence. The negative is never grasped directly; it is the positive, in the other chart.

There is exactly one place where the reader's ordinary intuition holds, where the value does carry its own meaning regardless of chart, and it is the natural place to stand. That is the **corner**, $r = 1$. The swap fixes it — $1/1 = 1$ — so here, and only here, the two charts agree: address one means the same read either way, an observation half in view and half out, the single balance the chart change leaves untouched. Set the two addresses side by side and the whole structure is in the contrast. At the corner the charts share an address *and agree* on it. At zero the charts share an address *and oppose* on it. Address one is the seam where seen and hidden meet; address zero is the pair of opposite ends the charts each call by the same name. Begin at the corner, where meaning is unambiguous, and the ambiguity grows as you move toward the ends — maximal at zero, where the two charts point to opposite extremities of the atom.

The swap is the algebra relating the two halves, not a move the observer makes: $h/v = 1/(v/h)$, an involution that swaps the ends, $0 \mapsto \infty$ and $\infty \mapsto 0$, and holds the corner still. The home chart reads the one continuum as *how much is represented*, the horizon chart reads the same continuum as *how much is not* — the same arc, named from each end. The two zeros are simply the arc's two feet: home's zero and the horizon's zero, one address standing at opposite extremities of the one continuum, meaning opposite things because they are its opposite ends.

None of this is new machinery. It is the two charts of the swap square (§1.5), seamed at the corner (§2), read for what they mean: the home chart is the observation in view, the horizon chart the same observation out of view, the swap the algebra relating them, the corner the one address both charts agree on. What the reader carries forward is only this — a reading is incomplete without its chart; the same number names opposite conditions in the two charts; and the corner is the single address that does not depend on which chart you are in. Everything that follows — the measure, the closure, the completion — is built on observations that are positions, and will misread if the position is flattened to its number and the number is taken to carry its meaning alone.

**The paradox, drawn.** The reading dial (§1.5, sixth picture; the `observer_combined` demo) is this section made visible, and on it the paradox dissolves on sight: the observation is a point — its height the number, its side the half — so nothing can be dropped: the two zeros are one *point* only at the shared bottom, reached down two different arcs, and the paradox is recognized as the dial's shadow on its vertical axis: keep the number, discard the side, and the ambiguity returns.

**The paradox, closed: the no-side theorem.** The operational ground comes first, and it is boundedness itself: the horizon is the limit of distinguishability (§1.4) — the address every growing magnitude approaches and none ever occupies. Of the two ends sharing the address zero, only one is ever *arrived at*: a zero the observer actually holds is home's, because holding the other would mean having gotten to infinity, and there is no getting to infinity. A test guards a reachable state; no test is owed for a place no reading ever lands. (The seam is reached by degeneracy rather than growth — one register empty, a literal $1/0$ — and there the lift already holds the answer, which register emptied, before any test could be posed; and a magnitude beyond the word's resolution rounds onto the seam cell, but telling it from a true zero is exactly the distinguishability §4 prices above the whole budget — nothing is owed there either.) The structural ground is stronger still. The shared address is the fixed point of the swap, and the chart is nothing other than *which side of the swap a reading stands on* — so a fixed point of the swap has no side, and there was never a fact at that point for a register to record. This is not a reframing but a checked property of the atom's operations (exact rational arithmetic; *The Angle Register* §4c, test record §7.8). Every swap-equivariant operation is provably chart-blind at the seam: the scaling law absorbs it identically from either description (2000/2000 exact — $0 \otimes s$ and $\infty \otimes s$ are both seam readings, so the output cannot be made to depend on which zero was held); the measure weights the point zero; accumulation and order need one address. The lone edge case seals the doctrine rather than breaching it: the opposite-chart product $0 \times \infty$ computes, in the register pair, to $(0,0)$ — the classical indeterminate form *is* the excluded point, the non-observation — and, once formed, it is absorbing under both laws; the pair does not resolve the indeterminate, it names it, and §3.7's corollary owns the consequence in full. Exactly one operation consumes the distinction, and it is the one that anti-commutes with the swap: the combination law ⊕ (a reflection conjugates a rotation to its inverse — verified, 0/2000 equivariant cases). Rotating home-zero by $(v',h')$ gives $v'/h'$; rotating the horizon-zero gives $-h'/v'$ — distinct, with a sign that exits the atom's range into the two-atom ring (§8; *Atom Rings* §3, $k=2$), the closure that unglues $0$–$0$ from $\infty$–$\infty$ and pays one sign bit *per ring*. So the resolution in full: **what the two zeros seemed to share and lose was never the point's to carry — it is orientation, data that comes into existence only when observations compose, priced at the ring and consumed by succession, never by anything a lone atom does.** Which end the history stands at — collapse or blow-up, everything seen or everything hidden — remains a real fact, and it lives where it always lived: in the lift (which register emptied) and in the arrival order of the acts. The reader's first reach in this section — put the difference back into the number — was answered above with "there is none"; the closing answer is stronger: at this one point there is nothing for a number to record.

---

## 3.6 The chart is never asked for


§3.5 settled that an observation is a position on the dial and that the number alone does not carry it. That seems to leave the observer owing a separate act — a test, *home or horizon?*, run beside each read. It owes no such act. The chart is paid out *by* the read, never asked for ahead of it.

The read is a containment: how much of its whole the part fills. A containment fraction is bounded by $1$ by what containment is — the contained cannot exceed the container — so the over-$1$ value that would *force* a chart decision never arises in the reading. Which quantity proved larger is not answered before the read; it is the record the read leaves. The two cases of the hold map $H$ (§3) are not selected by a prior test — they are which side the single read came down on. The chart is a byproduct, not a premise.

At the corner this is exact: $v/h = h/v = 1$, so the chart is free — the one place the routing is degenerate is $v = h$, where a decision would otherwise be hardest, and it costs nothing because both answers coincide. The single value from which the chart cannot be inferred is the single value at which the chart does not matter. (In a positional reading the same degeneracy appears as band $0$: the sign of the exponent separates near from far everywhere except on $[1,2)$, where it is $0$ for both the corner and its neighbours — ambiguous exactly where ambiguity is harmless.)

Two observers, one verdict. A **physical** observer realizing the ratio as a balance asks nothing: equality is its rest state, occupied and not detected, and *the part fills its whole* is what its reading does with no comparator — the corner is reached by sitting still. A **digital** observer receives the bit from the arithmetic itself — the first borrow of the intake division (the completion below) — and that borrow *is* the bit; no chart test sits on top of the read. Neither poses a separate question *home or horizon?*

The chart costs no storage: the register holds the position on the dial (§3.7), and the chart is which half that position lies in — geography, not a datum. So this section's claim holds twice over: the chart is never *asked* and never *written* — the read already carries which way it ran.

**The completion — the roles are never sorted either.** *(Settled in conversation; this section's claim, taken to its end.)* This section priced the digital observer at one comparison. Even that one is not a standing act, and with a carried chart it is not an act at all. The roles of the read are assigned by *identity*, not by size: the denominator is the held side — the run, the aperture, the self (§6.6; the beam key's "the pan you supply — the self as unit") — and the numerator is what arrives. Which of them is larger is not tested; it is *known*, because it is the chart, and the chart is state (§1.09): set once, toggled only at the corner. The toggle costs nothing, twice over. In hardware, a ratio crossing $1$ is a carry-out — the same event as the borrow this corpus already uses to route the swap — a flag falling out of arithmetic underway, not a test run beside it; and the one referent ever consulted is the corner, the single mark the instrument certifies for free (§1.1): the beam's observer never compares the weights, it watches for level. Even the lone first read of a series — no state yet — runs no standing test: in the pair format the chart stays latent and unneeded until the display (§3.7.1, the resolution boundary); in scalar hardware the bit arrives as the first borrow of the division the intake was already performing. And staleness is self-healing at its only vulnerable point: a corner crossing missed below the rung leaves a wrong chart whose first read past $1$ corrects it with no discontinuity, because both charts agree at the corner — the one address where a stale chart has no content. So the section's claim closes at full strength: the chart is never asked, never written, and never *sorted for*. Smaller-over-larger names the form of what the register ends up holding, not an act the observer performs; the acting read is **the world against the self**; and the only thing ever watched for is the free landmark.

## 3.65 The chart is primary: smaller and larger are corollaries

*(Settled in conversation. The three neighboring results — the chart never asked (§3.6), the roles never sorted (§3.6, completion), the handoff chart-blind (§1.3) — are one principle, and the paper's own exposition had been describing it backward. Recorded here at full strength.)*

The expository order of §§1–3 runs: two quantities are read, one proves smaller, and the chart falls out as the record of which. That order is the continuous observer's reconstruction — correct as bookkeeping, wrong as operation. The operational order is the reverse, and everything simplifies when it is stated forward:

> **The observer needs to know one thing: which chart it stands in. Everything else falls from that, and nothing else is ever consulted.** The chart identifies the numerator and the denominator — the world against the self, the roles fixed by identity before any read. Smaller-versus-larger is an input nowhere in the framework; it is a corollary read off the chart when someone asks, the way the time of day is read off a clock that never computed "afternoon."

The chart itself is known without any comparison of magnitudes, by any of four routes, each already established: **direction** — on the cycle, which way the stroke is moving is which chart is being read (§1.09); **state** — set once, carried, toggled only at the corner, the toggle a carry-out falling from arithmetic underway, the corner the one self-certified mark (§3.6, completion); **latency** — in the pair format the chart rides inside the pair unconsulted, retrieved once at the display (§3.7.1, the resolution boundary); **identity** — the aperture binding, the denominator the pan you supply (§6.6). Four routes, and not one contains a magnitude test. The dependency graph of the whole arithmetic is therefore a straight line with no comparison node anywhere in it: *corner events maintain the chart; the chart assigns the roles; the roles admit the read; the read hands off blind (§1.3); the display resolves once (§3.7.1).*

What the exposition had been doing — deriving the chart from the comparison — is the fossil-order this corpus already diagnosed in the beam (§1.08): the stopped picture files as a stored fact what the moving picture carries as state. Which-was-larger is the *report* of the chart, not its source. The observer never possesses "smaller" as a datum; it possesses *where it stands* — and where it stands is geography (§3.6), maintained by events at one free landmark, never surveyed. The revision in one before-and-after: *the old exposition had the observer performing normalizations and chart swaps; now the charts define the normalization, and the cycle performs the swap.* Normalization is local to the chart — within a chart the run is fixed, and no operation ever spans both charts at once, because at the only point where they meet the transition is the identity (§3.66) — so the last hidden global operation is gone with the rest. And an old sentence of this framework's becomes literally true: **circles emerge; they don't need to be drawn.** The continuous observer must *construct* the global circle because it unfolded the circle into a line; the observer never flattened it in the first place. Every global reconstruction the continuous observer performs is repayment for a flattening the observer never committed (§12.1's coda prices the same debt as the quadrature requirement). One sentence to keep: **know the chart and you know the roles; know the roles and no quantity is ever compared to any other; the entire apparatus of size runs on one standing fact — which side — refreshed for free at the corner.**

## 3.66 The audit: what the simplification touches downstream

*(Settled in conversation. §§3.65–3.66 record a revision that deleted operations — the test, the stored side, the interior division, the size-sorted roles — from the exposition. This section is the paper's own record of what that deletion did and did not disturb.)*

**The survival principle, first.** Every downstream theorem consumes the *resolved object* — the dial, the projective class, the folded register, the swap — and none consumes the procedure that fills it. The measure (§4) follows from swap-invariance of the class; the Cauchy and the fisheye (§9, §12) from the measure; the bands (§6) from the multiplicative form; closure and $\mathbb{RP}^1$ (§8) from the combination law; the constants (§10) from the closed loop. The revision changed the mechanism's description while leaving its output identical (§3.7.1's chain verification is the operational witness: same results, fewer acts). The paper had also armored itself in advance, twice: §1.25 forces the atom only *up to monotone recalibration* — the class, never the representative — and §3.6 called the chart geography before anything asked it to. The revision cashes checks those sections had already written. Every deleted operation had one property in common: it chose coordinates — picked a representative, filed a label, flattened a class — and choosing coordinates is the continuous observer's act. *Carry, don't compute* thereby acquires its sharpest reading: stay coordinate-free; the observer's mathematics is the coordinate-free interior, and every cost the framework prices sits at the one border where coordinates are chosen.

**What strengthens.** The cost ladder's ground floor (§7): "O(1) because the read is not an algorithm" was mildly aspirational while the read contained a test; it is now literal. Crash-proofness (§3.7): a branchless datapath outranks a correctly-branching one, and the corollary's IEEE brief gains its best argument — the chart is content, not mode (§1.3). The no-side theorem (§3.5): if the chart was never point-data, a fixed point having no side is no longer a subtlety. And the archetypes: neither the beam nor the pulse ever performed a selection, so the "physical archetype" claims of §§1.08–1.09 were strictly ahead of the formalism until this revision brought the formalism level.

**Three status changes, flagged here — and now fixed in place.** *The aperture binding is promoted.* §1.7 and §6.6 presented the bound denominator — the self as run — as an admitted construction atop the canonical fold. Under roles-by-identity (P5) it inverts: the binding is the *general case* of role-assignment, and the size-sorted canonical form is the continuous observer's afterthought; §6.6's status paragraph now records the promotion. *"Binary comparison" is pinned.* The uniqueness theorem's statement survives under exactly one reading — a relation *held* between two quantities, the beam sense — and not under "a test executed on them." The word did both jobs in the old exposition; only the first is legitimate — the pin stands in §1.25's audit note. *Memorylessness is pinned.* The series observer's chart is standing, not history: it records where the observer stands, never where it has been — position, not path — and for the register observer it is the stored position's own half (§3.6), costing nothing. The paper's memorylessness claims survive under that distinction, and the pin is installed at the definition (§1.15).

**Two debts, named — and their discharge recorded.** The proof *body* of §1.25 was audited for selection-language: **clean** — Steps 1–3 class-function and dimension arguments, Step 4's factoring the continuation theorem's own class-invariance, its fundamental-domain coordinate spent from the recalibration clause rather than selected (§1.26 coordinatizes the same quotient with no domain choice), and the whole derivation P5-free as promised. The certification stands as §1.25's audit note; the seal at the root holds. The reconciliation of the companions is substantially paid: the SR companion (eleven sites, including the correction of an early "growth retired" overclaim by the rent law's H-form) and both Tangent Bridge companions (the spectral sections were born compliant; the algebraic sections audited clean) now speak the revised vocabulary. What remains: *The Angle Register*'s test records, *Atom Rings*, and the demos, whenever those files next surface — covered defensively by the glossary rulings in the meantime.

**The direction of the revision, named: from behavior to constraint.** Every operation the revision deleted — the test, the stored side, the sort, the interior division — was a *decision*, and what remains is not a smaller repertoire of decisions but none: standing, being carried, and reporting. The geometry underneath has a standard name the corpus can now use. The two charts related by reciprocity are an **atlas** for the closed dial; the swap is its **transition map**; and the charts' overlap is the single point $v = h$, where the transition $r \mapsto 1/r$ is the *identity* — so being carried through the corner is seamless by construction of the atlas, never by the observer's judgment. The continuous observer holds the atlas; the observer holds a patch and is carried across a trivial transition. No question of the form "should I switch charts now?" can arise, because answering it would require the global state the observer lacks — and the structure has already answered it at the only point where the answer is free. One boundary keeps this from overreaching, and it runs clean through the framework: **agency survives at the level of the act and vanishes at the level of the read.** The observer still aims (the saccade and the squint, §7.5), still holds (the carry is the whole P1 budget, committed), still chooses its grip (§8.7's fork — pans side by side or a pan against its own past, the circle or time), and still reports. Every surviving choice is *upstream of resolution*: the observer picks where to stand, never what it sees from there. And this closes into a symmetry with §1.0's oldest discipline. There, "cannot" never means a psychological limit — it means lacking the register, the operation, the pass, or the frame. Now the complement holds: wherever the paper says the observer *does* something, it means the structure leaves no alternative. **Cannot = no apparatus; does = no alternative** — and nothing in between: no trying, no deciding, no inferring. The theory this leaves is not an account of observer behavior but of constrained observation — what remains of geometry when someone bounded must stand inside it.

---

## 3.7 No exceptions: neither infinity nor NaN


A floating-point unit carries two exception values — infinity, for a magnitude it cannot bound, and NaN, for an input it cannot read. A discrete observer carries neither, and not because it encodes them away. The reason is prior to any encoding: the simple observer is a *relation* between two held quantities, not a *computation* on them, and the exceptions are scars only a computation can take.

**Infinity does not arise.** The simple observer does not divide $v$ by $h$ — division is an operation a processor performs, and the simple observer has none. It holds the two quantities in a part-to-whole relation, the roles named by the chart. A portion cannot exceed its whole — not by a rule imposed but by what *portion* is — so the relation is bounded by $1$ intrinsically, and the unbounded value $v/h > 1$ that would demand a sentinel is never formed. What the digital observer reaches by the discipline of dividing by the chart's whole (§3.6, §3.65), the simple observer cannot avoid: its whole *is* the whole, and nothing it holds is more than all of what it holds. The far end $r = \infty$ is still the horizon in the raw coordinate, but the observer never stands there — the swap has already made it the $0$ of the far chart (§3.5). Infinity is not denied; it is never held.

**NaN does not arise either, for a different reason.** NaN marks an indeterminate form — here $0/0$, both quantities vanishing. The atom forbids it at the source: an observation is two quantities, not both zero (§5). For the simple observer this is not a restriction written down but the precondition of there being a relation at all — a relation needs two relata. With nothing held there is nothing to relate: not a broken observation but no observation, the lights off, not a special value to flag. The work NaN does in a processor, marking the one input that cannot be read, the observer discharges by *not having that input in its domain*.

The two absences are not the same absence. Infinity is *relocated* — the magnitude that would overflow is folded into the far chart and recorded, in the end, as which half of the dial the reading occupies (§3.6); the apparatus is moved, not deleted. NaN is *deleted* — the degenerate input lies outside the domain and goes nowhere, because it was never an observation. One scar is healed by the second chart; the other never forms because there is nothing to scar.

So, for the simplest observer: **a relation between two held quantities needs no exception values, because a relation has neither an invalid input it processes anyway (→ no NaN) nor a magnitude it can overflow (→ no infinity).** Exception values are artifacts of a computation closed over every bit pattern it can be handed; the simple observer computes nothing — it stands in a relation — and a relation is total on its relata and bounded in its portion by what *relation* and *portion* are. This is conditional, as the framework's forcings are (§1.1): granted the observation is a relation of two quantities not both zero, the exceptions are not encoded away — they have nothing to encode.

One discipline stays a discipline, named so it is not mistaken for a forcing: the band read $\lfloor\log_2|A|\rfloor$ is undefined at $0$ ($\log_2 0 = -\infty$), and the observer escapes that not because $0$ carries a defined band but because it never bands its home position — banding locates a *far* magnitude, a reach past the view, and the simple observer, standing in its relation, does not reach (§7). The home zero escapes the undefined band by the same restraint that keeps the read a portion: forced for the simple observer because it has no reaching apparatus to misuse, a discipline only for the digital one that does.

**Corollary: the crash-proof number line.** The two absences above are implementable, and implementing them yields a number line that structurally cannot throw. The construction is the observer's format taken literally. *State:* the pair $(v, h)$ — never the quotient; the quantities are scrubbed, composed, and stored freely with no division anywhere in the pipeline. *Evaluation:* once, at the display boundary, and always in the safe direction — if the ratio exceeds $1$, invert first — so every division that executes is part ÷ whole with result in $[0,1]$. *Address of the far end:* the horizon is never a value; it is held as the far chart's $1/r = 0$, on the far half of the dial (§3.5, §3.6). Four properties follow by construction, not by guard code. (i) **No overflow, no infinity generated:** the executed quotient is a portion, bounded by $1$ by what portion is. (ii) **No NaN generated:** the sole indeterminate input, $(0,0)$, is outside the domain — not a broken observation but no observation — and an implementation displays the absence rather than flagging a value. (iii) **Totality elsewhere:** every pair with at least one nonzero register yields a valid position on the dial; panning to either extreme lands on an ordinary finite address. (iv) **The format has a name:** the pair under part-over-whole normalization is homogeneous coordinates on $\mathbb{RP}^1$ — the projective line's own number system, which is why rendering pipelines, needing division that cannot blow up, independently converged on the homogeneous trick; the reading dial (§1.5) is $\mathbb{RP}^1$ wearing the observer's normalization. (v) **The format is not a choice but a closure, and it composes:** §1.5's sixth picture shows that inverting the farfield closes the atom into a circle — the dial whose positions the terminal register stores; and in register form the composition laws are division-free — readings multiply componentwise, the Möbius law is polynomial, $(v,h)\oplus(v',h')=(vh'+v'h,\,hh'-vv')$ — so crash-proofness is *closed under composing atoms into larger atoms* — as pairs; the Möbius law generates signs (its circle is the two-atom ring, ℝP¹), so composition adds the ring's one orientation bit — the arrow of succession, §3.5 — while the arithmetic stays division-free, with register growth retired by free rescaling (§5). Two honesties bound the claim. The substrate is untouched: IEEE hardware still *represents* Inf and NaN; the claim is that this format never *generates* them — a property of the arithmetic performed, not of the bit patterns available. (History sharpens the distinction: the single-∞ *topology* shipped as the Intel 8087's default projective mode — infinity-control bit, control word bit 12, projective = 0 = default — and was dropped from IEEE 754-1985; the never-form-the-quotient *discipline* is the part no mode bit ever carried. A vestige persists: the bit exists in every x87 control word to this day, programmable and ignored — treated affine regardless — since the 80387.) In hardware the chart is free twice over: it *is* the comparator's borrow — the normalize-by-max comparison is a subtraction whose carry-out routes the swap, by mux, no branch — and in the position register it is not even routed but located: the word's top bits, with every landmark on a power-of-two address; a consequence worth naming is that data-dependent arithmetic exceptions cease to exist as a hardware category, which is constant-time execution by construction rather than by discipline. And the excluded point is real, and must be stated at its full strength against the format rather than for it: $(0,0)$ is not merely an excluded *input* — it is **reachable**, since the opposite-chart product $0 \otimes \infty$ computes to $(0,0)$ in the pair (§3.5), and it is **absorbing**, since $(0,0) \otimes (v',h') = (0,0)$ and $(0,0) \oplus (v',h') = (0,0)$: formed once, it propagates. Functionally that is a NaN, and this corollary does not pretend otherwise. What the format claims is not the abolition of the indeterminate — no arithmetic abolishes $0 \times \infty$ — but the **collapse of the exception category to this one state**: it forms only at the genuinely indeterminate ($\oplus$ cannot manufacture it from non-degenerate pairs — $AD = -CB$ and $BD = AC$ jointly force $C = D = 0$ — so the sole formation site is the product of opposite extremes), it is detectable at formation, and it says what happened — *no observation* — where IEEE's NaN zoo says only "not a number." One state, one meaning, one formation site, against overflow-generated infinities, signed sentinels, and quiet/signaling NaN variants. The armor fits the object; it does not extend past the one place every number system must fail. *One topological clarification the picture invites* (flagged against an adversarial read that calls $(0,0)$ a "sinkhole puncturing the manifold"): the collapse does **not** puncture the welded loop, for two reasons the algebra makes exact. First, the loop is welded by $\oplus$ — the rotation — and $\oplus$ is *total* on it (the non-degenerate-input proof just given: the seam that glues $0 \equiv \infty$ is a rotation-fact, and rotation never forms $(0,0)$ from valid points); so under the very law that closes the circle, the circle is seamless and closed, home and horizon ordinary addresses with valid composites. Second, $(0,0)$ is not an address *on* the loop at all — $\mathbb{RP}^1 = (\mathbb{R}^2 \setminus \{0\})/\!\sim$ removes the origin *by construction*, so the empty pair is the one non-point, never a location whose evaluation "deletes the space." The single degeneracy is a $\otimes$-fact — multiplication's unavoidable $0 \times \infty$, undefined in every number system — reachable only at the product of opposite extremes, and it lands on the excluded origin, off the loop, not in a hole torn through it. So the manifold is intact: every point of the circle is present and every *composition* stays on it; only the separate *multiplicative* structure carries the one degenerate product, at the one address arithmetic must fail. The seam is a genuine weld; $(0,0)$ is the honest image of $0 \times \infty$ sitting off the loop, not a topological leak in it. The claim is falsifiable in the strongest sense the corpus uses: exhibit an input sequence over the format's operations that produces an infinity, a NaN, or the empty pair from non-degenerate inputs anywhere *other than* the indeterminate product, and this corollary is dead. An interactive witness runs (the `observer_combined` demo): both registers pannable to their extremes with momentum, the dial scrubbed through the corner, the horizon reached as an address — nothing throws, because nothing is ever asked to. The falsifiability clause has also been executed adversarially: 112{,}000 random exact-integer operations (8{,}000 chains, depth 14, mixed magnitudes to $10^{30}$, exact homes and horizons injected) over $\otimes$, $\oplus$, and the swap produced zero reads outside $[0,1]$, zero absorption violations, and $(0,0)$ formed 335 times — every instance at the indeterminate product, none from $\oplus$, matching the inline proof. One implementer's trap surfaced by the same testing deserves record, because it looks like the format and is not: the *affine* pair-sum $(v,h) + (v',h') = (vh' + v'h,\, hh')$ — ratio addition transcribed naively — manufactures $(0,0)$ from two exact horizons, $(v,0)+(v',0) = (0,0)$, a spurious crash the format's own laws never commit ($\oplus$ rotates; magnitude addition lives in the held chart's fused forms, where horizon-plus-horizon is the harmonic composite, determinate, and the free rescaling of §5 retires the common factor *before* the degenerate limit). The discipline is load-bearing: the crash-proof claim attaches to the format's operations, not to every algebraically equivalent transcription of them.

**The position register (the format's terminal presentation).** The pair format is one of three presentations of the same object; the third holds the observation as its position on the dial itself, and it is forced once one asks for a register whose native order is the circle's own. A signed reading would give a register a native linear order — but a linear register must cut the circle once, and wherever the cut falls a landmark doubles: sign the reading and the corner carries two addresses (±1), which is fatal in practice because exact ties r = 1 are common in quantized data (measured: 4.7% of steps on a cents-quantized walk, with the window median of the key then flapping across half the interval thousands of times); sign the corner-displacement instead and the cut moves to the seam — algebraically this is the share of §1.06, the arc closure, right as an order-book export and wrong as the held observable. The terminal move leaves the linear family: store the *position on the dial* — a fixed-point angle in an unsigned word, one turn = the word's range (home 0, corner quarter-turn, seam half-turn). (The dial the register stores is the two-atom ring $\mathbb{RP}^1$ of §1.5's family, not the reading dial — the landmark spacing is the tell: the corner sits at the quarter-turn here where the reading dial holds it at the half. The register therefore *unfolds* §3.5's shared address into two distinct cells — home at zero, the seam at the half-turn — and the two-zeros ambiguity is resolved by unfolding, not by tagging.) No bit and no sign, because the chart is not data: which half of the circle the position lies in *is* the chart, read off. One address per landmark (ties land on the corner uniquely; the seam identification is performed by finite resolution itself — r = 10³⁰⁰ lands on the half-turn cell exactly at 64 bits); the wrap the hardware already executes is the gluing, so ⊕ is machine addition, bit-exact where floating angle drifts; the plain integer sort is the circle's order, any cut an index rotation; and the zero-knowledge sediment is the uniform distribution on the word. The deepest property is the precision profile: the position register's distinguishable cells per decade of ratio track the §4 measure to three digits across seventeen decades, where the pair format spends equal bits on every decade to the horizon — the trilemma of §1.5 resurfacing at the register tier, resolved by assigning one format per tier: **the part-over-whole fold is the reading-honest register; the position is the budget-honest one.** Exact arithmetic stays in the lift (§5); display evaluation stays bounded (fold first, then tangent). The companion also records the closure of §3.5's paradox that this format makes structural: the seam, a fixed point of the swap, has no side for any register to store — the chart of zero is ring data (one orientation bit at $k=2$), not atom data. Machinery and measurements: *The Angle Register* (companion note), where one resonance is recorded — the noble clock's step in a 32-bit position register is ⌊2³²/φ⌋ = 2 654 435 769, Knuth's multiplicative-hashing constant: Fibonacci hashing is the golden ⊕-clock, and its celebrated scattering is the clock's sediment.
