## 13.16 The hopping, priced: what the seam forces, and that no new scale enters

*(Takes §13.8's first open item — "deriving the hopping coefficient from seam mechanics rather than receiving it" — through its mechanical half. Grade discipline up front: what a derivation can mean here is bounded by the thesis itself — the coefficient carries physics' received scales, and no algebra originates a scale (P3; §8.7's boundary) — so the derivable content is structural: which properties of the seam coupling are **forced**, and how many received numbers remain. The answer delivered below: three forcings, and **zero new numbers**. Executable record: `hopping_check.py`, shipped.)*

**Forcing one — reciprocity: the seam must be read from both sides.** §13.7's seam is read by handoff, and the swap says the two sides' reads are one fact quoted twice: $\kappa$ from below is $1/\kappa$ from above. A coupling that reads the seam one way only cannot conserve the hold's total — executed: a one-sided seam coupling fails to conserve norm at $O(1)$ ($|{\rm norm}-1| = 0.97$ after 200 steps; the failure's sign is state-dependent — decaying-sector packets lose, generic states gain, §15.13) *under the Cayley map itself*, because the Möbius evolution is unitary only for a Hermitian generator — Hermiticity, not merely a real spectrum: the one-sided open-ended coupling is nilpotent, every Cayley eigenvalue exactly $1$, and norm still blows up through non-normal transient growth (§15.13) — while the reciprocal seam holds norm at $1.8\times10^{-14}$. So unitarity — §13.4's E-invariant carried under composition — **forces the seam coupling Hermitian**: $J_{x,x+1} = \bar J_{x+1,x}$. The swap-symmetry of the seam is not a modeling convention; it is what makes a conserved hold possible at all. (Re-verified in passing from this build: Euler drifts at $2.6\%$ over the same run; the Cayley correction of §13.8 stands.)

**Forcing two — the form: parity gives the second difference its dispersion.** No privileged direction along the $K$-axis (P4) plus nearest-neighbor seam structure forces the dispersion even in $k$: $\omega(k) = 2J(1 - \cos k\,\Delta x)$, with the $k^2$ onset at small $k$ (executed: measured against the closed form to six decimals at four wavenumbers). An odd, transport-without-dispersion term would require a preferred direction along the hold. This is §13.7's constructed $\Delta^2$ earning its coefficient's *shape*: the second difference is the only parity-even nearest-neighbor form, and §13.11 already read the same operator as curvature.

**Forcing three — the running: refinement covariance fixes $1/\Delta x^2$.** The seat spacing $\Delta x$ is the observer's seat density, not the world's — the $K$-axis is a hold (§13.7), and how finely the observer populates it cannot be physics. No-external-scale therefore demands refinement covariance, and it is exactly the seam coupling's running that must carry it — executed: with $J\,\Delta x^2$ held invariant under $\Delta x \to \Delta x/2$, the packet's measured group velocity converges under refinement ($0.776 \to 0.794 \to 0.798$ — the earlier printed $0.800$ was two-decimal rounding, corrected §15.20 from the regenerated record — the deviations the vanishing lattice correction $\sin(k\Delta x)/k\Delta x$); with any other running ($J \to 2J$ and $J \to 8J$ controls) the velocity is wrong by the running's error — $\times\tfrac12$, $\times2$ in the refinement limit; at finite spacing the exact factors are $1/(2\cos(k\Delta x/2))$ and $2/\cos(k\Delta x/2)$ (corrected by the blind adjudication, §15.13) — and refinement never reaches the true velocity: the $J\,\Delta x$ control degenerates to zero velocity, the $J\,\Delta x^3$ control diverges — the seat density would be physics. **$J\,\Delta x^2$ is the seam coupling's unique refinement invariant**, and the $1/\Delta x^2$ running — the part of the received coefficient that looked most arbitrary — is the part that is forced.

**And the invariant introduces nothing new.** $J\,\Delta x^2 = \hbar^2/2m$: $\hbar$ is §13.4's received action, $m$ is §13.3's received mass, and the measured group velocity $(\hbar/m)k$ is the de Broglie bridge those sections already paid for (executed: $0.77\%$ at the *middle* lattice, $0.19\%$ at the finest, closing with refinement — the original record was lost and its "$0.76\%$ at the finest" conflated the pairing; corrected §15.20 per the round-3 blind reconstruction, confirmed by the regenerated record `hopping_check_regen.py`). So §13.8's ledger line "[coefficients received]" tightens: **the seam receives no coefficient of its own** — it inherits the pair $(\hbar, m)$ already in the ledger, seated in a slot whose every property (Hermitian, parity-even, $1/\Delta x^2$) is forced. The parallel with §13.3 is exact and one notch sharper: form native, magnitude received — and here the magnitude is second-hand, not even a new receipt.

**The ring makes the hopping a clock — the ledger's named handle, turned.** The smallest closed substrate is two seats: the two-atom ring, open problem #3's "concrete handle on the dynamics." So the hopping has an operational face in the framework's own currency — $J$ is the rate of the smallest ring's clock, read as a ratio against the E-rotation clock: a rate ratio, the observer's kind of number, not a dressed constant. What physics calls a coupling strength, the substrate reads as *how fast the smallest loop walks*.

**What stays open, exactly.** The bridge itself: *why* the seam's invariant is $\hbar^2/2m$ — the identification of the seam-clock rate with the H-branch mass through the de Broglie relation — lives at §13.4's commutator grade `[strong-motivated]`, and nothing here upgrades it. ## Open problems and frontiers

The framework is deliberately narrow — a minimal, memoryless observer and the algebra its four premises force — and it is honest about its seams. Six are open, catalogued here so the **Success Criterion** (front matter) has an explicit ledger of what is not yet met. Items 1 and 5 are internal forks the paper reaches but does not close; items 2 and 3 are the next target theorems; items 4 and 6 are where the abstract algebra meets a concrete deploying system.

**1. The magnitude radix, and the angular-to-magnitude bridge (§6, §7) — resolved by the Radix Bridge companion, two-tier.** The question was whether the forced dyadic *angular* lattice ($g=2$ by exact-closure/bisection) forces an identical base-2 *magnitude* radix in the value store. The companion (*The Radix Bridge*) settles it with a strict separation. **Value layer — radix-neutral.** The corner's local differential rate is indeed forced to $2$ ($\left.\tfrac{dr}{d\theta}\right|_{\pi/4}=\sec^2\tfrac{\pi}{4}=2$, confirmed as the halving-step limit $\Delta r_d/\Delta r_{d+1}\to 2$), but $\tan\theta$ is non-linear: $r_+ = \tan(\tfrac{\pi}{4}+\delta) = 1 + 2\delta + 2\delta^2 + \tfrac{8}{3}\delta^3 + \cdots$, and the cubic residual $\tfrac{8}{3}\delta^3$ per step does not integrate to zero, so the local rate cannot tile the magnitude line into exact powers of two. The homogeneous, scale-invariant value algebra ($\otimes,\oplus$, Cauchy) therefore admits *any* base — no value-layer theorem forces $g=2$. **Register layer — $g=2$ forced as the optimum.** The position register is natively dyadic (bisection), and mapping a store address through $\theta(k)=\arctan(g^{k})\approx \tfrac{\pi}{2}-2^{-k\log_2 g}$ aligns bit-for-bit only when $\log_2 g\in\mathbb{Z}$; for any non-dyadic $g$, $\log_2 g$ is irrational and the band index leaks a Weyl-equidistributed phase jitter $\varepsilon(k)=(k\log_2 g)\bmod 1$, removable only by a transcendental $O(\log_2 g)$ rescaling per step (the *Non-Dyadic Entropy Leak Theorem*). So $g=2$ is the unique zero-leak, constant-time $O(1)$ store. **Net:** the radix is contingent in the algebra and forced in the register — the bridge is not a value-layer theorem but a hardware-optimality one. *(The companion's own statement of the residual as "$8\delta^3$" should read $\tfrac{8}{3}\delta^3$; the coefficient is verified $8/3$. The remaining thread is whether "optimality of the register" should count as "forcing" in the framework's strict sense, or stay labelled an architecture-selection result, as the companion frames it.)*

**2. Dynamics — coupling mass, momentum, and energy to the kinematic shell (§8.7, §13.2).** The framework is purely kinematic: it derives invariant kinematic *forms* — single-axis special relativity, the $k$-calculus of the H-branch — but originates no scale, exactly as the thesis requires, since the pair is *received* from the world and never authored (the observer supplies the form, the interaction supplies the magnitude). The frontier is to couple external physical scalars to that shell without breaking scale-independence — pure observation extended to physical dynamics. **§13.3 takes the first step**: dynamics as the observer's kinematic pair lifted to an affine pair by a *received* scale (mass in the H-branch, action $\hbar$ in the E-branch), the scale never read and so scale-independence intact — with **general relativity** the scale promoted from a constant to a field — **§13.5 firms that into a first step** (local scale-invariance forces a scale/Weyl connection whose non-integrability is a tidally-read curvature; the equivalence principle falls out, and the connection's *time* component gives **gravitational redshift**, $z = \Delta\ln\lambda = \Delta\Phi$, from the $\dot h/h$ aperture-rate gradient). Richer observers, and the next consistency tests (§1.0, §7, §12.9) — partly stepped; still open.** The core paper fixes the minimal architecture — one carried scalar, carry-not-compute, memoryless ($M = 0$). entropy production is the price of memorylessness (the shed bits are what the first retained register would keep — the M-axis split), and production, like equilibrium, is indexed by the hold (the exact clock's KS entropy is zero at every rung while its address pays the §10.15 rent forever). **§13.14 enters the temperature door**: the canonical *form* is the statistical layer's (MaxEnt on §13.12's entropy, or detailed balance — the Boltzmann factor as the fare ratio held constant per rung, geometric on the ladder to $10^{-15}$), the *scale* is received — and for the accelerated aperture the received scale is kinematic: the received $1/\text{chord}^2$ correlator evaluated on the observer's worldline gives detailed balance at measured $\beta = 2\pi/a$, so $T = a/2\pi$, with the banked factor-of-two thread (§15.1a) executed and adjudicated (half-slope chord kernel vs full-argument control; statistics in the chord's power) and Tolman anchored. **§13.15 delivers the fluctuation layer**: entropy production as the word read against its reverse (the two-seat read at path level), the integral theorem as normalization, the second law as Jensen, the H-theorem as the mean of an exact pathwise identity, strong Crooks and Jarzynski executed by full enumeration on the driven fare ladder — and the layer natively memory-priced ($\Sigma$ needs the word; $M{\ge}1$). **The statistical body's named list is now walked end to end**; what remains is quantum-court work: deriving the correlator itself (part of the interacting-$\hat H$ body) and the canonical ensemble for interacting systems.

**4. The law of $K$ — the deployment of acuity (§7.5, §7.6) — resolved in shape; value received.** §7.5 fixes *detail* as angular occupancy for a given hold $K$; **§7.6 settles the $K$–aperture conjugacy** ($K = 2\rho_0\arctan S$, bounded by $K_{\max} = \pi\rho_0$, squint varying $K$, attention Möbius-redistributing a fixed $K_0$) **and the origin of $\rho_0$**: a variational balance of value (a concave function of resolved distinctions) against the $O(K)$ inspection rent gives $\rho_0^{*} = \tfrac{1}{2\theta_A}(\alpha/\beta - 1)$, so central acuity is a *dynamic equilibrium*, not a rigid constant — expanding under task demand, collapsing to zero when nothing is worth resolving. This answers the frontier's structural question (dynamic, not fixed), but does not make the capacity parameter-free: it relocates $\rho_0$ to the *received* task-to-cost ratio $\alpha/\beta$ ($\alpha$ demanded by the environment, $\beta$ the observer's processing cost), a coupling received exactly as mass and $\pi$ are, and it rests on a diminishing-returns value assumed, not forced by P1–P5. The fork is resolved; the value is external.

**5. The change-atom's reference identity (§6.5) — resolved.** The change-atom reads $\rho = A_2/A_1$ against a register carried by handoff, and the question was whether the denominator is the immediately prior state (a *rate*) or a retained datum (*displacement* from an anchor). §6.5 settles it: the difference is one bit of **register-update policy** — overwrite the reference each step and the read is the rate, at $M{=}0$ (the memoryless handoff's default); latch it to an anchor and the read is displacement, at $M{=}1$ (one retained register). The memoryless observer natively reads rate; displacement is the first thing one unit of memory buys, and rate-atoms telescope exactly in the lift ($\bigotimes_k A_k/A_{k-1} = A_N/A_0$) so the two are interconvertible. Not a gap in the primitive — the $M{=}0/M{=}1$ boundary.

**6. Domain warping — how biased domains deform the native Cauchy (§1.8; *The Stream*).** §1.8 exhibits the primitive's structural isomorphism in real domains — audio's analytic signal, vision's cone pairs — but domain-specific measures (pitch resolution, for one) deviate from the isotropic Cauchy under domain biases. Open: developing the wave dynamics of *The Stream* — the oscillator as a two-atom ring, phase unrolling, frequency doubling — and formalizing how an anisotropic observer domain warps the native distribution.

None of these is a repair to what is proved; each is a direction the primitives point but the minimal paper does not walk. They are the framework's live edges, and the Success Criterion is what will judge the ones that reach known physics.

## 14. Conclusion: the two observations

The paper opened with a taxonomy and spent its length inside one of the two categories. The conclusion restates the taxonomy with everything now behind it, because the division reads differently once the machinery has been built.

**What was built, in one arc.** From four operational premises — one carried scalar, carry-not-compute, no external scale, no privileged frame — a single primitive is *forced*, not chosen: the binary atom — the portion read with its side — unique up to recalibration by a pigeonhole on dimension (§1.25). The atom's involution is the swap; its fixed point is the corner, the one self-certified state; its finite hold folds the unbounded ladder onto two unit registers welded at one seam (§3), and the weld is where the whole system's exception lives — one crash address, reachable only at the genuinely indeterminate, absorbing thereafter, verified adversarially (§3.7). Scale-independence is the root: negate it and the atom, the corner, the swap, the carrier, the measure, and the total fall in sequence (§1.16). Downstream of the root: the unique swap-invariant measure, which is the Cauchy, which is the virtual circle worn in the slope coordinate (§4, §9); the interleaved pointing — many rises, one run — forced because one observation is one projective class and a class does not factor (§9, §9.2); the ladder of carriers, sphere upon sphere, with home a point at every rung, corner and horizon widening as spheres, each rung's horizon the previous rung's whole carrier (§12.10); the closed drawings — eight, clover, bouquet, sixteen glomes — in which the fused point at the middle of every figure is the observer's own address book, and the reader is drawn into the picture as its basepoint (§1.5); the offices of access — seen whole two rungs down, held one rung down, occupied at one's own rung, nothing above (§12.9); the carriers that compose, exactly three times, the framework having spent two of them before knowing their names (§8.8); and the signature fork, one sign bit in the pair law, whose compact branch closes into circles and pays π and whose indefinite branch saturates into boosts and pays γ — the aperture atom, the run read against itself across acts, being special relativity's $k$-factor priced at one accumulator (§6.6, §8.7). One primitive, carried to its consequences; nothing added along the way but the named further premises, and one edge — the parallel organizer, the memory tower — located rather than crossed (§13).

**What the fork has now paid out, on both branches.** The Success Criterion asked for recovery, and the fork has answered on each of its two settings — which is the sharpest single confirmation the corpus has, because the two answers are *different in kind* and the difference is predicted. The **indefinite** branch never closes: its orbit space is a line, simply connected, with no integer to give — so what it delivers is a continuous invariant, the rapidity, and special relativity's kinematics one received mass away (§13.2, §13.3). The **definite** branch closes: the read folds to $\mathbb{RP}^1$, whose fundamental group is $\mathbb{Z}$, and its generator is one directed passage of the seam — so what it delivers is an *integer*, and that integer is the quantum number, with the half-integer offset a second tally of the same passages (§13.4a). Nothing is received in the second result; it is the one place in the corpus where an established structure of physics is recovered outright rather than assembled. Read together the two say something neither says alone: **quantization is compactness.** That the world presents a continuous invariant along one axis and a discrete one along the other is not two facts about physics but one fact about the pair law — a single sign bit (§8.7), read once in each direction. And the account does not close there, because the argument was never about quantum mechanics: it is about holding pairs, and it runs at every rung where there is a composition to run at. §8.8 says how many such rungs exist — three, by Hurwitz, and no more in any dimension. Run it at the third, where the held object is the quadruple and the read is the reorientation it names — a rotation being *quadratic* in a quaternion exactly as a probability is quadratic in an amplitude — and the sign the read cannot see is **spin-½** (§13.4c), with the corpus's own §13.10 transport supplying the test: at $\gamma = 2$ its Thomas holonomy is exactly one full turn, so the frame returns unchanged and the stance returns as $-1$. The inventory then closes the account in a way only this framework can: three carriers, of which one is discrete, so **exactly two half-integer species are available to any observer** — and physics has exactly two, with the known 2D/3D split between anyons and fermions falling out of the two carriers' fundamental groups. The corpus's oldest slogan, that the read wraps at $\pi$ and not $2\pi$ because a ratio does not carry orientation (§9.5), turns out to have been carrying the zero-point energy the whole time — and its oldest discipline, hold the pair, to have been carrying spin. And the oldest *discipline* — hold the pair, never execute the quotient (§3.7) — turns out to have been carrying something larger still. Executing the quotient is descending a covering map; the pair is the unique double cover of its own read; and the observable is the square that forgets which sheet one is on. So the question of why a quantum state is a complex amplitude and not a probability has, in this framework, the same answer as everything else: **the square root in quantum mechanics is the pair the division would have destroyed** — and the factor of one half that has sat in the harmonic oscillator's ground state since 1925 is the price of one crossing, paid once per horizon.

**The taxonomy, restated with the machinery behind it.** Observation divides by the observer's **relation to the extent** $N$ — whether the whole is available to the act or arrives serially. Where $N$ is finite and available whole, observation can run **continuously**, in the **angle chart**: totals exist, every quantity is a fraction of a completed whole, and π — the total quantity of orientation, now defined in the observer's own primitive (§10) — is the unit of account. The drawn circle is the standard case, and the paper can now say precisely why: a page grants its reader two spare dimensions over every figure on it (§12.9), and two spare dimensions is exactly the room in which a carrier is seen whole. Where $N$ is not available whole — the extent arriving serially, always another sample — observation runs **discretely**, in the **slope chart**: no totals, only reads; ratios against a held run; the Cauchy standing where uniformity would have stood; the crash-proof pair where the completed line would have been. Audio and video are the standard cases, and the paper can now say precisely why: a stream is occupancy, not a completed whole — the serial mode, the path of measure zero, the mode in which the whole is only a limit taken from somewhere else. The two modes exchange at one rate quoted in both directions — **π/2** from the slope chart, the atom's mass, one register's content totaled; **2/π** from the angle chart, the bridge, a completed whole redistributed per unit of the observer's ruler — and every appearance of either constant anywhere in this paper is one of those crossings, the constant the fare.

**The division is a mode, not a wall.** Neither mode is an unbounded observer: whole-sight of every rung at once would erase every silhouette, every horizon, and with them the shared denominator — and an observation without an aperture is not an observation (§12.9). The same observer runs both modes, over different systems: continuously where it stands outside a finite whole, discretely where it is inside a serial stream. Continuous observation was never a second being; it is the same reading run where the extent is complete — and discrete observation, the subject of the title, is the same reading run everywhere else, which is nearly everywhere. The two modes correspond, term by term: the angle chart's totals are the slope chart's limits; continuous accumulation is discrete order (§12.6); the completed count is the whole-sight of the closed line (§12.9); and the exchange between them is not a translation that loses content but a fare paid at a border both sides can see.

**What the closed drawings add to the restatement.** The deepest form of the division is drawn, not stated. Open drawings — the number line, the semicircle with its arms, the sphere with its skeleton — are the angle chart's pictures: they presuppose the continuous observer's vantage, and they show the world with the observer left implicit at the center. Close them through the atom's own weld and the figures reorganize around a single fused point — the address book, home and every horizon at one junction — and that point is the observer, drawn in. At the top of the ladder the open drawing runs out entirely: above $S^3$ there is no vantage, no open picture, and the closed drawing is the only one left (§1.5). That is the taxonomy made final: **continuous observation is a picture of the system; discrete observation is a picture that contains its own reader.** Where the extent is complete, the observer may stand outside and total; where it arrives serially, the observer appears in the figure, at the seam, as the point every excursion leaves from and returns to.

**One sentence, both modes.** The angle chart is what the world looks like from above a finite whole; the slope chart is what the world looks like from inside a serial one; π/2 and 2/π are the price of pretending, for one calculation, to be on the other side; and the geometry of discrete observation is the discovery that the inside view is not the poorer one — it is the one that carries its own observer, prices its own exceptions, needs no external unit, and is available at every rung of every ladder, including the rungs where no other view exists.

**And the pair is the world's.** In neither mode does the observer invent its $v$ and $h$. A physical interaction determines the pair and the observer receives it — observation is only the holding of that pair and the reading of the part against the whole. That is the whole connection between this mathematics and the physics it describes — **the algebra is the observer's, the pair is the world's** — and it inverts the classical starting point, where the mathematician assigns coordinates to the world; here the coordinates are handed up by the interaction and geometry is reconstructed from them. It is why the paper's results are constraints on what any system can *present* to a reader, not theorems about a figure the reader drew. An observer authors its operations and nothing else; its inputs arrive. So it holds pairs and never totals, reads what comes and never what it built, and appears in its own closed picture as the one point it did not have to choose.

**And one motion, both observers — the thesis returned to.** The paper opened with a cycle seen twice, and everything since has been its anatomy. The continuous observer keeps paper and sees a wave: the loop unrolled, periods counted, extension endless. The observer keeps one carry and sees a circle: the loop held closed, compressed toward its seam by the fisheye, walked forever without a count. The wave is the receipt; the circle is the motion; π/2 is the fare between them — and the geometry of discrete observation is, in the end, the recognition that the circle was walked before it was ever drawn, and that physics' three centuries of waveforms are the continuous observer's ledger of the **magnitudes** the walker never evaluated. Not of the laps: the laps the walker does number, because the seam is one-way and a one-way passage counts itself — and the number it keeps, the only integer a bounded reader can carry without borrowing memory, is the quantum number (§13.4a). The walker totals nothing and counts its own turns; the ledger holds the values it never reached.

Whether they are one exchange rate in three uniforms or three distinct constants is the session's standing open question, filed — like the two walls — in the weakest class: watch, don't touch, and re-check the distance whenever any one of them moves. It is the natural next question and it is not yet executed.

**15.12 The shell theorem — per-shell constancy proved on the forced lattice (X; `tb_shell_theorem.md`, `covariance_check.py`; sequel to the A.6 probe).** The residue the A.6 probe left — one covariance bound — is closed, and with it per-shell constancy at proof grade for the observer's own lattice: the cardinal kernel factors exactly as character × envelope; the dyadic shells span exactly $2^{j-1}$ periods of the character (commensurability — counting, not a limit), so its shell mean is the fare $2/\pi$ identically; the envelope's shell integral is $2\ln2 + 2\ln\cos x_j$ in closed form (the depth-stationary edge profile, named); and the covariance obeys $|E_j| \le (2B/N)\csc 2x_j$, $B = \sqrt{1-4/\pi^2} + \tfrac2\pi\arcsin\tfrac2\pi - 1 \approx 0.2105$, by parts off the commensurate zero-mean, with $x_j = 2^{j-1}\pi/N$ the shell's inner edge in the half-angle variable (the convention pinned by the §15.13 adjudication — the full-angle reading makes the outermost bound vacuous) (verified valid at every shell, $N = 64$–$4096$, worst ratio $0.223$; the measured $E_j$ is itself shell-stationary and $\sim 4^{-j}$, one order inside the bound — closed form banked at §15.13). Corollaries: both courts' shell constants derived, stated in one convention (both sides of the evaluation point counted; corrected by the blind adjudication, §15.13) — $\tfrac2\pi\ln2$ at the peak (the character held at its corner), $\tfrac4{\pi^2}\ln2$ on the average ($\tfrac2{\pi^2}\ln2$ per side; the character averaged over its period, the ratio between the courts the character's mean $2/\pi$) — with constancy asymptotic in shell index ($O(2^{-j})$ approach; the innermost and outermost shells carry the $O(1)$, §15.13) — A.6's harmonic floor proved for the forced lattice, and A.2's "$\approx 0.45$" corrected to exactly $\tfrac2\pi\ln2 = 0.4413$ (the $j\to\infty$ per-shell asymptote; measured mid-shell values $0.445$–$0.452$), the shells forcing the $\ln N$ coefficient while the end shells compose the constant. Still open, exactly as before: the universal envelope's quantifier over arbitrary node systems; and the `[P]` identification of this corner-vs-mean split with OI-7(b)'s corner-split awaits the fold-and-character document. The session's pattern held once more: the open problem moved not by addition but by *location* — from "the conjugate function" to "one covariance term" to "one quantifier."

**15.13 The second round's new sections, blind-adjudicated (X; `gbo_adjudication_3.md`; 26 components, 20 confirmed, 4 corrected in place, none refuted in substance).** The claims left unadjudicated by §15.11 — §13.16's three forcings and ring clock, and the §15.12 shell theorem with its probe findings — were run on the same protocol: eleven claims extracted into twenty-six adjudicable components and handed to five independent adjudicators barred from the paper, the notes, and the shipped scripts, each implementing from scratch and instructed to refute. **Twenty confirmed**, several past their stated precision (the Hermitian-seam norm at $2.6\times10^{-14}$; the ring period to $2.4\times10^{-12}$; the commensurable $2/\pi$ shell mean to thirty digits with no limit taken; the covariance bound's constant $B$ recovered in exact closed form and its worst ratio $0.223$ reproduced to three digits; both courts' $\ln N$ coefficients to six digits *including their intercepts*, which match the classical constants $\tfrac2\pi(\gamma+\ln\tfrac8\pi)$ and the Fourier partial-sum $1.2703$). The covariance lemma — the proof's load-bearing step — was **reconstructed independently end to end** by an adjudicator instructed to find the gap: commensurability kills the boundary terms, the factor $2$ is the half-angle Jacobian, and $\csc x - \csc 2x \le \csc 2x$ delivers the double angle; no gap found, and the bound runs $\sim4.5\times$ conservative at the binding shell because $\int G = 0$ exactly. **Four corrected in place**: §13.16's control factors ($\times\tfrac12$, $\times2$) hold only in the refinement limit — the exact finite-spacing factors are $1/(2\cos(k\Delta x/2))$ and $2/\cos(k\Delta x/2)$, and the wrong-runnings' failure is degenerate convergence (to zero) and divergence, not non-convergence; §15.12's average-court shell constant was quoted per-side against the peak's both-sides convention ($\tfrac4{\pi^2}\ln2$ both sides, the two courts' ratio then exactly the character's mean $2/\pi$); per-shell constancy is asymptotic ($O(2^{-j})$), the end shells composing the $O(1)$; and the covariance bound's $x_j$ is pinned as the half-angle inner edge $2^{j-1}\pi/N$. Banked from the refutation attempts, since the attempts again sharpened rather than broke: the shell covariance has a *closed form*, ~~$E_j \to \tfrac{\pi^2-12}{\pi^4}\,4^{-j}$ per side~~ **— corrected round 6 (§15.21): this is where the factor of $\pi$ enters the corpus. The integral §15.20 identifies this with, $\int_{2^{j-1}\pi}^{2^{j}\pi}(|\sin u| - \tfrac2\pi)\tfrac2u\,du$, evaluates to $\tfrac{\pi^2-12}{\pi^3}4^{-j} = -0.0687085\cdot4^{-j}$, verified to six digits. The discrepancy is a factor of $\pi$ exactly, and **no reading of "per side" produces it** — a side convention is a factor of $2$ (the shell's halves measure $-0.0509$ and $-0.0178$ per $4^{-j}$, neither being $\tfrac{\pi^2-12}{\pi^4}$). *Gate discharged (§15.22):* `tb_shell_theorem.md` arrived, and it states this limit *only as the integral* — never in closed form. So the closed form is this entry's own unrecorded evaluation, and the factor of $\pi$ is an arithmetic slip that entered here, not a transcription from outside. The "per side" qualifier is *faithful* to the note ($E_j$ is defined one-sided on $I_j \subset (0,\pi)$, while the note's Corollary 1 says "per shell, two-sided, all atoms" separately); §15.20 dropping it is a second and independent defect. The value is now proved rather than measured: $\tfrac{\pi^2-12}{\pi^3}$ is the $n{=}1$ rung of a complete asymptotic ladder in even $\zeta$ values. What is settled is the integral's value** (five digits; the $4^{-j}$ is two-sided Euler–Maclaurin cancellation, not smoothness); the cot- and csc-envelope kernels satisfy $\mathrm{mean}_{\cot}(N) = \mathrm{mean}_{\csc}(N/2)$ *exactly* — **re-confirmed round 7, and the word *exactly* is now earned rather than measured: the quadrature residual is not an error at all but the excised neighbourhood of the singular endpoint, tracking the cutoff linearly at exactly the predicted $N/\pi$ across twenty orders of magnitude ($1\mathrm{e}{-}20$ through $1\mathrm{e}{-}40$), so the identity holds to whatever precision the regularization is set to. Promoted from a banked curiosity to the load-bearing statement of the parity question: it is what closes F2, since it says the odd-$N$ circle court at $N$ *is* the even-$N$ shell court at $2N$, with no asymptotic step — *and then proved, in the same sitting* (§15.22): substitute $\varphi = 2t$, expand the character, and the whole thing reduces to $\int_0^{\pi/2}(1-\cos 2nt)\cot t\,dt$ at argument $2n$ equalling $\int_0^{\pi/2}(1-\cos 2nt)\csc t\,dt$ at argument $n$, both $= 2H_{\mathrm{odd}}(n)$. Banked round 3, load-bearing round 7, proved one hour later**; Cayley unitarity needs Hermiticity and not merely a real spectrum (the nilpotent one-sided seam, every Cayley eigenvalue $1$, still blows up non-normally); Euler's drift is strictly growth; a finite packet adds $e^{-\Delta x^2/8\sigma^2}$ to the sinc bridge; and the parity-odd seam term is transport-only just as $k\to0$. The direction held a third time: smaller and truer.

**15.14 The universal envelope — prior art found, transport probed (X; `a6_universal_probe.md`, `transport_probe.py`, `transport_probe2.py`).** A.6's last residue — the quantifier over arbitrary node systems — taken through the two steps the agenda ordered. **Prior art first, and the existence half is classical**: the universal max-court floor holds at the sharp $2/\pi$ (Erdős 1961, *Acta Math. Acad. Sci. Hungar.* 12, 235–244 — $|\Lambda_n^* - \tfrac2\pi\log n| \le c$ over all node systems, the same $2/\pi$ the forced lattice pays as fare); the universal pointwise floor off arbitrarily small exceptional sets is Erdős–Vértesi (*Acta Math. Acad. Sci. Hungar.* 36 (1980), 71–89; ISNM 60 (1981), 299–309 — $\lambda_n(X,x) > \eta(\varepsilon)\log n$ off measure $\varepsilon$), and it integrates to a universal $L^1$ floor at a non-sharp constant. These are now *citations at A.6, not proof obligations*. **Not found classically**: the sharp mean-court constant at arbitrary nodes — whether the forced lattice's $4/\pi^2$ (proved §15.12, adjudicated §15.13) is the universal minimum (cite-check pending against Brutman 1997 and the optimal-node literature). **Then the transport probe, executed**: shells by distance rank against six node families ($N = 129$–$1025$; the equispaced control reproduces the theorem — doubling slope $\to 0.4047$, interior shells $\to (4/\pi^2)\ln2$). Every family tested — jittered, iid, van der Corput, clustered, doubled-gap — dominates the lattice *in every shell* (zero violations; the ill-conditioned families astronomically). ~~But *locally* the strict shell-wise transport fails: smooth low-frequency modulations dip single shells $\sim10^{-3}$ below the lattice~~ — **corrected by the round-4 blind adjudication (§15.16): the dips were the F5 quadrature artifact; at converged quadrature shell-wise domination holds locally too (0 dips in 290 comparisons), and indeed per individual rank (0/513)** — while the total mean excess stays positive with clean quadratic scaling (excess$/(a/h)^2 \approx 9.7$, constant over amplitudes — a measured positive second variation at the lattice). So the rearrangement route is unrefuted *shell-wise*, stronger than this entry first recorded — and the open problem relocates once more, from "one quantifier" to **"one quadratic form"**: positivity of the second variation of the mean Lebesgue functional at the forced lattice — which is plausibly the *same calculation* as the Tangent Bridge's own §15.3 open thread (second variation $\Rightarrow c_1 = 2/\pi$), the two courts' versions of one statement. The framework's live remainder on A.6 is exactly two items: that quadratic form, and observer-derivability of the classical floor. `[X for the probe and the citations; the minimizer statement is E-class with a registered cite-check.]`

**15.15 The quadratic form, measured — the mean-court Hessian's full spectrum (X; `second_variation_probe.py`, `second_variation_probe.md`; same-day sequel to §15.14).** The quadratic form §15.14 relocated the problem to is now a symmetry-reduced, fully measured object. Exact by symmetry: rotation-by-one-spacing makes the Hessian of the mean Lebesgue functional at the forced lattice **circulant**, so the Fourier modes $\varepsilon_i = a\sin(m\theta_i + \varphi)$ are its *exact* eigenvectors — **with $a$ in units of the node spacing $h = 2\pi/N$, the convention this entry and §15.16–§15.17 use throughout and none of them states; in radians every $H$ below is larger by $h^{-2} = (N/2\pi)^2$ and $H(1,N)$ does not tend to $8$ (pinned round 6, §15.21)** — — the whole form is one spectrum $H(m)$, $m = 1\ldots(N{-}1)/2$, with $\varphi$-degenerate pairs (verified $10^{-12}$) and $m \leftrightarrow N{-}m$ aliasing. Measured, after a numerical repair that promotes §15.13's F5 from wording note to *method requirement* (uniform-grid quadrature errors align coherently with the perturbation mode at the $10^{-2}$ level — kinks must be integrated node-aligned): **the lattice is an exact critical point** (first variation $\le 3\times10^{-13}$ across all $128$ modes at $N=257$ — machine zero, as mode-negation symmetry predicts); **the spectrum is positive definite, every mode measured** — local minimality of the forced lattice over the entire mode space; **the softest mode is the conformal one**, $m=1$ ($x \to x + a\sin x$, the infinitesimal Möbius deformation), and its eigenvalue is **exactly $8$ in the limit** ($7.998424 \to 7.999957$ at $N = 65\to513$, deficits $\times\tfrac14$ per doubling — $H(1) = 8 - O(N^{-2})$); and the spectral law is $H(m,N) \approx A + 4\ln(2N\sin(\pi m/N))$ — **four per natural log of the effective wavenumber in spacing units** ($B = 3.9912$ full-spectrum fit; doubling differences match to $2\times10^{-3}$ through saturation; transports across $N$ at fixed $m/N$; $A \approx 0.50$, small-$m$ corrections dying by $m\approx4$). The registered cite-check executed: max-court optimal nodes are classical (Bernstein–Erdős conjectures, proved by Kilgore and by de Boor–Pinkus, *J. Approx. Theory* 24 (1978) 273–288, 289–303 — equioscillation, interval); **no literature found on minimizing the mean Lebesgue function**, interval or circle — the minimizer statement stays E-class, candidate-new at low confidence, Brutman 1997 unread (paywalled). Derivation targets, banked in order of tractability: $H(1)=8$ (the conformal mode); $B=4$ (whether $4 = \pi^2\cdot\tfrac4{\pi^2}$ is a fare in disguise is to be *tested, not asserted*); the additive $\approx\tfrac12$. The session's pattern, a fifth time: from "one quadratic form" to "one spectrum, three constants."

**15.16 The spectrum closed, the formula proved at its grade, and one retraction (X; `hessian_formula.py`, `hessian_formula.md`, `gbo_adjudication_4.md`; round-4 blind adjudication, four independent adjudicators, F5 trap undisclosed as a protocol test).** Three movements in one entry. **First, the derivation**: the mean-court Hessian split exactly into a moving-kink term and a smooth term — the kink term in closed form, $H_{\rm kink} = (\pi/N)\sum_{j=1}^{N-1}\csc(\pi j/N) = 2\ln N + 2(\gamma + \ln\tfrac2\pi) + o(1)$, *mode-blind* (the csc envelope pricing the moving kinks identically for every mode), resting on the structural gift that the perturbed cardinal's zeros are exactly the other nodes at every amplitude ($N$ odd essential); the smooth term an explicit bounded-integrand integral. **Adjudicated in all five parts** at $10^{-11}$ by an adjudicator instructed to find the gap (toy and off-lattice-zero tests, factor hunts, extra-zero hunts at strong perturbation — all failed to break it), with one wording sharpening installed: only the $1/u^2$ poles cancel; the surviving $1/u$ pole is tamed by the $|\ell_i|$ factor. **Second, the constants closed** — the adjudicators returned more than they were asked: $H(1,N) = 8 - 4\zeta(2)/N^2 - \zeta(4)/N^4 + o(N^{-4})$ — **round 6 closed the tail exactly: $H(1,N) = 8 - \sum_{k\ge1} 16\zeta(2k)/(4^k N^{2k})$, the cotangent expansion of §15.17's $\tfrac{4\pi}N\cot\tfrac\pi{2N}$, convergent and exact at every finite $N$; the next term is $-\zeta(6)/4N^6$ (§15.21)** — (limit exactly $8$, bounded at $2\times10^{-14}$; the conformal mode's smooth response cancels the kink term's $2\ln N$ divergence exactly, leaving the integer); slope exactly $4$ ($\pm 5\times10^{-6}$; this entry's earlier $3.9987$ was small-$m$ fit bias); and the additive constant *identified*: $A = 4\gamma + 4\ln\tfrac2\pi$, so the law reads $H(m,N) = 4[\gamma + \ln(\tfrac{4N}\pi\sin\tfrac{\pi m}N)] + g(m/N)/\tilde m^2$, $g(0)=\tfrac16$, $g(\tfrac12)=\tfrac19$ — **round 6 closed the function between the two endpoints: $g(u) = \tfrac16 - \tfrac{\sin^2 \pi u}{18}$, $u = m/N$, verified to $\le5\times10^{-8}$ at thirteen values of $u$ (§15.21); and pinned $\tilde m$, which this entry uses undefined — it is the *effective wavenumber* $\tilde m = (N/\pi)\sin(\pi m/N)$, not the mode index, read as which $g(\tfrac12)$ comes out $\pi^2/36$, wrong by $\pi^2/4$** — with the $m{=}1$ anchor offset $8 - 4\ln2\pi - A$ constant in $N$ to $10^{-9}$, so the conformal-eigenvalue expansion and the spectral law are one statement. Whether the law's $4$ is $\pi^2\cdot\tfrac4{\pi^2}$ in uniform: still to be tested, not asserted — but the kink/smooth split prices it $2+2$, half envelope, half response. **Third, the retraction**: §15.14's local shell dips **refuted** — the coordinator's own $10^{-3}$ dips were the F5 kink-alignment artifact (reproduced by the adjudicator with matching magnitude *and* mode-selectivity on commensurate grids), and at converged quadrature shell-wise domination holds locally too, **and per individual rank** ($0/513$) — the transport route is *stronger* than §15.14 recorded, and the rank-wise minimization conjecture is banked. The F5 protocol test passed: two adjudicators rediscovered the trap independently and one used it to kill the contaminated claim; F5's failure profile is now quantified from three directions (fake first variations at $10^{-6}$, $H$ distorted up to $9\%$, sign-indefinite shell artifacts at $10^{-3}$). Also banked: criticality past first order (cubic $\lesssim10^{-11}$); per-shell excesses individually quadratic, mass in the high shells. Still open, exactly: analytic derivation of the smooth term's asymptotics (the second $2$ per $\ln$, the $\zeta$-series at $m=1$); the rank-domination proof; observer-derivability. The adjudication was net-constructive for the first time — it returned more closed forms than it consumed. Smaller, truer, and this once *richer*.

**15.17 The spectrum in exact closed form, and the two courts' boost prices (identity-grade, UNADJUDICATED — round-5 candidate; `hessian_closed_form.py`, `maxcourt_c1.py`, `spectrum_closed_form.md`).** The session's last push, two results. **First**: the lattice sums behind the Hessian's smooth term all close ($A_i = -(N{-}2m)\cos m\theta_i$; $B_i = 2m(N{-}m) - 2m^2\cos2m\theta_i$; $T_1, T_2$ elementary via root-of-unity partial fractions), and with them the entire spectrum collapses to one elementary formula, machine-verified at every mode tested ($10^{-13}$, full spectrum at $N{=}17$, through Nyquist at $65$, $257$): $$H(m,N) = \frac{4\pi}{N}\sum_{j\ \mathrm{odd}}^{2m-1}\cot\frac{j\pi}{2N}$$ — **the mean-court Hessian is an odd-harmonic cotangent ladder.** Corollaries: $H(1,N) = \tfrac{4\pi}N\cot\tfrac\pi{2N}$ *exactly at finite $N$* (round 4's $\zeta$-series is the cotangent expansion — the generating identity found); each mode's increment is a single cotangent; positivity is term-by-term (local minimality reduces to the one identity); the slope-4 law and $A = 4\gamma + 4\ln\tfrac2\pi$ follow from $H_{\rm odd}$ asymptotics; and the join with the Tangent Bridge is no longer analogy — TB §15.3's max-court cone spectrum is $\tfrac4\pi H_{\rm odd}(m{-}1)$, the *raw* odd-harmonic ladder, and the mean-court Hessian is its *cot-regularized* twin. Proof debt, exactly one: derive the identity from the reduced formula (one definite integral with elementary integrand). **Second**: TB §15.3's open item "second variation $\Rightarrow c_1 = 2/\pi$" executed on the circle-court $\Lambda_N$ — and the number is right but the *form* is corrected: the boost's excess is $\tfrac2\pi|x| + O(x^2)$, a **corner, not a curvature** ($\Delta\Lambda/x \to 0.63662$ at $2.5\times10^{-4}$ relative, double limit, cross-checked by the closed-form per-branch first variation, $\max g/N \to 2/\pi$, argmax at the stretched cell). The peak court prices the boost with a kink; the mean court prices it smoothly ($x^2$, the exact cotangent) — **the corner-vs-mean split surfacing in the variational layer itself**. One tension flagged, not resolved: TB's record has the boost asymptotically *null* ($4/\pi N$) for its tangent-court kernel; the circle court pays $\psi_1|x|$; both numerics are solid, so the difference sits in the object or the unit map (half-angle, chord/arc) — needs `firstvar.js`'s conventions, external. ~~Everything in this entry is unadjudicated~~ — **adjudicated same day, round 5 (§15.19): the spectral identity held to 81 digits; all six lattice sums proved with sharp validity boundaries; the corner confirmed at 2/π with the full mode ladder measured — see §15.19 for the two-courts unification this produced.**

**15.19 Round five: the identity at eighty-one digits, the sums proved, the ladder doubled, and a kill condition struck (X; `gbo_adjudication_5.md`; four adjudicators, everything §15.17–§1.27 covered).** Four results, in descending order of permanence. **First, the spectral identity is as exact as measurement can say**: pushed with arbitrary-precision arithmetic to amplitude $10^{-60}$ at 200 digits of working precision, $H(m,N) = \frac{4\pi}N\sum_{\rm odd}^{2m-1}\cot\frac{j\pi}{2N}$ held to **81 digits** with every residual scaling as the test stencil's own truncation; $\varphi$-independence is exact; and the identity extends coherently through the aliasing edge (the $j{=}N$ term vanishes exactly where the mode aliases). A quadrature-free lemma fell out (each cardinal is an integer trig polynomial of degree $(N{-}1)/2$ for *arbitrary* nodes, so the mean-court functional is a finite closed-form sum) — the named candidate stepping stone to the analytic proof. **Second, the lattice sums are now proved, not verified**: machine cyclotomic proofs plus general-$N$ derivations for all six; $A_i$ and $T_1$ valid on *double* the claimed range ($m \le N{-}1$); the $\sin^4$ sum's boundary $2m \le N{-}1$ sharp, with the unified tent law $\frac N2\min(m \bmod N,\, N - m \bmod N)$ and exact out-of-range replacements for $B_i$, $T_2$ ($m \to N{-}m$); the phase family proved ($A_i = -(N{-}2m)\cos(m\theta_i + \varphi)$) — the identities are structural, not sine-specific. **Third, the two courts sing one ladder**: the corner confirmed at $2/\pi$ (quoted intercepts reproduced to $10^{-6}$; evenness amended — exact only at the cosine phase), and the adjudicator measured past the docket: the max court's full linear ladder is $a(m) = \frac2\pi H_{\rm odd}(2m{-}1)$, strictly increasing, five modes, two $N$, errors $\le 10^{-5}$ — **the same odd-harmonic ladder as the mean-court Hessian, ratio exactly $4\pi$ mode by mode**. The corner-vs-mean split is now the *order of variation* of one shared spectrum: the peak pays the ladder linearly, the mean pays it quadratically. The TB record's first-variation law is refuted at every mode *as indexed*, yet matches exactly under mode-doubling-plus-factor-2 ($c_{\rm ext}(2m) = 2a(m)$) — the two-courts tension (F6) is sharpened to a convention question with a measured answer key, still awaiting the TB harness. Banked: the finite-$N$ law $a_N(m) = \frac2\pi[H_{\rm odd}(2m{-}1) - m/N]$ (conjecture, five modes to three digits). **Fourth, the foundations bent at their definitions, as foundations should**: §1.27's theorem needed four pins (ratio *profile* for $n$-magnitude acts — "one scalar" is the pair case; joint domains; generation as factorization — forced, since no polynomial invariants exist; the $\bot$ convention for zero deliveries); the act's proposition is relabeled a *coherence lemma* (its content: P3 makes co-readability an equivalence, so "act" is well-posed — and gauge independence is thereby *maximality*, not metaphysics); and **the two-tier law's kill condition was struck as registered** — the corner generator $g = 1$ is the constant map, light-speed absorption read as foundations — the law surviving only with the regular-generator restriction, boundary absorption as a third declared loss site, lossless defined as injective, and the read's loss restated intra-act (profile truncation, never gauge removal). All repairs installed in place at §1.27. The register's falsifiability discipline earned its keep in the strongest way available: a kill condition registered in the morning was struck by evening, and what survived is truer than what was registered. Five rounds, one day, and the pattern held every time: smaller, truer — and twice now, richer.

**15.20 The shell note received, three flags closed, one record regenerated, and the two-courts tension half-dissolved (X; `f6_kernel_translate_test.py`, `hopping_check_regen.py`).** `tb_shell_theorem.md` arrived, and the reconciliation ran clean in both directions. ~~**F2 closed:**~~ **F2 re-opened round 6, and closed for good round 7 on the note itself (§15.22). The note's two "[verified], route named but not written" strengthenings now have their numbers: the shell-stationary limit the note writes as $\int(|\sin u| - \tfrac2\pi)\tfrac2u\,du$ per shell is round 3's banked closed form ~~$E_j \to \tfrac{\pi^2-12}{\pi^4}4^{-j}$~~ — **corrected round 6: $E_j \to \tfrac{\pi^2-12}{\pi^3}4^{-j} = -0.0687085\cdot4^{-j}$, a factor of $\pi$ larger, and the integral must carry the limits $[2^{j-1}\pi,\ 2^j\pi]$ that this sentence omits (it diverges logarithmically at $u=0$ without them). §15.12's own quoted ratio $|E_j|/\mathrm{bound} = 0.223$ reproduces at $0.2231\to0.2234$ ($N = 64\to4096$) under the corrected value and would read $0.0711$ under the published one, so §15.12 is right and the closed form banked against it is not. Policy adopted with the author: **scripts are saved henceforth** — this flag stood for three rounds only because a record wasn't. **F6 half-dissolved by replication:** the two-functionals hypothesis tested — the fixed-kernel-translate Lebesgue functional (the TB note's own $K_N$, rigid translates at warped nodes) has boost response $O(1/N)$, *asymptotically null for every mode*, while adaptive Lagrange interpolation pays $(2/\pi)|x|$ $N$-independently.
