**15.21 Round six: the tower adjudicated and one of its levels struck, two transcription errors caught, and the gap function closed (X; `gbo_adjudication_6.md`, `connection_tower_v2.md`, `upload_list_round6.md`; five blind adjudicators, ~30 components — 8 confirmed, 12 corrected, 9 refuted, 1 untestable; scripts saved under `adj_C/` and `round6_scripts/`).** The docket §1.27 set — check that `connection_tower.md`'s definitions are standard and its four textual identifications carry no stretch — answered in both directions, and the page came back smaller. **First, the structural findings, each reached independently by more than one adjudicator (the protocol's only strong signal).** *Level 3 of the tower is empty as constructed*: under §13.7's own $\kappa_x = h_x/h_{x-1}$ together with §6.6's $k_t = h_t/h_{t-1}$, the connection is $A = d\ln h$, a discrete differential of a site function — **exact by construction**, so the plaquette holonomy telescopes and $F = dA \equiv 0$ identically, for every aperture profile (verified, $4.4\times10^{-16}$ on random positive $h$). Non-trivial curvature needs $\kappa$ as an *independent link variable* not derived from any site function, which §13.7 does not supply; reached also from the topological side (flat $\not\Rightarrow$ level 1 without $H^1(B;\mathbb R) = 0$ — counterexample $C_4\times\mathbb Z$, flat with non-trivial holonomy) and from the overclaim sweep. Registered as a debt; until discharged the tower has three levels, and §13.9–13.11's loop holonomy belongs to §13.6's Lorentz connection, not to this $\mathbb R^+$ one. *Levels 0 and 1 coincide* as the page defines them — "supply none" and "$\kappa\equiv1$ / $A_t = 0$" used interchangeably for rung 0 while rung 1 is *defined* as $\kappa\equiv1$; and $A_t = 0$ is a gauge choice under which weight-1 sections **are** transportable, negating §1.27(iii) rather than restating it. §6.5's change-atom, offered as level 0's instance, *supplies* a transition scalar and carries a weight-1 datum across an act boundary: it is level 1's minimal case, over one edge. *Gravitational redshift is the $A_x\neq0$ case*, on §13.5's own displayed $z = \Delta\ln\lambda = \int\partial_x\ln\lambda\,dx = \Delta\Phi$ and §13.7's "whose spatial gradient was the redshift potential" — the page's citation of $z$ was materially elided, dropping the very term that decides it; a uniform $A_t\neq0$ shifts every clock alike, cosmological drift, not gravity. *And the closing move is a category error*: Einstein's equations govern the Levi-Civita connection of a metric (Lorentz/$GL$, non-abelian, metric-compatible), not an abelian $\mathbb R^+$ scale connection whose own dynamics are Maxwell-type in $F = dA$ sourced by a dilatation current — Weyl's 1918 programme, and the page silently halved §13.5's two-part admission by carrying the field equations forward and dropping *"a metric of Riemannian (not merely conformal) type"*, which is the half that makes the identification a category error rather than a gap. The **second-clock objection** (Einstein to Weyl, 1918) applies to exactly the case in which level 3 is non-empty and is acknowledged nowhere in the corpus; now registered. The page's meta-claim — *"it proves nothing new: every load-bearing statement is §1.27's theorem, a verbatim manuscript sentence, or a definition"* — was the most-refuted item on the sheet, and its refutation is the reason the rest had to be checked: the claim is one of *safety*, and it bought the page its `[definitional]` grade. The manuscript contains zero occurrences of "principal bundle", "line bundle", "structure group", "global section", "trivialization", "plaquette", "weight-1". Regraded `[constructed]` — a reclassification, not a promotion: the page makes claims of its own, so it is held to a claim's standard, and three of those claims failed. Surviving verbatim and unbroken: §13.7's seams as the space-direction connection with $A_x = \ln\kappa_x$ named "connection" in the text (B1, with $\kappa_x\in[0,\infty]$ against the structure group's $(0,\infty)$ — the bundle lives over the non-degenerate locus), §13.3's affine lift as the section choice (B2, an isomorphism only for $m\neq0$), *adjacent as questions, identical as object* (B5), and §15.18's rediscovery claim against §1.25's actual text (E2). **Second, two transcription errors, both landing on §15.20, both re-derived by the reconciler before recording.** The shell-stationary limit was published a factor of $\pi$ small — $E_j\to\tfrac{\pi^2-12}{\pi^3}4^{-j}$, not $/\pi^4$ — with §15.12's own quoted ratio $0.223$ the decisive witness (it reproduces at $0.2231\to0.2234$ under the correction and would read $0.0711$ under the published value), and the integral stated with no limits though it diverges at $u = 0$. And F2's closure joined two different objects: the note's $\sin(N\varphi/2)/(N\tan(\varphi/2))$ is the **even**-$N$ cardinal kernel, $2\pi$-antiperiodic at odd $N$ and therefore not a trigonometric polynomial — contradicting §15.19's own quadrature-free lemma — while the shell note runs even and the circle court runs odd. **F2 is re-opened as a parity question.** And note how the first of the two was found, because it is the round's cheapest lesson: the adjudicator caught the wrong value at §15.20, but the *verification sweep after installation* found the same value banked one entry earlier, at **§15.13**, carrying a "per side" qualifier §15.20 silently dropped — and no side convention is a factor of $\pi$ (a side is a factor of $2$; the shell's halves measure $-0.0509$ and $-0.0178$ per $4^{-j}$). So this is not a transcription slip between two entries but a value that has been in the corpus since round 3 and was propagated once. Corrected at both sites; which entry introduced the $\pi$ is not decidable from the manuscript and is gated on `tb_shell_theorem.md`. The audit of §15's remaining numerical transcriptions against their sources is on the round-7 docket, and it is now known not to be hypothetical. **Third, the block that could not be broken, and what it returned.** Adjudicator C rebuilt the mean-court Lebesgue functional from §15.14–§15.17's prose alone — barred from every prior script, establishing its own F5-proof convergence discipline before testing anything — and reproduced the cotangent ladder, the $\varphi$-independence, the term-by-term positivity and the lattice's exact criticality at a worst relative deviation of $7.1\times10^{-21}$; verbatim, *"I could not break C2, C3, C4, or the kink half of C5."* Two results came back that were not asked for. §15.16's gap between its two tabulated endpoints is now a function: $$g(u) = \tfrac16 - \tfrac{\sin^2\pi u}{18}, \qquad u = m/N,$$ verified to $\le5\times10^{-8}$ at thirteen values of $u$ and $3\times10^{-23}$ at $u = \tfrac12$, with $g(0) = \tfrac16$ and $g(\tfrac12) = \tfrac19$ falling out as the endpoints — measured, **not yet derived**; the Euler–Maclaurin route on the ladder is round 7's. And §15.14's $\zeta$-series is not a series but a tail in closed form, $H(1,N) = 8 - \sum_{k\ge1}16\zeta(2k)/(4^kN^{2k})$ — the cotangent expansion of §15.17's $\tfrac{4\pi}N\cot\tfrac\pi{2N}$, convergent and exact at every finite $N$, next term $-\zeta(6)/4N^6$, residual scaling $N^{-10}$ past $k=4$. This is precisely the "generating identity" §15.17 recorded as found but never wrote out. Two conventions were also pinned, both silently load-bearing on published numbers: the perturbation amplitude $a$ is in units of the node spacing $h = 2\pi/N$ (in radians $H(1,N)$ is larger by $(N/2\pi)^2$ and does not tend to $8$), and $\tilde m$ is the effective wavenumber $(N/\pi)\sin(\pi m/N)$, not the mode index (as the index, $g(\tfrac12)$ reads $\pi^2/36$, wrong by $\pi^2/4$). Neither convention appears anywhere in §15.14–§15.17; both are now installed at their entries. **What the round cost and what it bought.** A page regraded, a level struck, a closure re-opened, a published constant corrected — against a gap function closed, a $\zeta$-tail summed, two conventions pinned, and an identity that survived being rebuilt from nothing by an adversary who was trying to break it. The missing-document list was *not* regenerated, by instruction: `upload_list_round6.md` tiers it by what each item gates, and the round's own finding is that it needed none of them — blocks A, B, D5–D6 and E are checks against this manuscript's own text and against standard differential geometry. Round-7 docket: supply level 3 or delete it (with the second-clock objection answered, not inherited); restate the level-0/level-1 distinction so the rungs differ; settle F2's parity; **prove** $g(u)$; and audit §15's numerical transcriptions against their sources. Six rounds, and the pattern held again in its sharpest form yet — the round refuted more than any before it, and returned more than it consumed. Smaller, truer, richer.

**15.22 The shell note received in full: F2 closed at the source, the covariance limit proved, and a round-3 banking promoted to load-bearing and then proved (X; `tb_shell_theorem_discharge.md`, `shell_verify.py`, `shell_twin.py`, `mean_identity.py`, `mean_identity_proof.py`; not an adjudication round — a gate discharge, the note being a primary source and the four open questions decidable by derivation rather than by polling).** `tb_shell_theorem.md` arrived — Tier 1, item 1 on `upload_list_round6.md`, the document with the most gated on it — and the reconciliation ran in an unexpected direction: **every one of the note's own claims survived, and the defects round 6 found were all in this manuscript's reports of it.** Lemma 1 is exact at every parity ($1.1\times10^{-41}$); Lemma 2's $2\ln2 + 2\ln\cos x_j$ reproduces at $2.3\times10^{-41}$ and is stated for the **cot** integrand, which settles the ambiguity §15.20 could not; Lemma 3's $B = \sqrt{1-4/\pi^2} + \tfrac2\pi\arcsin\tfrac2\pi - 1$ equals $\max|S|$ exactly at $0.210513662353$, and its covariance bound holds at all thirty-two shells over $N = 64\ldots4096$ with **zero violations and a worst ratio of $0.223426$** — the note's own quoted $0.223$, reproduced from a from-scratch implementation that shared no line with `covariance_check.py`. Two cross-checks the note's own script could not have run: probe #1's three measured edge masses, reported second-hand as $0.1365, 0.1244, 0.0702$, fall out of Lemma 2's closed form as $0.1365293747, 0.1244170615, 0.07023049277$ — every digit, from a document the measurement did not come from; and Corollary 1, tested directly on $\bar\lambda(N)$ with panels at every kernel zero rather than through the shell decomposition, gives increments per doubling converging to $0.28092183$ against $(4/\pi^2)\ln 2 = 0.28092197$. **F2 closes, and its target moves.** Round 6's parity refutation was correct in substance — $K_N(\varphi+2\pi)/K_N(\varphi) = (-1)^N$, so the declared kernel is the even-$N$ cardinal function — but wrong about whose defect it was: the note is an even-$N$ document throughout (nodes $\theta_k = (2k+1)\pi/N$, runs $N = 64\ldots4096$) and *never mentions parity at all*. It claimed nothing false. §15.20 carried its lemma into an odd-$N$ court with a scope its source had not stated. **R2 is regraded from a theorem defect to a citation defect** — the first time in seven rounds that a refutation has survived intact while changing its subject, and the reason the distinction matters is that a wrong theorem must be repaired while a mis-cited one must only be re-scoped. The odd-$N$ twin was derived anyway and is elementary ($L_j^{\csc} = 2\ln2 - 2\ln(1-\tan^2(x_j/2))$: **same interior constant $2\ln2$, edge correction of the opposite sign**, $-0.687$ against $+0.373$ at the outermost shell of $N=257$), and Lemma 3 turns out parity-robust in its own right, since $g(u) = \tfrac2N\csc(u/N)$ is positive and decreasing on the same range and the by-parts proof goes through verbatim, bound $\tfrac{2B}N(\csc x_j - \csc 2x_j)$, thirty-two shells, zero violations. But **the twin is not needed, and the reason is a sentence this manuscript has been carrying unused since round 3**: §15.13's banked $\mathrm{mean}_{\cot}(N) = \mathrm{mean}_{\csc}(N/2)$ is *exact*, re-tested here at $N = 16\ldots1024$ and, in the form the circle court actually needs, $\mathrm{mean}_{\csc}(N) = \mathrm{mean}_{\cot}(2N)$ at $N = 17, 33, 65, 129, 257$ — and the word *exact* is now earned rather than measured, because the residual turns out not to be an error at all: the quadrature pulls its lower endpoint off the singularity by $\varepsilon$ and thereby omits masses $N\varepsilon/\pi$ and $2N\varepsilon/\pi$ from the two sides, so the residual should be exactly $N\varepsilon/\pi$ — and it is, to eight digits, at every $\varepsilon$ from $10^{-20}$ to $10^{-40}$ ($5.4112681$ against $17/\pi = 5.4112681$). Subtract the regularization and nothing remains at any tested $N$. **The odd-$N$ circle court at $N$ is the even-$N$ shell court at $2N$, exactly**; Corollary 1 transfers by a change of argument with no asymptotic step. A banking made from failed refutation attempts, sitting unremarked for four rounds, is what closes the flag — and that put it in the worst position a sentence can occupy, unproved *and* load-bearing, which is why its proof went straight onto the docket. **It came off the docket in the same sitting, and the proof is elementary enough to be embarrassing.** Substitute $\varphi = 2t$: both means become integrals over $[0,\pi/2]$, and the claim is $\int_0^{\pi/2}|\sin 2Mt|\cot t\,dt = \int_0^{\pi/2}|\sin Mt|\csc t\,dt$. Expand the character — and because $\sum_k(4k^2-1)^{-1} = \tfrac12$ its Fourier series can be written $|\sin Mt| = \tfrac4\pi\sum_k(1-\cos 2kMt)/(4k^2-1)$, every numerator $O(t^2)$ at the origin, which is what makes term-by-term integration against a singular weight legal. Everything then reduces to two elementary integrals, $A(n) = \int_0^{\pi/2}(1-\cos2nt)\cot t\,dt$ and $B(n) = \int_0^{\pi/2}(1-\cos2nt)\csc t\,dt$, and it is enough that $A(2n) = B(n)$. Both evaluate by one telescope, $1 - \cos 2nt = 2\sin t\sum_{j\le n}\sin((2j-1)t)$: the csc weight cancels $\sin t$ outright and $\int_0^{\pi/2}\sin((2j-1)t)\,dt = 1/(2j-1)$ **because the cosine of an odd quarter-turn vanishes** — the same corner the note's Corollary 2 stands on, used a fourth time — giving $B(n) = 2H_{\mathrm{odd}}(n)$; the cot weight instead leaves $2\cos t\sum_j\sin((2j-1)t) = 2\sum_{j<n}\sin 2jt + \sin 2nt$, whose integrals are $1/j$ at odd $j$ and $0$ at even, giving $A(n) = 2\sum_{j<n,\,j\text{ odd}}1/j + [n\text{ odd}]/n$. At even argument the correction term is absent and the odd $j$ below $2n$ are exactly $1,3,\ldots,2n-1$, so $A(2n) = 2H_{\mathrm{odd}}(n) = B(n)$. $\square$ Checked in exact rational arithmetic at $n = 1\ldots399$, zero failures. **And note where the parity enters: nowhere** — the proof never assumes $N$ even, only that one side is written at doubled argument, which is why the two courts coincide as an identity between integrals rather than as an asymptotic agreement. Two things fall out. The mean has a closed form in the corpus's own $H_{\mathrm{odd}}$ — the object §15.19's max-court ladder $a(m) = \tfrac2\pi H_{\mathrm{odd}}(2m-1)$ is already built from — namely $\mathrm{mean}_{\csc}(M) = \tfrac{16}{\pi^2}\sum_{k\ge1}H_{\mathrm{odd}}(kM)/(4k^2-1)$, agreeing with quadrature to $1.3\times10^{-13}$; and **the note's Corollary 1 falls out of that series with no shell decomposition, no covariance bound and no asymptotics at all**, since $H_{\mathrm{odd}}(n) = \tfrac12\ln n + (\tfrac\gamma2 + \ln2) + O(1/n)$ gives $\mathrm{mean}_{\csc}(M) = \tfrac4{\pi^2}\ln M + C + O(1/M)$ with $C = \tfrac8{\pi^2}\big(\sum_k \tfrac{\ln k}{4k^2-1} + \tfrac\gamma2 + \ln2\big) = 0.989431273831$ — an $O(1)$ the note left unevaluated *(and, §15.23: a constant Watson evaluated in 1930, so the route here is independent but the result is not new; the $O(1/M)$ is also two orders coarse — the $1/M$ term is absent)*, and one that closes a loop inside this entry, since $C - \tfrac4{\pi^2}\ln2 = 0.7085093027$ against the $0.7085093$ measured above by direct quadrature on an unrelated route. *Recorded against the reconciler:* the independent route here first produced only the asymptotic shadow of that identity — that the odd court's $O(1)$ exceeds the even court's by exactly $(4/\pi^2)\ln2$, measured to $8.6\times10^{-9}$ — and was drafted as a new result before the grep found §15.13 already holding the exact form. Logged as confirmation by a second route, not as an addition; the banked form is strictly stronger. **The note's two "[verified], route named but not written" strengthenings are now written, and one is stronger than the note assumed.** For stationarity, the expansion $\tfrac2N\cot(u/N) = \tfrac2u(1 - \tfrac{(u/N)^2}{3} - \tfrac{(u/N)^4}{45} - \cdots)$ makes the $N^{-2}$ correction $-\tfrac{2}{3N^2}([Su] - \int S\,du)$; the endpoint bracket vanishes by the note's own commensurability, and $\int_0^\pi S\,du = \pi - 0 - \pi = 0$ makes the second vanish too — a **second cancellation the note did not use** — so the $N^{-2}$ term is identically zero and the true law is $E_j - E_j^\infty = \tfrac{(12-\pi^2)\pi\,4^{j-1}}{15\,N^4} + O(4^{2j}/N^6)$, measured-to-predicted $1.0000004$ at $N=4096$. The note's bound is correct but two orders coarser in $N$ than the truth. For the decay, the note's guess — *"presumably by a second integration by parts"* — is right in spirit and the actual route is cleaner: $|\sin u| - \tfrac2\pi = -\tfrac4\pi\sum_k \tfrac{\cos 2ku}{4k^2-1}$ turns each shell integral into $\mathrm{Ci}(4ka) - \mathrm{Ci}(2ka)$, and with $a = 2^{j-1}\pi$ **both arguments are even multiples of $\pi$** — the same commensurability that carries Lemma 3, used a third time — where $\sin$ vanishes, $\cos$ is $1$, and the asymptotic expansion collapses to $\mathrm{Ci}(z) \sim -\sum_n (-1)^{n-1}(2n-1)!\,z^{-2n}$. With $T_n := 4^n/2 - \sum_{m\le n} 4^{n-m}\zeta(2m)$ — itself the closed form of $\sum_k k^{-2n}(4k^2-1)^{-1}$, checked at $n = 1,2,3$ — the whole ladder falls out: $E_j \sim -\tfrac8\pi\sum_{n\ge1}(-1)^{n-1}(2n-1)!\,(1-4^{-n})\,T_n\,\pi^{-2n}4^{-jn}$, with rungs $\tfrac{\pi^2-12}{\pi^3} = -0.0687085270146032$, $\tfrac{720-60\pi^2-\pi^4}{2\pi^5} = +0.0496939354113388$, and $-0.1046341757$; residual at $j=8$ is $1.16\times10^{-11}$ with one rung and $2.72\times10^{-24}$ with four. **So R1's retraction moves from measured to proved**, and its provenance question is decided in the only way that was ever going to settle it: **the note never states the limit in closed form at all** — only the integral, and the words about the second integration by parts — so $(\pi^2-12)/\pi^4$ was never a transcription from outside, but §15.13's own unrecorded evaluation, and its factor of $\pi$ an arithmetic slip that entered the corpus at the moment of banking. The "per side" qualifier, correspondingly, is **faithful**: the note's $E_j$ is one-sided on $I_j \subset (0,\pi)$ while its Corollary 1 says "two-sided, all atoms" separately, so §15.13 read its source correctly and §15.20's dropping of the qualifier is a second, independent defect. D3 moves `UNTESTABLE` → `CONFIRMED`, with correction. Two honest qualifications on the new ladder: it is **asymptotic, not convergent** — $(2n-1)!$ wins eventually — and it is therefore *not* the same kind of object as round 6's $\zeta$-tail for $H(1,N)$, which is convergent and exact at every finite $N$; the corpus now holds two ladders in even $\zeta$ values that must not be conflated, and the resemblance is precisely what invites the conflation. *(That $\pi^2-12$ governs both the $4^{-j}$ coefficient and the $N^{-4}$ correction is not coincidence: both descend from $\zeta(2) = \pi^2/6$ measured against the character's period-mean $2/\pi$.)* **What the note does not pay, it says so:** the universal Faber envelope remains `[open]`, every statement in it a forced-lattice statement, and the quantifier over arbitrary node systems is the one step A.6 always named — nothing here touches it. OI-7(b) stays `[P]`, still gated on the fold-and-character document; F6 stays gated on the cone-spectrum companion. Four new records are named and absent — `covariance_check.py`, `faber_probe.py`, `shell_factor_probe.py`, `tb_a6_probe.md` — all Tier 3, none gating a live question, since every constant and bound they hold has now been re-derived. Round-7 docket, revised: ~~prove the mean identity~~ **discharged above, one hour after it was registered — the only reason it was written down at all is that this entry had just made an unproved sentence load-bearing, and that is a condition worth being uncomfortable about**; evaluate or name $\sum_k \ln k/(4k^2-1) = 0.238906893837\ldots$, the one number in $C$ still given only as a sum (Abel-rearranged it is $\tfrac12\sum_{k\ge2}\ln\tfrac{k}{k-1}/(2k-1)$, which smells like a Wallis-type product; if it has a classical name the mean court's $O(1)$ joins the peak court's $\tfrac2\pi(\gamma+\ln\tfrac8\pi)$ as a named constant rather than a computed one); consolidate the two $\zeta$ ladders with their difference in kind stated; retire the $N^{-2}$ covariance bound wherever the $O(1)$ accounting uses it; and the four items round 6 left — level 3 or its deletion, the level-0/level-1 restatement, the proof of $g(u)$, and §15's transcription audit, now known live. The flag count falls to four. A gate that had been open since §15.20 closed, and it closed by exonerating the document it was waiting on.

**15.23 The mean court's $O(1)$ named — it is Watson's constant, and the round-7 corollary is a rediscovery of 1930 (X; `watson_constant.py`; a docket item discharged, not a round).** Round 7's docket asked whether $S := \sum_k \ln k/(4k^2-1) = 0.238906893837\ldots$ has a classical name, on the hope that the mean court's $O(1)$ would join the peak court's $\tfrac2\pi(\gamma+\ln\tfrac8\pi)$ as a named constant. It does, and the name arrives with an attribution this entry has to take on the chin. **The mean court at odd argument is not *like* the classical Lebesgue constant of Fourier series; it is that constant.** With $M = 2n+1$, $|\sin(M\varphi/2)|/\sin(\varphi/2) = 2|D_n(\varphi)|$ for the Dirichlet kernel $D_n = \sin((n+\tfrac12)\varphi)/(2\sin(\varphi/2))$, so $\mathrm{mean}_{\csc}(2n+1) = \tfrac1\pi\int_{-\pi}^{\pi}|D_n| = L_n$ identically — two quadratures on two different integrands, agreeing to sixteen digits at $n = 1,2,3,5,10,50,200$. Hence $C = \tfrac8{\pi^2}(S + \tfrac\gamma2 + \ln2) = 0.98943127383114695174$ is **Watson's constant** (G. N. Watson, *The constants of Landau and Lebesgue*, Quart. J. Math. Oxford **1** (1930) 310–318), the additive constant in $L_n = \tfrac4{\pi^2}\ln(2n+1) + C + o(1)$; and Watson's own statement of it, $C = \tfrac8{\pi^2}S - \tfrac4{\pi^2}\psi(\tfrac12)$, is this corpus's formula with $\tfrac\gamma2+\ln2$ written as $-\tfrac12\psi(\tfrac12)$ — the same object in the same shape, ninety-six years earlier. **So §15.22's "the note's Corollary 1 falls out of that series with no shell decomposition, no covariance bound and no asymptotics at all, and the $O(1)$ the note left unevaluated is $0.989431273831$" is a rediscovery, and is regraded as one.** What survives is the route, not the result: the derivation via §15.13's identity and the $H_{\mathrm{odd}}$ series is independent and reached the constant from a direction — a forced-lattice shell decomposition — that has nothing to do with Fourier partial sums. Two smaller things sharpen the point. The Abel-rearranged form the docket recorded as a lead, $\tfrac12\sum_{k\ge2}\ln\tfrac{k}{k-1}/(2k-1)$, **is Watson's own alternative form**: expanding $\lambda(2j+2)-1 = \sum_{n\ \mathrm{odd}\ge3}n^{-(2j+2)}$ and swapping gives $\sum_{j\ge0}(\lambda(2j+2)-1)/(2j+1) = \sum_{n\ \mathrm{odd}\ge3}\mathrm{artanh}(1/n)/n$, which is the docket's expression after one index shift — all four representations agreeing to $6\times10^{-92}$. The corpus had independently walked to the exact representation Watson used, and then written *"smells like a Wallis-type product"* beside it. **It is not.** PSLQ at ninety working digits, tolerance $10^{-75}$, coefficients to $10^8$, over every subset of size $\le5$ of $\{1, \ln2, \ln\pi, \gamma, \ln A, \zeta(3)/\pi^2, G/\pi, \ln\Gamma(\tfrac14), \zeta'(2)/\pi^2\}$ returns **no relation involving $S$**, and `mp.identify` returns nothing for $S$, $e^S$, $e^{2S}$, $e^{4S}$, $\pi e^S$ or $\pi^2 S$. The search is not vacuous: with $S$ removed from the vector and every other setting unchanged it recovers $\ln2 + \ln\pi + \gamma - 12\ln A - 6\zeta'(2)/\pi^2 = 0$, the Glaisher–Kinkelin relation, to ninety-one digits. **The docket item therefore resolves as *named, not evaluated*** — which is the honest half-answer, and is also Watson's: he introduced the constant and did not evaluate it either. Two results fall out of the attempt and are kept. First, a **third representation, and a third $\zeta$ ladder**: since $1/(4k^2-1) = \sum_{m\ge0}4^{-(m+1)}k^{-(2m+2)}$ and $\sum_k \ln k\,k^{-s} = -\zeta'(s)$, one line gives $S = -\sum_{m\ge0}\zeta'(2m+2)/4^{m+1}$, whose terms decay like $16^{-m}$ — ninety digits in ninety-one terms, and the cheapest of the four by a wide margin. The corpus now holds **three** ladders in even $\zeta$ values and they are three different kinds of object: round 6's $H(1,N) = 8 - \sum_k 16\zeta(2k)/(4^kN^{2k})$, convergent and exact at every finite $N$; round 7's $E_j$ ladder in $(2n-1)!\,T_n$, asymptotic and divergent; and this one, convergent in $\zeta'$ rather than $\zeta$. The docket's "consolidate the two $\zeta$ ladders" is now a three-way distinction, and the resemblance that invited the original conflation has become more inviting, not less. Second, **a free rung that corrects §15.22 by two orders**. The $O(1/M)$ written there is not merely coarse — the $1/M$ term is *absent*: $\psi(n+\tfrac12) = \ln n + \tfrac1{24n^2} + O(n^{-4})$, the $1/(2n)$ of $\psi$'s expansion cancelling exactly against the $1/(2n)$ of $\ln(n+\tfrac12)$, so $H_{\mathrm{odd}}(n) = \tfrac12\ln n + (\tfrac\gamma2+\ln2) + \tfrac1{48n^2} + O(n^{-4})$, and feeding that through $\mathrm{mean}_{\csc}(M) = \tfrac{16}{\pi^2}\sum_k H_{\mathrm{odd}}(kM)/(4k^2-1)$ gives $\mathrm{mean}_{\csc}(M) = \tfrac4{\pi^2}\ln M + C + a_2/M^2 + O(M^{-4})$ with $a_2 = \tfrac1{3\pi^2}\sum_k \tfrac1{k^2(4k^2-1)} = \tfrac{2-\pi^2/6}{3\pi^2} = 0.011991900206$, the inner sum closing by the partial fraction $1/(k^2(4k^2-1)) = 4/(4k^2-1) - 1/k^2 \Rightarrow 4\cdot\tfrac12 - \zeta(2)$. Measured residual times $M^2$, divided by $a_2$: $0.9994247$ at $M=17$ rising to $0.9999994$ at $M=513$, deviations themselves falling like $M^{-2}$. **This is the third time in two rounds that an error term written at the order a crude estimate allowed has turned out to vanish at that order** — the $N^{-2}$ covariance correction, the $10^{-23}$ that was a quadrature cutoff, and now this — and the pattern is worth naming: *the corpus's error terms are systematically pessimistic because they are inherited from bounds rather than computed from expansions.* One record kept for its own sake: MathWorld's *Lebesgue Constants* entry cites OEIS A086052 for this constant's decimal expansion, and A086052 is *sums of the first $n$ 6-almost primes* ($64, 160, 304, 464,\ldots$). Recorded, not propagated — no A-number is claimed here. **What this costs, and what it does not.** F2's closure is untouched: it rests on §15.13's identity $\mathrm{mean}_{\cot}(N) = \mathrm{mean}_{\csc}(N/2)$, which is proved at §15.22 and is not Watson's. The shell note's Lemmas 1–3 and Corollary 2 are untouched, as is the peak court's $\tfrac2\pi(\gamma+\ln\tfrac8\pi)$ — a forced-lattice *maximum*, a different court from the Fourier *mean*, and the whole point of the two-courts frame is that they do not reduce to each other. What moves is the novelty grade of exactly one corollary, and what the corpus gains is worth more than that corollary: **its central mean-court object now has a ninety-six-year literature attached to it, and none of that literature has been read.** Round-9 docket, revised: ~~name $\sum_k\ln k/(4k^2-1)$~~ **discharged — named (Watson), not evaluated, and PSLQ-negative to ninety digits**; consolidate *three* $\zeta$ ladders, not two, with the difference in kind stated at all three sites; retire the $N^{-2}$ covariance bound and, with it, audit every $O(\cdot)$ in §15 that was inherited from a bound rather than computed from an expansion; and — new, and generated by this entry — **a provenance audit against the literature**, running the corpus's own transcription-audit method outward instead of inward: for every result in §15 stated as the corpus's own, ask whether it is classical. The mean identity itself is first in that queue, unaudited. Level 3, the level-0/level-1 restatement, the $g(u)$ proof and §15's internal transcription audit all carry unchanged.


**15.24 The provenance audit run outward: four rediscoveries, the newest two years old, and what survives is an interpretation rather than a formula (X; `provenance_audit.py`, `ob_check.py`, `chen_choi_check.py`; a docket item discharged, not a round).** Round 8 ended by observing that the corpus's central mean-court object now had a ninety-six-year literature attached to it *and that none of that literature had been read*. Round 9's instruction was to read it — and, more than that, to run the corpus's own transcription-audit method **outward**: for every result in §15 stated as the corpus's own, ask whether it is classical. Watson has now been read. The queue behind him was longer than expected, and **four results the corpus stated as its own are in the literature — three of them stated as the corpus's own this month, and the fourth was this round's own claim.** **(1)** §15.22's $\mathrm{mean}_{\csc}(M) = \tfrac{16}{\pi^2}\sum_k H_{\mathrm{odd}}(kM)/(4k^2-1)$ is, at $M = 2n+1$, verbatim MathWorld *Lebesgue Constants* eq. (15) and CRC eq. (10) — three equations below the one round 8 read for Watson's constant, on the same page. *The attribution is contested and the conflict is recorded rather than resolved:* MathWorld and the CRC credit **Zygmund, *Trigonometric Series* (1959)**; Ortigueira & Bengochea (2024) print the identical formula as their eq. (3) and credit **Szegő, Math. Z. 9 (1921) 163–166**. Neither primary was accessible; both attributions are secondary-source only and they differ by thirty-eight years. **(2)** §15.23's "free rung" $a_2 = (2-\pi^2/6)/(3\pi^2)$, presented as a *correction to* the literature's $O(1/M)$, is **Watson's own $c_1 = (12-\pi^2)/72$**, printed in his 1930 table alongside $c_1\ldots c_7$ to fifteen decimals; the vanishing of the $1/M$ term is his too. **(3) The even court was published in 2024, and the corpus's own audit had already checked the page that lacks it and read the absence as an opening.** Substituting $\varphi = 2t$, $\mathrm{mean}_{\csc}(N) = \tfrac2\pi\int_0^{\pi/2}|\sin Nt|\csc t\,dt$ is *identically* the $I_n$ of **M. D. Ortigueira & G. Bengochea, "On Lebesgue Constants," Axioms 13 (2024) Art. 505**, eq. (8) — a paper whose stated purpose is precisely the even case — and their Theorem 3, eq. (15) carries a Fejér-type tangent closed form at even argument the corpus does not have, $I_n = \tfrac4\pi\sum_{k\le n/2}\tan\!\big(\tfrac{(2k-1)\pi}{2n}\big)/(2k-1)$, with the odd case reducing to Fejér's classical $1/n + \tfrac2\pi\sum_k \tan(k\pi/n)/k$. Checked against this manuscript's own quadrature at $N = 1\ldots65$, **both parities, thirty-five digits** — and the residual is not error but exactly $N\varepsilon/\pi$, the excised singular endpoint, **F5's signature for the third time**, this time certifying an identity instead of hiding one. *(A citation defect found in passing and recorded, not corrected: Fejér's tangent formula is universally cited to Crelle **138** (1910); it was read here directly, open access, at **Fejér, Ann. Sci. ENS (3) 28 (1911) 63–104, Appendix p. 100 ff., eq. (57)**, under the heading "Nouvelle expression pour les constantes de M. Lebesgue," where he presents it as new and cites his own 1910 note only for the asymptotic. Crelle 138 could not be accessed.)* **(4) And the fourth is this round's own claim.** From round 7's $T_r$ and round 8's $\psi(n+\tfrac12)$ rung, one line closes **every** coefficient of Watson's expansion — where Watson wrote only that they "are expressible in finite terms" and tabulated seven: $a_{2r} = \tfrac8{\pi^2}(1-2^{1-2r})B_{2r}T_r/(2r)$, $c_r = \tfrac{\pi^2}4 a_{2r}$, reproducing $c_1\ldots c_7$ to Watson's printed precision. **It is Chen & Choi, RGMIA Res. Rep. Coll. 17 (2014) Art. 9, eq. (3.11)**, restated as Chen & Cheng, ibid. Art. 49, eq. (3.7): $\lambda_j = \tfrac8{\pi^2}\tfrac{B_{2j}}{2j}(2^{2j-1}-1)\big(1+\sum_{k\le j}(-1)^k B_{2k}\pi^{2k}/(2k)!\big)$. The bridge is Euler's $\zeta(2m) = (-1)^{m+1}B_{2m}(2\pi)^{2m}/(2(2m)!)$, under which $2^{1-2r}T_r = 1+\sum_{k\le r}(-1)^kB_{2k}\pi^{2k}/(2k)!$ **identically** — checked at $r = 1\ldots10$ to $2\times10^{-61}$, the two coefficient formulas agreeing over the same range to working precision, and Art. 49's printed $\lambda_3 = (937440-78120\pi^2-1302\pi^4-31\pi^6)/(952560\pi^2)$ recovered to $1.8\times10^{-62}$. **The $T_r$ packaging is a reparametrisation, not new content — and $T_r$ itself has no name**, being partial fractions in $x = k^2$ plus the textbook telescope $\sum_k(4k^2-1)^{-1} = \tfrac12$; round 7 presented it as a find, and it is notation. **The one constant that came through clean is the one the corpus had already labelled classical.** The peak court's $\tfrac2\pi(\gamma+\ln\tfrac8\pi)$ is the Chebyshev-node Lebesgue constant of **Günttner, SIAM J. Numer. Anal. 17 (1980) 512–520**, its full expansion at **Shivakumar & Wong, Math. Comp. 39 (1982) 195–200** — and §15.19 calls it *"the classical constant"* already. That is this round in miniature. **A scope defect in §15.22, found by turning the same instrument inward.** The entry's bolded *"note where the parity enters: nowhere — the proof never assumes $N$ even, only that one side is written at doubled argument"* **is false, because writing one side at doubled argument *is* $N$ even.** Direct probe: $\mathrm{mean}_{\cot}(N) - \mathrm{mean}_{\csc}(N/2) = -0.0953, +0.0455, -0.0397, +0.0273, -0.0249$ at $N = 3,5,7,9,11$. **The identity holds at even $N$ only.** Same failure mode §15.20 was faulted for at R2 — a lemma carried into a court whose scope its derivation had not established — now aimed at the entry that made the fault. **F2 is not reopened**: its closure uses the identity as $\mathrm{mean}_{\csc}(N) = \mathrm{mean}_{\cot}(2N)$, first argument even by construction; the repair is a scope annotation, not a retraction. **And the shorter proof is the one that makes the scope visible.** Round 7's character expansion is replaceable by three lines: $|\sin Mt|$ is symmetric about $\pi/2$ **for every integer $M$**; $\cot\tfrac t2 + \tan\tfrac t2 = 2/\sin t$; fold $[0,\pi]$ onto $[0,\tfrac\pi2]$ and $\mathrm{mean}_{\cot}(2M)$ becomes $\tfrac2\pi\int_0^{\pi/2}|\sin Mu|\csc u\,du = \mathrm{mean}_{\csc}(M)$. Verified to $3\times10^{-61}$ at $M = 1,2,3,4,5,8,17,33$. Step one is where the parity lives. **What survives is not a formula but an interpretation, and it is not in print.** $D^*_M(t) = \tfrac12\sin(Mt)\cot\tfrac t2 = \tfrac12+\cos t+\cdots+\cos((M-1)t)+\tfrac12\cos Mt$ is the cardinal kernel for trigonometric interpolation at **$2M$ equidistant nodes**, so $\mathrm{mean}_{\cot}(2M) = \|D^*_M\|_1 = I_M$: **$\mathrm{mean}_{\cot}$ is the even-node court and $\mathrm{mean}_{\csc}$ the odd-node court**, $\mathrm{mean}_{\csc}(N)$ is the period-mean of the Lebesgue function of $N$-node equidistant trigonometric interpolation, and at $M = 2n+1$ this reads $\|D^*_{2n+1}\|_1 = L_n$. Ortigueira & Bengochea never mention interpolation, equidistant nodes, $\cot(t/2)$, or a kernel of any kind — they work with the bare integral, and the bridge is one line that two independent searches **found stated nowhere**. *A clean negative is not claimed:* the place it would hide is **Ehlich & Zeller, Math. Ann. 164 (1966) 105–112**, paywalled, and Shakirov's Russian series on the Lebesgue constants of the two classical trigonometric interpolation Lagrange polynomials, likewise; both go onto the upload list. Untouched by the audit: the forced-lattice route itself — the shell decomposition, Lemmas 1–3, Corollary 2, the covariance bound, the $4^{-j}$ ladder — statements about a different object. **The pattern, and it is round 8's pattern's sibling.** Round 8 named *the corpus's error terms are systematically pessimistic because they are inherited from bounds rather than computed from expansions*; round 9 names ***the corpus's novelty claims are systematically optimistic because they are made from the inside.*** Three rounds, four rediscoveries, and in two of them the literature sat on a page the corpus had already opened. That is not bad luck but a missing step in the method: **the outward audit costs the same as the inward one and belongs before a result is written down, not after.** *(One correction to round 8's record: its "literature consulted" list names OEIS A243258, which is **not** Watson's constant but $0.5212516264554098\ldots = \tfrac2\pi(2\ln2-\ln\pi+\gamma)$, the optimal-node constant, a sibling of the peak court's differing by $\tfrac2\pi\ln2$. Recorded, not propagated.)* Round-10 docket: import O&B's even-argument tangent form as a credited closed form for $\mathrm{mean}_{\cot}(2M)$; **ask whether $\mathrm{mean}_{\cot}$ at *odd* argument has one, since O&B cover $\mathrm{mean}_{\cot}$ at even argument only and the scope defect above is exactly why that is a separate question rather than a corollary**; write the interpretation up with its negative-search record and its two unread gates attached; then the four carried items — the three $\zeta$ ladders, the $N^{-2}$ retirement and the $O(\cdot)$ sweep, level 3, the level-0/level-1 restatement, $g(u)$, and §15's internal transcription audit. The flag count stays at four; **F5 earned its keep a third time.**

**15.25 Round ten: the odd court gets a finite closed form, the price of $\pi/2$ not being a node is named, and the simplicity question is answered as a division of labour rather than a win (X; `odd_tangent_form.py`, `odd_tangent_reduce.py`, `derivation_cost.py`, `odd_court_verify.py`, `closedform_check.out`, `derivation_cost_ledger.md`; two searches run outward, one mathematical result discharged, one claim demoted before anyone else could demote it).** Round 9 left the odd $\mathrm{mean}_{\cot}$ court with structure and no arithmetic: an $H_{\mathrm{odd}}$ series that gives every asymptotic rung and no cheap value at any finite $N$. Round 10's instruction was to attack that and to audit outward at the same time, and the two turned out to be one search. **First, the mathematics, which is settled.** For $N$ odd write $R = (N-1)/2$ and $J(N) = \int_0^{\pi/2}|\sin Nt|\cot t\,dt$, so that $\mathrm{mean}_{\cot}(N) = \tfrac2\pi J(N)$. Three steps. (i) $\sin(Nt)\cot t = 2\sum_{s=1}^{R}\cos((2s-1)t) + \cos(Nt)$, with antiderivative $F(t) = 2\sum_s \sin((2s-1)t)/(2s-1) + \sin(Nt)/N$. (ii) The sign intervals of $\sin Nt$ are the panels $[m\pi/N,(m+1)\pi/N]$, and **for $N$ odd $\pi/2$ is not a node** — the last panel is a half panel — so telescoping the alternating panel sum leaves a boundary term that has no even-$N$ counterpart: $J = 2\sum_{m=1}^{R}(-1)^{m-1}F(m\pi/N) + (-1)^R F(\pi/2)$. (iii) Swapping the order of summation and closing the $m$-sum with $\sum_{m=1}^{R}(-1)^{m-1}\sin(m\phi) = \tfrac12\tan(\phi/2) - (-1)^R\sin((R+\tfrac12)\phi)/(2\cos(\phi/2))$, where $\phi = (2s-1)\pi/N$ makes $(R+\tfrac12)\phi = (2s-1)\pi/2$ **exactly**, so $\sin((R+\tfrac12)\phi) = (-1)^{s-1}$. The tangent appears there, and so does a secant:
$$J(N) = 2\sum_{s=1}^{R}\frac{\tan\theta_s}{2s-1} + \frac1N - 2(-1)^R\sum_{s=1}^{R}(-1)^{s-1}\frac{\sec\theta_s - 1}{2s-1},\qquad \theta_s = \frac{(2s-1)\pi}{2N}.$$
Confirmed exact against node-aligned quadrature at $N = 1,3,5,\ldots,101$ at forty-five working digits, maximum deviation $1.1\times10^{-45}$; cross-checked against the $H_{\mathrm{odd}}$ series — a route sharing no machinery with the derivation — to $\le 2.1\times10^{-45}$; and the same machinery run at even $N$ as a control recovers Fejér 1911 eq. (57) and Ortigueira–Bengochea eqs. (15)/(23) to $\le 7\times10^{-46}$. **The secant sum is exactly the price of $\pi/2$ not being a node**, and it is not a perturbation: it is $O(1)$, alternating, and its share of the total falls only from $0.171$ at $N=5$ to $0.104$ at $N=129$ without heading to zero. **Then the secant sum turned out to be removable.** Using $\tan t + \sec t = \tan(\tfrac\pi4 + \tfrac t2)$ and $\tan t - \sec t = -\tan(\tfrac\pi4 - \tfrac t2)$, the two sums fuse into one:
$$\boxed{\ \mathrm{mean}_{\cot}(N) = \frac{2}{\pi}\left[\frac1N + 2\sum_{s=1}^{(N-1)/2}\varepsilon_s\,\frac{1 - \tan\!\big(\tfrac{\pi(N - \varepsilon_s(2s-1))}{4N}\big)}{2s-1}\right],\qquad \varepsilon_s = (-1)^{(N-1)/2 + s - 1},\ N\ \text{odd}.\ }$$
Confirmed exact at every tested odd $N$ up to $257$, against both the secant form and quadrature, to $\le 3.2\times10^{-45}$. **This is a tangent form but it is not the Fejér shape, and the difference is the whole content.** Fejér and O&B have a fixed angle $k\pi/(2M)$ and a fixed sign; here the sign $\varepsilon_s$ alternates **and enters the angle**. At $N=13$ the angle numerators $N \mp (2s-1)$ run $12,16,8,20,4,24$ — they **straddle $N$ from both sides**, where Fejér/O&B run the one-sided ladder $2s-1$. The even court has no room for that alternation because $\pi/2$ is a node there; the straddle is the lattice reading $\pi/2$ as an interior point, and it is the structural reason the integral side had no occasion to write this down. Grade: **`[constructed]` + `[verified]`**, novelty deliberately left unstated pending the two gates below. **Second, the simplicity assessment, which was Tom's question and does not resolve in the corpus's favour.** Operationalized on four axes against the same object, comparing the finite tangent form (T) with the $H_{\mathrm{odd}}$ series (S). *Axis 1, cost to a value:* (T) wins by a factor of $10^{30}$ — at $M=33$, sixteen terms exact against a series whose error falls like $\ln K/K$ and needs $K\sim10^{32}$ for thirty digits (predicted $\text{error}\cdot K = 3.439$, measured $3.642$ at $K=10^5$). *Axis 2, cost to the asymptotics:* (S) wins by a hundred and three years — in (S), $M$ occurs in exactly one place, inside $H_{\mathrm{odd}}(kM)$, so one $\psi$-substitution yields the log coefficient, Watson's constant and every rung; in (T), $M$ sits in the summand *and* the term count, and the literature's own timeline is the measurement (form 1911, constant 1930, general rung 2014). *Axis 3, does the advantage deliver where nothing is published:* yes, three ways. **(A) There is no $1/N$ term at either parity, and at odd $N$ that is a cancellation rather than an absence** — the floor's $\ln(1-1/(kN))$ summed against $\sum_{k\ \mathrm{odd}}1/(k(4k^2-1)) = \tfrac12\ln2$ produces $-(4\ln2)/(\pi^2N)$, killing the explicit $+(4\ln2)/(\pi^2N)$ exactly — leaving $\mathrm{mean}_{\cot}(N) = \tfrac4{\pi^2}\ln N + 0.708509302740\ldots + O(N^{-2})$ at both parities, which closes a loop with §15.22's independently quadratured $0.7085093$. **(B) The $1/N^2$ coefficient splits by parity, both halves in closed form, and the two have opposite signs:** even $4a_2 = 4(2-\pi^2/6)/(3\pi^2) = +0.047967600824011835$, odd $\tfrac{16}{\pi^2}[V/12 - U/4] = -0.088652171543569508$ with $V = \sum_k 1/(k^2(4k^2-1)) = 2 - \pi^2/6$ and $U = \sum_{k\ \mathrm{odd}}1/(k^2(4k^2-1)) = \pi/2 - \pi^2/8 = \tfrac\pi8(4-\pi)$. **The even-node court approaches its asymptote from above and the odd-node court from below.** (C) $\mathrm{mean}_{\csc}(N) - \mathrm{mean}_{\cot}(N) = \tfrac4{\pi^2}\ln2 + 0.1006440717495725/N^2$. All three confirmed twice: through the accelerated series, and through a refit from node-aligned quadrature alone — no $H_{\mathrm{odd}}$, no $\psi$, no $\zeta'$ anywhere in it — with Richardson extrapolation over pairs $(N,2N)$ agreeing to $5.7\times10^{-9}$ (odd) and $6.2\times10^{-11}$ (even). **F5 signature five for five, and this time the excised endpoint mass $N\varepsilon/\pi$ was restored explicitly rather than merely observed.** *Axis 4, the confound, stated before anyone else states it:* the discrete route is not machinery-free — it imports a Fourier series for $|\sin Mt|$, $\psi$'s asymptotic expansion, and $\zeta(2m)$ with Bernoulli numbers, all of it continuous analysis. **What the vantage supplies is not independence from the toolkit but the decomposition the toolkit is applied to**, one in which $N$ occurs exactly once; single-occurrence is the whole advantage and it is a property of the form. **And the counter-example has to be recorded: the shortest derivation anywhere in this material is round 9's three-line fold, and it is a continuous-style proof** — a symmetry, a trig identity, a change of variable — against round 7's fifteen-line discrete proof of the same fact. *"Discrete is simpler" is false as a blanket claim, and the corpus's own shortest proof is the witness against it.* The honest verdict is a **division of labour**: values at finite $N$ to the continuous side by $10^{30}$; asymptotic structure to the discrete side by a century; and the *existence of the odd $\mathrm{mean}_{\cot}$ question at all* to the discrete side only. That is the shape a programme recovering continuous mathematics from a discrete vantage should produce — surplus exactly where its representation is efficient, and nowhere else. **Third, the audit, which is mostly negative and contains one live danger.** Searched outward against the literature: the odd-$N$ $\cot$ object **not found** (and a structural argument backs it — $\mathrm{mean}_{\cot}$ at odd $N$ is not any interpolation operator's Lebesgue constant, so the classical authors had no motive to form it; verified directly that the words "cot" and "cotangent" do not occur anywhere in Ortigueira–Bengochea 2024); the tangent-plus-secant form **not found**; $\pi/2 - \pi^2/8$ in this context **not found**; the parity-dependent coefficient **not found** — *but the even half of it is the weak point and is hereby written as a rediscovery risk, not a claim.* **The bare even coefficient $+0.047967600824$ is exactly $4\times$ the classical Fejér/Fourier $1/N^2$ coefficient $\tfrac4{\pi^2}(2-\pi^2/6)/12 = 0.0119919002060$** (measured ratio $4.000000000000000003$), it sits inside a literature containing at least two papers that explicitly advertise infinite asymptotic expansions of this very object family, and neither has been read. **The gates, both blocked:** Feng, *Math. Numer. Sinica* **7**(4) (1985) 420–425 — abstract recovered identically from two sources, *"An infinite asymptotic expansion is given for the Lebesgue constants associated with trigonometric interpolation corresponding to the equidistant nodal points"*, full text unavailable, estimated $75$–$85\%$ that it contains an explicit $1/N^2$ coefficient for some parity and $\sim50\%$ for the even/$\cot$ family; and — **new this round** — **Günttner, *SIAM J. Numer. Anal.* 17 (1980) 512–520**, which derives asymptotic expansions for trigonometric interpolation at equidistant nodes with explicit $\zeta(2v)$-built coefficients, robots-blocked. Shakirov, *Math. Notes* **102** (2017) 111–123, is **partially open** and now looks unlikely to be the source ($\sim75$–$80\%$ against): its object is the Lebesgue *function* approximated by simplest trigonometric and algebraic-trigonometric polynomials, and the author's free 2016 odd-node paper stops at the $O(1)$ constant with no inverse-square term. Ehlich–Zeller is established indirectly (via Smith 2006, Ibrahimoglu 2016) as an evaluation-of-norms and location-of-maximum result, not parity-dependent asymptotics, and drops in priority. **One correction to §15.23, and it is the second time this constant's A-number has had to be fixed.** §15.23 recorded MathWorld's citation of OEIS **A086052** for Watson's constant and correctly identified it as wrong (*sums of the first $n$ 6-almost primes*) while claiming no A-number in its place. The right one exists: **A243277**, which cites Finch §4.2 p. 251. Recorded and now propagated. The other four constants of this round — $0.708509302740$, $+0.047967600824$, $-0.088652171544$, $0.100644071750$ — have **no OEIS entry found**, which is weak evidence and is recorded as weak. **What round 10 costs and what it does not.** Nothing installed before this entry is disturbed. The odd-court closed form is new mathematics by every check available here and is graded as constructed-and-verified with novelty held open; the sign flip in (B) is the cleanest single statement the odd court has produced and would be the headline of any write-up, with the even half carrying an explicit rediscovery flag; the simplicity claim is demoted from "a win" to "a division of labour" **on the corpus's own evidence, and that demotion is the honest outcome of the round.** Round-9's named pattern — *the corpus's novelty claims are systematically optimistic because they are made from the inside* — has now been applied to claims made this round, before publication rather than after, which is the first time that has happened. **Round-11 docket:** import O&B's even-argument tangent form with credit, now doubly motivated since the corpus's only cheap arithmetic at even $N$ is theirs and its only cheap arithmetic at odd $N$ is this round's; read Feng 1985 and Günttner 1980 in full before the even coefficient is asserted anywhere as first-time-published — **top of the upload list, above F6**; write the surviving interpretation up with its negative-search record attached rather than stripped; consolidate the three $\zeta$ ladders with the difference in kind stated at all three sites *(carried)*; retire the $N^{-2}$ covariance bound and audit every $O(\cdot)$ in §15 inherited from a bound rather than computed from an expansion *(carried)*; level 3 or its removal, the level-0/level-1 restatement, the $g(u) = \tfrac16 - \sin^2(\pi u)/18$ proof, and §15's internal transcription audit *(all carried)*.
